Lincoln Educational Services Corp. [LINC]  /  Universal Technical Institute, Inc. [UTI]

Enrollment to Rebound amid Rising Demand for “AI-Proof” Trade Schools

• LINC and UTI both provide post-secondary, career-oriented Vocational and Technical training for Skilled Trades across key Industrial sectors, including  Automotive / Transportation Technology, Building / Electrical /  HVAC, Healthcare, and Information Technology.

• Presenter explains that LINC and UTI offer exposure to the “Massive” Secular Demand for Skilled Trades, one of the very few Career Paths he expects to AVOID “AI Disruption.”  Healthcare roles including Nurse Aides and Radiology Technicians are a key Growth area, offering Students a Return on Investment that compares FAVORABLY with Traditional Universities.

• Presenter attributes the recent Selloff to a “One-Year Screw-Up,” NOT impaired Businesses.  Both companies missed the Spring Recruiting Season as a “Viral” TikTok Trend steered High School Graduates toward Community College and “Weird, Low-Value” Certifications.  UTI also lost several Recruiters, though the company has since rehired many.

• Corporate Partnerships are an emerging Tailwind, as large Industrial and Healthcare Employers seek to partner with Trade Schools to build a “Hiring Funnel” of Skilled Workers.  UTI is “At the Forefront” of this Trend, with LINC set to adopt a similar Model.

• Even after “Haircutting” Street Estimates, both stocks trade at just ~10x FY28 Consensus EPS with NO material Balance Sheet Leverage.  Presenter argues Reported Earnings UNDERSTATE Profitability because of the “J-Curve” on New Schools, with Valuations implying just 6x – 7x EBITDA for “Mature” Schools excluding Growth Spend.  While the Near-term Setup is unfavorable given a “Seasonally Weak” 3Q, he believes simply “Not Blowing Up Again” would be “A Major Win,” and expects the Setup to improve markedly into CY27 as Tax-Loss Selling abates.

The Charles Schwab Corporation [SCHW]

Agentic AI Cash Sweeps Pose “Existential Threat” to NIM-driven Business Model

• SCHW operates as a Savings & Loan Holding company that provides Wealth Management, Securities Brokerage, Banking, Asset Management, Custody, and Financial Advisory services through 2 segments: 1) Investor Services; and 2) Advisor Services.

• Presenter believes SCHW faces significant “Existential Risk” amid Competition from Robinhood Markets [HOOD] and Interactive Brokers Group [IBKR].  The company’s Earnings depend on Net Interest Margin [NIM] from Client Cash Balances, on which SCHW pays ZERO vs. Peers paying as much as 3% – 4%.  Paying Comparable Rates would reduce Earnings by ~50%, and Presenter expects Agentic AI to ACCELERATE “Cash Attrition.”

• Consumer Tools such as Muse [META] will help Clients identify the Cash “Drag” and “Shop” Balances to Brokers offering Incentives.  Furthermore, Competitors are deploying AI Portfolio Optimizers, which SCHW is UNWILLING to match, as “Sweeping” Cash Balances would erode nearly ALL Earnings.  Mgmt. must now choose between meeting Competitors’ Cash Yields and accepting substantially HIGHER Churn, particularly as SCHW lags in popular products like Prediction Markets and Options.  Presenter finds no good option – a HOOD-style Platform Fee with a ~75bps NIM yields just $2 – $4 of EPS, while “Walling Off the Garden” from AI leaves a “Melting Ice Cube.”

• Tokenization represents another significant Threat as Tokenized Money Market Funds and Equities would offer “Near Real-time” Liquidity, removing the primary reason to hold idle Cash at SCHW.  A shift toward Decentralized Finance [DeFi] should INCREASE Competition and REDUCE Inflows, while an average Client Age of ~49 (likely “Much Higher” on an Asset-weighted Basis) leaves the Platform exposed as younger Investors churn.

• Presenter sees the Multiple “Capped” at 8x – 10x, as FY28 Estimates assume an elevated Fed Funds Rate that is unlikely to persist.  He models BELOW-Street FY28 EPS of ~$8.00 (vs. $9.06 Consensus) and applies a 9x Multiple to arrive at a Price Target of $72/share (~27% Downside).  Lastly, he frames the Short as a “Natural Portfolio Hedge,” emphasizing that a Market Decline would “Shrink” Client Balances.

Markel Group Inc. [MKL]

“High-Severity” Line Exits Unlock Structural Combined Ratio Improvement

• MKL is a diverse Holding Company engaging in marketing and underwriting Specialty Insurance products in the US, Bermuda, UK, and Germany.

• Presenter views MKL as a “Rare Self-Help Story” in a “Soft” Insurance Market, as Mgmt. has begun to embrace “Constructive Criticism” from Activist Jana Partners.  After years of “Stepping on Rakes” by underwriting Low-Frequency / High-Severity Risks such as Intellectual Property and Reinsurance, MKL exited several Reinsurance lines at the behest of Jana and the Board and now has “The Right People in the Right Places.”

• Presenter credits Markel Insurance CEO Simon Wilson with a strong Turnaround effort, and believes that, absent “Unforced Errors,” the Core Business’ Pro Forma Combined Ratio should trend toward the “High-80%’s.”  Even in a “Very Soft” Market, he expects Technology Tools to enable “Smarter & Cheaper” Underwriting, with progress ALREADY evident over the past ~12 months.

• Furthermore, Presenter notes that the former Markel Ventures, a “Mini Berkshire Hathaway” of Controlling Stakes in Operating Companies now reported as Industrial and Consumer segments, accounts for 20% – 25% of Operating Income.  These businesses have “Taken it on the Chin” recently given exposure to Construction, Building Products, and Auto / Transport amid elevated Interest Rates, but remain “Generally Quality” businesses to own over the long term.  Presenter also believes a reinvigorated CEO Tom Gayner “Got the Smelling Salts,” building on a proven Track Record.

• Bears may argue MKL is levered to the “Wrong Side” of the AI Trade via an Equity Portfolio consisting of perceived “AI Losers” such as LPL Financial Holding [LPLA].  Nonetheless, the stock has historically bottomed near Book Value, which Presenter expects to exceed $1,600/share by Year-end 2026 vs. the current Stock Price of ~$1,740/share. His 12 – 18-month Price Target is $2,400/share (~39% Upside) based on a ~1.3x Book Value Multiple, vs. just ~13% Downside Risk to $1,500/share.

Lincoln Educational Services Corp. [LINC]  /  Universal Technical Institute, Inc. [UTI]

Enrollment to Rebound amid Rising Demand for “AI-Proof” Trade Schools

• LINC and UTI both provide post-secondary, career-oriented Vocational and Technical training for Skilled Trades across key Industrial sectors, including  Automotive / Transportation Technology, Building / Electrical /  HVAC, Healthcare, and Information Technology.

• Presenter explains that LINC and UTI offer exposure to the “Massive” Secular Demand for Skilled Trades, one of the very few Career Paths he expects to AVOID “AI Disruption.”  Healthcare roles including Nurse Aides and Radiology Technicians are a key Growth area, offering Students a Return on Investment that compares FAVORABLY with Traditional Universities.

• Presenter attributes the recent Selloff to a “One-Year Screw-Up,” NOT impaired Businesses.  Both companies missed the Spring Recruiting Season as a “Viral” TikTok Trend steered High School Graduates toward Community College and “Weird, Low-Value” Certifications.  UTI also lost several Recruiters, though the company has since rehired many.

• Corporate Partnerships are an emerging Tailwind, as large Industrial and Healthcare Employers seek to partner with Trade Schools to build a “Hiring Funnel” of Skilled Workers.  UTI is “At the Forefront” of this Trend, with LINC set to adopt a similar Model.

• Even after “Haircutting” Street Estimates, both stocks trade at just ~10x FY28 Consensus EPS with NO material Balance Sheet Leverage.  Presenter argues Reported Earnings UNDERSTATE Profitability because of the “J-Curve” on New Schools, with Valuations implying just 6x – 7x EBITDA for “Mature” Schools excluding Growth Spend.  While the Near-term Setup is unfavorable given a “Seasonally Weak” 3Q, he believes simply “Not Blowing Up Again” would be “A Major Win,” and expects the Setup to improve markedly into CY27 as Tax-Loss Selling abates.

Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. [ICE]

“Overlooked” Volume Lift from AI-Driven Power Hedging + Lower Contract Minimums

• ICE operates Global Commodity and Financial Marketplaces, as well as Electronic Energy Markets and Soft Commodity Exchanges, through 3 segments: 1) Exchanges (~55% of Revenue); 2) Fixed Income & Data Services (~24%) and 3) Mortgage Technology (~21%).

• Presenter highlights several Growth Opportunities that remain UNDER-appreciated by the Street.  Specifically, ICE operates the world’s LARGEST Marketplace for Energy Derivatives, the “Foundational Infrastructure” for Global Energy Hedging, which should benefit from both INCREASED Energy Volatility tied to the Iran and Ukraine-Russia conflicts and strong Growth in AI Power Infrastructure.  In July 2026, ICE also announced plans to offer US Dollar-denominated, Cash-settled GPU Compute Futures, part of a broader race among major Derivatives Marketplaces to convert AI Data Center Processing Capacity into a standardized, tradable Commodity.

• Furthermore, ICE’s Mortgage Technology business offers “Upside Optionality” IF Interest Rates decline, yet  Presenter argues the Market is assigning “ZERO Credit” to this segment.  He emphasizes that recent Contract changes with LOWER Minimums should also shift the segment toward MORE Transaction-based Revenue.

• Presenter notes the shares trade at a “Discounted Valuation” both Historically and relative to Peers, though he acknowledges this is “Somewhat Justified” given weakness in the Mortgage -related business.  He forecasts FY28 EPS of $10.00 – $11.00 (vs. $9.93 Consensus) and applies a “Reasonable” ~20x Multiple to arrive at a Price Target of $213/share (~38% Upside).

Golar LNG Limited [GLNG]

FLNG EBITDA Set to “QUADRUPLE” + Year-End Strategic Review Catalyst

• GLNG is a Floating Liquefied Natural Gas [FLNG] company that designs, builds, owns, and operates FLNG vessels that convert Natural Gas at Offshore Production Sites into LNG for export.

• Presenter frames GLNG NOT as an Energy company but as a “Shipping Business” with “NO Consumer Demand” exposure, which charges Gas Producers to liquefy and transport their product to Buyers, primarily in Europe and Japan.  He believes Buyers will “Scramble to Diversify” Supply away from Qatar and Russia, with Argentina emerging as the Key Incremental Customer for GLNG’s 4th Vessel as the country exports Natural Gas globally.

• The company’s Fleet is set to DOUBLE from 4 Vessels to 8 over the next 3 – 4 years, with each unit driving a “Step-Change” in Earnings Power.  Each smaller Mark I Vessel generates ~$250M of EBITDA Annually and each larger Mark II generates ~$400M, with Build Costs of ~$1.8B and ~$2.4B, respectively.  Presenter estimates the Recurring EBITDA from each New Vessel adds “At Least” $20/share of Value to the stock.

• He highlights 2 Additional Levers beyond the Fleet Build: 1) IF European Gas Prices remain elevated, GLNG’s Commodity-linked Upside could generate ~$1B of Incremental EBITDA; 2) Mgmt. has retained Goldman Sachs Group [GS] to run a Strategic Review that could yield a Partner who will “Accelerate Growth” or result in an Outright Sale.

• Presenter thinks a Deal for GLNG’s 4th Vessel could be announced in 4Q26, and with the Strategic Review set to conclude by Year-end 2026, he envisions an eventual Takeout for $75/share (~51% Upside).

CoStar Group, Inc. [CSGP]

Homes.com Spending Cuts to Fuel “EBITDA Revision Story” Under New CFO

• CSGP provides Information, Analytics, and Online Marketplace services to the Commercial Real Estate [CRE], Hospitality, and Residential Industries through an integrated subscription-based platform.

• Presenter refers to CSGP as a “Very Hated Stock” with Substantial Upside Potential, arguing the long-held Bear Case is “Priced In, and Then Some” with the shares approaching a 10-year LOW.  Rather than betting on a Fundamental Inflection, he views CSGP as an “EBITDA Story” with a Near-term Catalyst, expecting New CFO Robin Rossman to RAISE EBITDA and Margin Guidance on the next Earnings Call (Est. 10/28/26).

• The anticipated Revisions stem primarily from Homes.com, where Mgmt. has committed to $100M – $150M LESS Incremental Spend each year, and IR Commentary suggests the Cuts could be even MORE aggressive.  Importantly, Margins should recover as the Investment Cycle “Winds Down.”  While the Thesis does NOT rely on CSGP shutting down Homes.com, Presenter believes such a decision would trigger an “Automatic 15% – 20% Pop” in the stock.

• Presenter acknowledges Pricing Pressure from Zillow Group [Z] has slowed Apartments.com Growth from “HSD%’s” to “MSD%’s.”  However, with CoStar Suite growing “HSD%’s,” he models 7% – 8% “Blended” Growth PLUS Margin Expansion.  At ~12x FY28 Consensus EPS, CSGP trades at a steep DISCOUNT to Info Services Peers such as S&P Global [SPGI] at 18x, and Presenter sees ~30% Upside to $37/share as the Valuation Gap narrows.

CBRE Group, Inc. [CBRE]

“Depressed” Multiple Despite Data Center Momentum + CRE Leasing Re-Acceleration

• CBRE operates as a Commercial Real Estate [CRE] services and investment company in the US, UK, and Internationally through 4 segments: 1) Advisory Services (~46% of Operating Profit); 2) Building Operations & Experience (~34%); 3) Project Management (~15%) and 4) Real Estate Investments (~5%).

• Presenter frames CBRE as a “Perceived AI Loser” poised to actually BENEFIT from AI Tailwinds, with further Upside from AI-supported Efficiency, Margin Expansion, and an accelerating CRE Recovery, “Notwithstanding Rates.”

• He explains that the CRE Recovery is now “Well Underway” after 3 “Depressed” years, as the Rate Cycle curtailed Construction Starts.  However, diminished New Supply now meets strengthening Demand driven by a reacceleration in Economic Activity.  Presenter emphasizes CBRE is MORE sensitive to the Economic Trajectory than to Interest Rates, with the most Rate-sensitive Transactions business (i.e., Property Sales & Mortgage Origination) just ~10% of Fee Revenue.  Instead, the bulk of Advisory Services is driven by Global Leasing, which grew ~24% in 2Q26, with Mgmt. guiding to “Teens%” Growth for the balance of the year.

• Furthermore, CBRE has built a substantial Data Center & Critical Infrastructure Services business, now comprising “LDD%” of Fee Revenue and growing ~40%.  Presenter views Mgmt.’s Path to ~$1B of Segment EBITDA by 2030 as “Highly Visible,” vs. FY26 Total Company EBITDA of ~$3.8B, positioning Data Centers as a “Substantial” portion of the business, supported by Secular Tailwinds.

• As the HIGHEST “Flow-through” Advisory businesses grow, Presenter anticipates “Significant” Margin Expansion.  Additionally, the CFO has begun discussing absolute DECLINES in Non-Commission Costs, driven by a combination of Outsourcing and AI Efficiency.  With Consensus modeling NO Operating Leverage in FY27 and “Way Too Little” in FY28, Margins could “Really Surprise” to the Upside.

• Lastly, Presenter notes CBRE trades at a “Discounted” ~15x FY27 P/E Multiple due to the aforementioned AI Disruption / Interest Rate Fears.  Applying a “Mid-Cycle” ~20x Multiple to his FY27 EPS Estimate of $10.00 (vs. $9.09 Consensus), he arrives at a Price Target of $200/share (~49% Upside).

Broadridge Financial Solutions, Inc. [BR]

Tokenization + “24/7 Trading” Threatens Investor Communications “Monopoly”

• BR provides Investor Communications and Technology-driven solutions for the Financial Services Industry in the US and Internationally, operating through 2 segments: 1) Investor Communication Solutions [ICS]; and 2) Global Technology & Operations [GTO].

• Presenter believes Tokenization of Securities will “Structurally Erode” BR’s role in the Post-Trade and Investor Communications Chain.  “24/7 Trading” is expected by year-end, and the New York Stock Exchange has already applied for SEC approval to trade Tokenized Securities.  He likens this transition to the adoption of Electronic Trading decades ago and anticipates the change will unfold “A Lot Faster Than People Think.”

• Smart Contracts would REMOVE the need for BR’s Services by: 1) Eliminating “T+1” Settlement; and 2) Enabling direct Shareholder Communications, giving Issuers a “Straight Route” to Beneficial Owners rather than through Dealer-held Securities.  Presenter sees 2 paths to Tokenization: 1) Third-Party Custody Vehicles resembling Stablecoins; or 2) Issuers Tokenizing their own shares through Exchanges.  He expects Competition between the 2 Models will ACCELERATE adoption, with the latter ultimately winning.

• The Infrastructure Buildout is already underway, with the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation [DTCC] “Aggressively” building Clearing & Settlement for Tokenized Securities, State Street [STT] and The Bank of New York Mellon [BK] developing Record-keeping Models, and Goldman Sachs Group [GS] pursuing various initiatives.

• Bulls point to BR’s In-house Blockchain and Smart Contract solutions, arguing a “Hybrid” Market will still require the company’s services.  However, Presenter counters that Tokenization opens the Market to MULTIPLE Players, jeopardizing BR’s “Monopoly” Position, while even a “Hybrid” Market would result in CONTRACTING Transaction-Based Revenue and FEWER Revenue-Generating products.  As such, Presenter forecasts ~30% Downside to $115/share.

The Brink’s Company [BCO]

NATL Synergies + Shift to Higher-Growth ATM Services “Overlooked” by Market

• BCO provides Cash and Valuables Management, Digital Retail Solutions [DRS], and ATM Managed Services [AMS] in North America, Latin America, Europe, and Internationally.

• Presenter explains that BCO is “Mix-shifting” AWAY from Low-Margin, Capital-Intensive Cash-in-Transit TOWARD Subscription-based Managed Services.  DRS (i.e., Smart Safes with Provisional Credit) and AMS (i.e., End-to-end Outsourced ATM Operations) now represent ~30% of Revenue having grown “MDD%’s” Organically for 14 Consecutive Quarters, and carry “Mid-30%’s” Incremental Margins vs. ~10% for the Base business.  Both carry 5-year Subscription Terms priced on Cash Acceptance rather than Volume, insulating Revenue from DECLINING Cash Usage.

• BCO’s pending ~$6.6B Acquisition of NCR Atleos [NATL], expected to close in Early 1Q27, significantly accelerates this ongoing Mix Shift.  Mgmt. has guided to 35%+ Adjusted EPS Accretion in Year 1, almost entirely from Multiple Arbitrage with “Negligible” Synergies baked in and has indicated Accretion could reach 50%+ with ~$200M of Run-rate Cost Synergies by Year 3.

• Combined, BCO will manage 100K+ ATMs, several times the Scale of even the largest Banks, allowing the company to operate these ATMs with LOWER Cost, SUPERIOR Uptime, and LESS Risk than Banks can achieve on their own.  With less than 10% of the Market currently outsourced, Mgmt. estimates a TAM 2x – 3x the present size.  Additionally, ~$1B of Pro Forma FCF should return Leverage to the 2.0x – 3.0x Target during 2027, freeing ~50% of FCF for Share Repurchases at a “Depressed” Multiple, alongside small, highly-synergistic ATM “Bolt-ons.”

• Finally, Presenter sees “Asymmetric” Risk / Reward, emphasizing the Thesis only requires the Deal to close “On Time” with Cost Synergies met.  Applying an ~11x Multiple to his FY28 Pro Forma EPS Estimate of ~$18.00 (vs. $11.76 Consensus), he arrives at a Price Target of $200/share (~87% Upside), with additional Synergies and Buybacks offering Incremental Upside.

Ares Management Corporation [ARES]

Growth Tailwind from “Dry Powder” Deployment + “Huge” AI Financing Opportunity

• ARES operates as an Alternative Asset Manager through 4 primary Investment segments: 1) The Credit Group; 2) The Real Assets Group; 3) The Private Equity Group; and 4) Other Businesses.

• Presenter describes ARES as “One of the Most Consistent HDD% Top-Line Growers” across the “Alts” space, delivering even in “Difficult Environments,” with 2Q26 Top-line +17%, Fee-Related Earnings [FRE] +20%, and Distributable Earnings [DE] up OVER 30%.  She points to “Pretty Mechanical” ~15% Top-line Growth, driven by $100B+ of “Dry Powder” NOT yet earning Fees, which she expects to be deployed over the next ~2 years.

• Presenter also underscores a “Relatively Favorable” Lending Environment, with Spreads UP 25bps – 50bps y/y, Leverage ~0.5x LOWER, Loan Terms / Covenants “Meaningfully Improved,” and LESS Competition at the High-end as Retail-dependent Funds retrench.  Within US Direct Lending, ~50% of Deployment is derived from the Existing Portfolio, which is growing EBITDA by 8% – 10% and re-levered every 3 – 5 years, creating a “Natural Deployment Opportunity.”  Beyond US Direct Lending, the Asset-Based Finance [ABF], Europe, and Infrastructure businesses remain “Very Strong.”  The Pipeline ended 2Q26 at a “Record” level and has increased another ~20% per a recent Mgmt. Update.  Moreover, “Whisperings” of Middle-Market Private Equity Sponsors returning to the Market represent UPSIDE to her current Top-line Growth Forecast.

• Presenter highlights 2 Additional Tailwinds:

1)       AI Financing – Peers have raised “Tens of Billions” behind this theme, representing a “Huge” Long-term Opportunity across Alts.  ARES is approaching AI Financing conservatively, mirroring the company’s “Slow & Careful” entry into Retail Private Credit.

2)       Retail Redemptions – Headlines are improving, with the latest Ares Strategic Income Fund [ASIF] Net New Redemptions “Far LOWER“ than in 1H26.  Assuming this Trend holds, she expects ARES to work through Capped Redemptions by Year-end 2026 or early 2027.

• Lastly, she notes the Dividend Yield, at ~4.6%, has returned to Pre-COVID levels, and applying a “Mid-20x’s” Multiple to her FY27 DE Estimate, Presenter arrives at a Price Target of $180/share (~48% Upside).

Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc. [ARE]

Biotech Funding Surge to Drive Lab Leasing Inflection

• ARE is a Real Estate Investment Trust [REIT] that owns, operates, and develops Life Science Lab campuses for Pharmaceutical, Biotechnology, Diagnostic & Personal Care Products companies, Research Institutions, and related Government Agencies in the US.

• Presenter refers to ARE as the “One Big Mispricing” among Financials and the “Purest Play” on US Biotech Lab Real Estate.  ARE has underperformed the iShares US Real Estate ETF [IYR] by ~78% over the past 5 years, a gap he reads as the Supply Curve finally nearing a POSITIVE Inflection.

• He explains that Biotech relies heavily on raising Equity Capital and trades as a “Bond Proxy,” so “Near-Zero” Rates in 2020 – 2021 drove “Record” Fundraising that cascaded from Public to Private Markets and ultimately into Lab Development.  The sector became “Massively Overbuilt,” and Presenter quips that in Late 2021 / Early 2022, “You knew it was getting crazy when Local Liquor Stores in MA were being turned into Biotech Labs,” just before the Interest Rate “Reset.”

• However, Demand is now beginning to accelerate, with the SPDR S&P Biotech ETF [XBI] up ~30% YTD and AI-sensitive Biotech names “Well Beyond That.”  Presenter contends AI will facilitate FASTER Drug Discovery & Development with much HIGHER “Hit Rates,” potentially enabling the Industry to produce 2x – 3x as many Drugs per year, an “Early-Phase Boom Demand Pull” NOT yet visible in Industry Fundamentals.  Private Biotech Funding has surged ~175% y/y and historically LEADS Lab Leasing by ~6 quarters with a high R-squared.  Presenter expects a “Material Inflection” in 2027 given the acceleration already experienced in 1H26.

• Lastly, he notes ARE trades at an implied ~9.5% Cap Rate vs. ~7% for Private Life Science Assets and 8% – 9% on the company’s own Non-Core Sales.  Framing the XBI rally as the “Demand Curve” and ARE’s Underperformance as the “Supply Curve,” Presenter believes Lab Pricing is set to RISE, a turn NOT yet reflected in the stock.  He expresses the Idea as Long ARE vs. Short IYR, a way to capture Secular AI Exposure without a large Momentum component, plus upside IF Rates decline.  His 12-month Price Target is $75/share (~50% Upside).

Alkami Technology, Inc. [ALKT]

Stock “Dislocated” after Failed Strategic Review, but “Activist Saga is NOT Over”

• ALKT provides a Cloud-based Digital Banking platform for Financial Institutions, predominantly among Credit Unions and smaller Banks, with a growing Commercial Banking offering.

• ALKT shares fell over 20% on September 23rd after the Board ended a Strategic Review, but Presenter is adamant the “Saga is NOT Over.”  He views the company’s products as “Mission Critical” with LOW Churn and emphasizes that Bank Vendor Management requirements make winning business DIFFICULT for Newer Entrants, creating a Market that “Almost Feels Like An Oligopoly.”  Notably, Activist JANA Partners, a “Noisier” Shareholder, maintains a Top 5 Position.

• Presenter draws parallels to MarketAxess Holdings [MKTX], whose shares languished amid Share Losses to aggressive Competitors, shrinking Margins, and a Low-volatility Macro Backdrop.  Meanwhile, the Board was quietly running a private Auction in the Spring of 2026 that culminated with a Buyout by Intercontinental Exchange [ICE] at a ~33% Premium.

• Presenter believes the ALKT Sale failed on Price rather than Lack of Interest, an outcome he refers to as a “Head Scratcher.”  Mgmt. framed the announcement as a way to “End Renewal Uncertainty” among Customers, implying signings could ACCELERATE, and reaffirmed Full-year Guidance with NO negative read on Fundamentals.  He also highlights that General Atlantic aggressively bought shares in the “Mid-to-High-Teens” during 1Q26 – 2Q26 and received a Board waiver to own up to 19.9% while remaining eligible for a Business Combination.

• With the shares so “Dislocated” (i.e., down ~40% in less than a month), Presenter expects strong Strategic Interest .  He points to Q2 Holdings [QTWO] as the “Most Obvious” Buyer, while ALKT would offer Temenos AG [TEMN.SW] a digestible entry point for its US ambitions.  He regards Fiserv [FISV] a “Natural Fit” but currently too levered and believes Jack Henry & Associates [JKHY] would also make sense.  Presenter envisions a Takeout at ~$23/share (~67% Upside).

Affirm Holdings, Inc. [AFRM]

“Underappreciated” Agentic Winner with Rate Fears “Already in Guidance”

• AFRM is a leading Buy Now, Pay-Later [BNPL] Network, operating a platform for Digital and Mobile-first Commerce in the US, Canada, and Internationally.

• Presenter points to a “Long Growth Runway” for AFRM, as BNPL represents only “MSD%’s” of US E-Commerce Payments, and E-Commerce is just ~17% of Retail Volume.  The product allows Consumers to split a Purchase into Fixed Payments at Checkout with NO Late Fees or Compounding of Interest.  AFRM Underwrites / Funds the Loan, while the Merchant pays a Fee in exchange for HIGHER Conversion and LARGER Basket Sizes.

• Unlike Klarna Group [KLAR] and Afterpay [XYZ], whose “Pay-in-4” Products are Short-term, ZERO-Interest and Small-Ticket, ~85% of AFRM Volume is Interest-bearing Monthly-Installment Loans – the HIGHER-Ticket, LONGER-Duration, HARDER-to-Underwrite end of the Market.  AFRM is growing FASTER than Peers while dominating the most profitable segment, with a decade of proprietary Data providing the “Real Moat.”

• Presenter considers the recent selloff on Interest Rate Fears and the “AI Agents Will Kill BNPL” Narrative “UNFOUNDED.”  Mgmt. already bakes Rate Hikes into Margin Guidance, so any Rate CUTS would provide Upside.  Regarding Agentic AI, Merchants value BNPL for driving Frequency and Basket Size, so Merchant Agents will “Surface Rather Than Hide” AFRM.  Consumer Agents, which understand a User’s Finances BETTER than any Checkout Page, should also recommend BNPL MORE often than a “Distracted Human,” a Tailwind for Share Gains.

• Presenter expects Amazon.com [AMZN], Intuit [INTU], Shopify UK [SHOP], ServiceTitan [TTAN] to add ~$10B of Incremental GMV on top of Same-Store Growth.  She models ~38% GMV Growth in FY27, ~4% RLTC [Revenue Less Transaction Costs] Margin, and CY28 GAAP EPS of ~$4.00 (vs. $3.39 Consensus).  Following the “Rate & Agentic Selloff,” AFRM shares now trade at just ~17.5x her Forward EPS Forecast vs. a historical 20x – 30x range.  Presenter contends a business compounding GMV in the “High-30%’s” will NOT remain at 18x, particularly with CONSERVATIVE Rate Assumptions and Agents working in its favor.  She envisions a “Re-Rating” to the ~25x Historical Midpoint, implying ~40% Upside to $100/share.

ACI Worldwide, Inc. [ACIW]

Biller Sale Creates “Sexy” Payments Infrastructure Takeout Target

• ACIW provides mission-critical Payments Software to the world’s largest Banks, Merchants, and Billers across 2 segments: 1) Payment Software; and 2) Biller.

• Presenter has followed ACIW for several years and describes the franchise as “Core Bank Payments Technology Infrastructure” that remains “Unnoticed and Underappreciated.”  With ~60% of the business tied to Large Global Banks, ACIW is LESS visible in the US, despite serving top Domestic Institutions including Bank of America [BAC], Citigroup [C], and Wells Fargo [WFC].  Also, while NOT as “Flashy” as companies such as Fidelity National Information Services [FIS], ACIW maintains leading Market Share in Money Transfers and helps Tier-1 Banks modernize Payment Technology.

• Presenter dismisses the “Disintermediation” Bear Case, arguing that even as Money Movement migrates toward Blockchain / Bitcoin, “Banks CANNOT Transfer Without ACI” as part of the Solution.  He frames the Core Franchise as “Sticky” Payment Software and a “Rule of 50” Company, pairing 9% – 10% Revenue Growth with 42% – 43% Margins.

• The Catalyst is a Separation of the Biller segment, which Presenter characterizes as a SLOWER-growth, Merchant Acquiring-type business in the US.  Mgmt. first raised the prospect of a Separation a few years ago, but the Idea only resurfaced ~3 months ago, sending ACIW above $60/share before the stock retraced to ~$49/share as news flow faded and Investors appeared to “Give Up.”  Nevertheless, Presenter believes a Biller Sale could materialize “Soon” (i.e., ~1 – 2 months), with Proceeds directed toward Buybacks.

• ACIW currently trades at ~9x EV/EBITDA, a “Convoluted” Blend of a LOWER-Multiple Biller business and a HIGHER-Multiple Payment Software business.  Stripping out Biller leaves a “Pure, Sexy, Digestible” Acquisition Target.  Applying a ~12x EBITDA Multiple to the Pro Forma company, Presenter arrives at a Price Target of $65/share (~31% Upside), with a Bull Case of $80/share (~63% Upside) at ~15x.

ideas.2026-09-23-katz-host-anto-katz-tmt-ideas:
Josh Resnick (Jericho) — Short European Automakers (MBG, BMW, VOW, STLA)

Bottom line: Thematic short. China profits are gone, US exports face tariffs, and Chinese EVs are taking European share. Dividends go away and there is no long-term equity value; Stellantis could go to zero.

Thesis

• China: the automakers used to make money in China, and that profit has evaporated.

• United States: profits are challenged by tariffs and the requirement to build their own US factories.

• Europe: increasingly pressured by Chinese EVs, which are "better cars and half the price." Every country shows the same chart: Chinese market share going up and to the right.

• Local production: Chinese manufacturers are now building factories in Europe, so they will no longer pay import duties. Josh calls it a potential "wrecking ball for this industry."

• Dividends at risk: they all pay large dividends except Stellantis. Volkswagen agreed with its unions to cut 50,000 jobs. When push comes to shove, employees matter more than dividends, so Josh expects all the dividends to go away within a year or two.

Key Data Points

• Volkswagen "imploded" with a big profit warning in the last few weeks.

• Stellantis inventories rose 20% last quarter despite anemic sales, so Josh expects more negative outlook revisions.

Valuation / Target

• No support for any of the stocks and no long-term equity value. Stellantis is probably going to zero "in pretty short order."

Catalysts

• Further profit warnings and outlook cuts, dividend eliminations, and Chinese OEM factory openings in Europe.

Casey Savage (Avala Global) — Long U

Bottom line: Long Unity. AI-driven ad network improvement plus runtime data has taken Vector from worst to second-best network. Casey targets the high $50s: +30% by year-end and +70% in 12 months.

Company / Business Model

• Mobile gaming ad network (Vector) connecting games with advertisers, plus the Unity game engine.

Thesis

• Dislocation: earlier this year the stock was seen as an AI loser with execution questions. Management has since changed the narrative and executed.

• Under-monetized market: mobile gaming ads earn pennies on the dollar vs. Meta.

• AI-led product inflection: Vector has gone from one of the worst-performing networks to the second best, using AI models to bid more effectively in auctions.

• Runtime data: gameplay data from the engine now informs bidding and is starting to work. The runtime integration began at the end of Q2 and was the most important development.

• Avala's edge: a full market-share and impression-level build; Casey believes the market doesn't understand the conversion-rate math.

• Checks: channel checks are decent, and management sounded constructive at recent conferences. Casey thinks the runtime integration may be performing a bit ahead.

• The AI models keep improving, and the data points show continued acceleration.

Key Data Points

• Incrementals ~80%.

• Vector growth accelerating quarter over quarter in the low 20s; further acceleration expected in Q3.

Valuation / Target

• >$1.3B of EBITDA at 20x gives a high-$50s price target.

• Possibly +30% into year-end and +70% a year from now.

Catalysts

• Q3 and Q4 earnings; a multi-year path beyond the next two quarters.

Risks / Pushbacks

• AppLovin, twice Unity's size, is the biggest risk.

• The runtime impact could plateau and never quite work. Avala keeps monitoring gaming checks.

Other Notes

• Joe Flaum (Newbrook) is short APP on the flip side of this thesis.

Noel Culhane (Artisan Partners) — Short TTWO

Bottom line: Short Take-Two into GTA VI. It's a "travel and arrive" setup, and the street's ~$10B of 4-year FCF implies ~200M units the console base can't absorb.

Company / Business Model

• Video game publisher; Grand Theft Auto VI is its big release after 13 years and launches in a couple of months.

Thesis

• Priced in: the stock has more than doubled over the last couple of years in anticipation.

• Travel and arrive: game stocks typically don't do well around big launches — Nintendo six months after a hardware launch, Take-Two with Red Dead Redemption, CD Projekt with Cyberpunk. There is little incremental information once the biggest, and probably only, hit title is out.

• Unit expectations: buy-side unit expectations look high.

• Street FCF: the street models ~$10B of FCF over four years, growing every year, which implies close to 200M GTA units over the cycle. Noel doesn't think there will be 200M consoles to sell into, so long-term estimates look wrong.

Key Data Points

• The stock reacted negatively to the trailer and is down ~$50 over the last two months.

Risks / Pushbacks

• The stock could pop into the retail launch, and 2027 earnings are likely above the street before years after that come in lower.

Emilio Lamar (Third Point) — Short CHTR, TMUS

Bottom line: Short US telcos that don't own the complete home bundle. Agents will cross-sell wireless and home internet at the lowest bundled price.

Thesis

• Owning the home: "it's all about owning the home." Carriers spend customer acquisition cost cross-selling wireless with home internet.

• How Muse behaves: looking at an AT&T bill, Muse typically tries to cross-sell home internet onto a wireless plan at the lowest possible price to clear the sale. Adding to the bundle costs nothing extra.

• 1MW laser demonstration to the DoW at the end of this year; further production contracts.

• Gamified learning app focused on languages, with newer chess, math and music offerings; monetized through paid subscriptions.

Thesis

• Peak user momentum: data over the summer and into the fall showed probably the biggest acceleration in a couple of years, which Casey thinks sets up a big slowdown.

• Core debate: whether Duolingo can monetize users. Avala doesn't believe it can, because daily users aren't translating into higher-value subscribers or earnings.

• Headwinds: Max conversions, renewals and the cost of acquiring users.

• Timing: the growth slowdown hasn't shown up yet but is "on the come."

• Cost pressure: bonus payouts of $10M+ were called out, which hints at second-half margin issues.

• Management is controlling what it can, but monetization is "a tremendous challenge."

Key Data Points

• Q2: DAUs +23%, total bookings +8%, adjusted EBITDA margin down 530bps.

• "User data good, revenue and margin data not so great."

Valuation / Target

• ~$80 stock over 12 months, using 25x 2027 EPS of ~$3.24.

Catalysts

• Q3 results; the growth deceleration becoming visible.

Risks / Pushbacks

• Product improvements could drive sustained, better paid conversion.

• Avala monitors downloads, monthly DAUs by geography, paid conversion and renewal rates.

• YipitData recently flagged reduced confidence in its DAU tracking, so the data may be less reliable.

Aaron Weitman (CastleKnight) — Longs: AKER NO, MOD, SIMO, CLS

Bottom line: Still bullish on AI infrastructure. Aaron calls most of these names potential doubles, with near-term catalysts at Aker (Nscale IPO) and Modine (industrial separation).

Thesis — General

• Still pretty positive on AI.

• Won't join the crowd shorting neoclouds and AI companies — "feels masochistic… too messy and life's too short."

Aker ASA (AKER NO)

• Public-market way to play the upcoming Nscale IPO.

• Depending on where Nscale prices, Aker could move up 20–40% quickly and double longer term.

Modine (MOD)

• Catalyst in the next week or so: the industrial business is finally being separated and the company is being renamed. Aaron wasn't sure whether to see the rename as "lipstick," but it makes the story more interesting.

• Near-leaks of customer wins: Google is known, and Modine may have won Amazon.

• Earnings power could move materially above consensus over the next couple of years.

Silicon Motion (SIMO) and Celestica (CLS)

• Other ways to keep playing the AI theme; could be doubles or more over the next year.

Emilio Lamar (Third Point) — Short CHTR, TMUS

Bottom line: Short US telcos that don't own the complete home bundle. Agents will cross-sell wireless and home internet at the lowest bundled price.

Thesis

• Owning the home: "it's all about owning the home." Carriers spend customer acquisition cost cross-selling wireless with home internet.

• How Muse behaves: looking at an AT&T bill, Muse typically tries to cross-sell home internet onto a wireless plan at the lowest possible price to clear the sale. Adding to the bundle costs nothing extra.

• Charter: Emilio likes pressing the short here and is also short the unsecured bonds.

• T-Mobile: wireless-only, without a comparable home internet bundle to compete on aggregate pricing.

Shane Sandoval (Atreides) — Long CBRS

Bottom line: Long Cerebras. SRAM-based, wafer-scale inference wins on latency. Shane sees >$20 EPS in 2028 and $500–550 over 24–36 months.

Company / Business Model

• AI accelerator company. Atreides has been invested for many years. It recently IPO'd, and the stock has been anemic since day one.

• Different trade-off from Nvidia, custom ASICs and startups: wafer-scale, all-SRAM, built on lagging-edge TSMC nodes to solve AI's memory-bandwidth needs.

Thesis

• Growth vector 1 — OpenAI: the company came public with an OpenAI deal whose first tranche is 750MW.

• Growth vector 2 — AMD and AWS: recently signed; both should go live at the beginning of next year.

• Growth vector 3 — enterprises and all labs: splitting inference into prefill vs. decode, and more specifically attention vs. feed-forward networks, should drive multiplicative demand for Cerebras.

• Latency: over time latency has proven one of the most important aspects of technology. Cerebras has published 750 tokens/sec on leading OpenAI models and should move to single-digit thousands of tokens/sec over the next 6–9 months — a "dramatically different paradigm."

• Pricing: those tokens can be priced at many multiples of today's GPU spot pricing.

• Structural cost advantage: SRAM rather than HBM DRAM, and lagging-edge TSMC nodes, bring massively expanding incremental margins and shorter lead times.

• Customer expansion: Shane expects the customer base to broaden beyond the three massive labs and silicon providers.

Key Data Points

• Line of sight to ~1GW of power exiting 2027 into early 2028, which is only ~40% of wafer supply.

• Monetization of ~$15B per GW.

Valuation / Target

• North of $20 EPS in 2028.

• Stock should be closer to $500–550 over the next 24–36 months.

• Simplest framework is the gigawatt/megawatt math used across cloud.

Catalysts

• AMD and AWS go-lives early next year; the token-speed step-up over 6–9 months; new customer announcements.

Risks / Pushbacks

• The first two quarters as a public company "weren't great."

• Supply constraints on power are bigger than the market credits.

• Market debate over technical efficiency on very large models and MoE structures, and over whether the business can scale many multiples.

Brian Finn (Findell Capital) — Long BULL

Bottom line: Long Webull. It is the AI-native retail broker and the biggest beneficiary of the SEC's PDT-rule repeal. Brian targets ~$13 vs. a stock under $8.

Company / Business Model

• Online retail brokerage for very active traders, competing with Robinhood and Interactive Brokers. Makes money on trades.

Thesis

• AI integration: a data-rich platform well integrated with AI — agents can create trade reports and actually execute trades. Robinhood can't do this, and IBKR's agents are read-only and still being built out.

• Regulatory catalyst: in June the SEC scrapped the 2001 pattern-day-trader rule that barred accounts under $25K from trading on margin.

• Biggest beneficiary: Webull's average account is ~$5K, so it benefits more than any other broker, and it already has.

• Trade count drives revenue: notional stock volume looks a little weak, but trade count is what drives revenue, and it is rising because of the rule change and because people are deploying small AI agents to trade.

Key Data Points

• Management guided to ~20% transaction growth from the rule change. Actual: more than 70%, with Q2 equity notional volume up 73%.

• August is running well ahead of last year and consensus.

• Trades per dollar of notional volume: 8–11 throughout 2025, 15 in August, still rising.

Valuation / Target

• 2027 EPS of $0.51 vs. a lower consensus.

• Comps: HOOD ~49x, IBKR ~34x.

• 25x gives ~$13/share vs. a stock a little under $8: about $2 of downside vs. $5–6 of upside near term. The China risk is already well reflected in the multiple.

Risks / Pushbacks

• China: the founder is a Chinese national with voting control, and some employees are Chinese. Mitigants: a US broker-dealer entity, US-based board and management, KPMG as auditor, and the Chinese brokerage has been deregistered. Staff could move to Singapore or be replaced with higher-cost hires; today Webull arbitrages cheaper Chinese engineering labor. Brian sees headline risk that is more or less contained.

• Macro and rates: the stock traded off on last week's rate hike, and in the 2022 cycle HOOD and IBKR volumes fell sharply. Brian sees today as closer to 2023 (higher for longer, orderly tape) than 2022, when the Fed raised 375bps, but it is a risk to track.

Josh Resnick (Jericho) — Short European Automakers (MBG, BMW, VOW, STLA)

Bottom line: Thematic short. China profits are gone, US exports face tariffs, and Chinese EVs are taking European share. Dividends go away and there is no long-term equity value; Stellantis could go to zero.

Thesis

• China: the automakers used to make money in China, and that profit has evaporated.

• United States: profits are challenged by tariffs and the requirement to build their own US factories.

• Europe: increasingly pressured by Chinese EVs, which are "better cars and half the price." Every country shows the same chart: Chinese market share going up and to the right.

• Local production: Chinese manufacturers are now building factories in Europe, so they will no longer pay import duties. Josh calls it a potential "wrecking ball for this industry."

• Dividends at risk: they all pay large dividends except Stellantis. Volkswagen agreed with its unions to cut 50,000 jobs. When push comes to shove, employees matter more than dividends, so Josh expects all the dividends to go away within a year or two.

Key Data Points

• Volkswagen "imploded" with a big profit warning in the last few weeks.

• Stellantis inventories rose 20% last quarter despite anemic sales, so Josh expects more negative outlook revisions.

Valuation / Target

• No support for any of the stocks and no long-term equity value. Stellantis is probably going to zero "in pretty short order."

Catalysts

• Further profit warnings and outlook cuts, dividend eliminations, and Chinese OEM factory openings in Europe.

Joe Flaum (Newbrook Capital) — Short APP

Bottom line: Short AppLovin. It is a first mover now facing Unity Vector, in a shrinking gaming ad market, at peak margins, with a slow e-commerce push. "The beat machine is broken."

Company / Business Model

• Mobile ad platform serving ads inside video games, now expanding into e-commerce advertising.

Thesis

• First-mover history: an incredible story over the last couple of years, reaching a ~$250B market cap. AppLovin was the first mover in applying AI recommendation-engine technology (as at Meta and Google), was effectively a monopoly, and locked up the supply side with a timely acquisition.

• Competition: Unity Vector now has a competing product, which is the other side of Casey's Unity long; Joe agrees Unity is taking share.

• Shrinking ecosystem: inventory and engagement for in-game ads are actually down, so the industry isn't growing.

• Peak margins: margins can only go down as AppLovin invests to roll out e-commerce.

• E-commerce: historically AppLovin only showed game ads inside games. The new e-commerce business has started slowly and should stay difficult, as experimental ad dollars flow to chatbots like OpenAI and other AI initiatives.

Valuation / Target

• As growth slows, estimates come down. At ~10x EBITDA, the stock can de-rate toward the low-to-mid $200s.

Bottom line: Still bullish on AI infrastructure. Aaron calls most of these names potential doubles, with near-term catalysts at Aker (Nscale IPO) and Modine (industrial separation).

Thesis — General

Eric Bannasch (Cadian Capital) — Long AG1 GY

Bottom line: Long Auto1. The merchant business alone justifies the ~18x P/E; the "Carvana of Europe" retail business comes for free, and total EPS growth is ~40%. The stock is mispriced as an AI loser.

Company / Business Model

• European platform buying used cars — ~90% from consumers selling their own vehicles — and reselling to dealers/merchants (B2B) or consumers (B2C).

• Merchant business: in operation since inception (15+ years). Sells ~900K units a year and is profitable.

• Retail business: entered 7–8 years ago. Sells ~135K units to consumers.

Thesis

• Merchant business growth: growing in the mid-teens, recently a bit higher, likely 12–16% over the next 2–3 years. ~$300M of EBITDA this year, which is more than 100% of company profit.

• Dominant but under-penetrated: Auto1 dominates Europe yet represents only 2–3% of used-car turnover. It is structurally the only player doing this at scale and is very entrenched.

• Supply-side moat: 1,000+ intake sites and a massive consumer brand. It works like a default Kelley Blue Book: ~40–50% of European consumers selling a car download the app to check a price even if they sell elsewhere, which makes it a great top-of-funnel marketing tool.

• Retail optionality: the retail business grows 20–40% and loses only ~$25–30M of EBITDA. It is already the #2 dealer in continental Europe and will become by far the biggest as it scales. Focus markets are Germany, France and Spain, with presence in Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal and Belgium. Eric calls it structurally super sound because the supply side can't be replicated.

• Merchant earnings compound: low-20s earnings growth on mid-to-low-teens top-line growth.

• Combined: total company EPS growth is closer to 40%.

Valuation / Target

• ~18x (actually a bit less) street 2027 earnings — reasonable for the merchant business alone at 20%+ profit growth, which deserves a higher multiple.

• The retail business is implicitly valued at zero to negative.

Catalysts

• Continued compounding in merchant; retail scaling toward profitability; unwinding of the quant-driven short interest.

Risks / Pushbacks

• Market classification as an AI loser. Eric disagrees: the company physically inspects, repairs and moves 4,000-lb cars.

Other Notes

• In Q1, when AI drove the software sell-off, short interest jumped from ~3–4% to 17% in a single quarter.

• European short disclosures show roughly 10–14 quant funds short and only one fundamental long/short fund, so Eric reads the stock's level as a quant-driven read of the business.

Ravee Mehta (Nishkama) — Long 700 HK

Bottom line: Long Tencent at 12x earnings. The street models a slowdown, and Tencent likely launches a Muse-equivalent with WeChat advantages, so Ravee sees limited downside.

Company / Business Model

• Tencent — WeChat super-app ecosystem, gaming and advertising, plus a large portfolio of investments.

Thesis

• Estimates set low: the street models a deceleration even though growth recently re-accelerated.

• Next Muse product: Tencent could have the next Muse-type product and "very likely will"; it's mainly a matter of securing enough compute.

• Could beat Muse: the WeChat app ecosystem and portfolio companies would likely integrate with it right away.

• Downside protection: the market already knows the product is coming, so there isn't much downside to the lows, and the stock has probably bottomed.

Valuation / Target

• 12x earnings. Ravee doesn't know the upside or exactly what the product is, but thinks the risk/reward is good.

Catalysts

• Launch of a Muse-style agent product once compute capacity allows.

Other Notes

• Ravee was surprised no one pitched declared Muse winners like Meta and Twilio; Nishkama owns some of those, and Okta.
