ideas.2026-09-11-myst-miko-tam-myst-bear-s-den:
Zscaler, Inc. [ZS]

“SASE Saturation” + Bundled Rivals Compress Net New ARR / Free Cash Flow

• ZS operates as a Security Software company, offering a Cloud-based platform that provides Web & Mobile Security, Threat Protection, Cloud Application Visibility, and Networking Solutions.

• Presenter explains that the Security Software space has broadly rallied over the past 3 months amid growing Demand to secure Agentic Workflows, justifiably lifting Peers such as CrowdStrike [CRWD], Palo Alto Networks [PANW], and Fortinet [FTNT].  However, he believes ZS has been swept up in the same Rally despite facing MORE “Idiosyncratic” Issues the Market currently “UNDER-appreciates.”

• Presenter asserts the SASE [Secure Access Service Edge] Market is becoming INCREASINGLY Competitive, with New Customers often buying Vertically-integrated “Bundles” from PANW or smaller businesses turning to Cloudflare [NET].  While ZS still “Dominates” the Enterprise tier, his Checks point to a mounting “Substitution Effect” as Enterprises add Cloud-related Security spend elsewhere, a dynamic he ties directly to Net New ARR [NNARR] Growth “Stalling” to the “MSD%’s.”

• Presenter also views ZS’ recent Price Increases as more Defensive than Offensive, a byproduct of Hardware Investment REQUIRED to support rising Customer Usage as all Traffic passes through the company’s Database.  He notes this dynamic has weighed on Margins, citing particularly “Light” Free Cash Flow in F4Q26 (July) relative to prior quarters.

• Finally, Presenter contends ZS is “Masking” underlying weakness through M&A, arguing that “Stripping Out” Acquisitions such as Red Canary exposes materially “Softer” NNARR.  He expects NNARR and Free Cash Flow to continue to disappoint, with Competition limiting the company’s ability to move “Down-market” as SASE grows MORE Commoditized, supporting his Price Target of $102/share (~38% Downside).

Vestas Wind Systems A/S [VWS.DC]

Order “Pull-Forward” Ahead of Tax Credit Expiry Obscures Volume / Margin Reset

• VWS.DC is the world’s largest designer, manufacturer, installer, and service provider of Wind Turbines in the US, Denmark, and Internationally, operating through 2 segments: 1) Power Solutions; and 2) Service.

• VWS shares “Squeezed” higher following strong 2Q26 Earnings, though Presenter attributes much of the strength to “Demand Pull-Forward” from 2 of the company’s largest Markets.  ~70% of 2Q Orders came from the US and Germany, due primarily to: 1) The US PTC [Production Tax Credit] Window closing on July 3rd; and 2) Germany overhauling its Feed-In Tariff structure, which Presenter believes will have materially NEGATIVE implications going forward.

• The 45X Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit currently drives ~20% of EBIT and is set to expire at the end of 2027, creating a substantial Headwind for the Onshore business.  Presenter also highlights a Key Risk facing the Offshore business, emphasizing the company has NEVER built and delivered a Turbine the size of its current Flagship Model at scale before, while Ship-Tracking reveals VWS is booking Revenues AHEAD of Physical Deliveries.  He also expects intensifying Chinese Competition to pressure Pricing outside the US.

• Furthermore, while the Service business is “Booking a Ton of Revenue,” Costs are running “TOO HIGH.”  Revenue on Long-term Service Contracts is recognized PRIOR to Billing, and VWS’ Group Contract Asset stood at €3.3B in 2Q26.  This represents Revenue already booked on Margin Assumptions Presenter contends are “NOT Feasible” given the existing Cost Base.  This can only be resolved via Cost Reductions OR lowering the Estimated Contract Margins, thereby REVERSING Profit already booked.  Presenter explains the Service segment experienced a similar “Reset” in 2024 and flags recent Insider Selling as a sign this could happen again within the next few quarters.

• Lastly, Presenter’s EPS Estimates sit ~25% BELOW the Street for FY27, with the Gap widening further into FY28 as Margins could turn NEGATIVE once Contract Assets “Reset.”  As such, he forecasts ~40% Downside to DKK129/share.

UniFirst Corporation of Massachusetts [UNF]

CTAS Acquisition Faces FTC Hurdles amid “Implausible” Divestitures

• UNF provides Workplace Uniforms and Protective Work Wear Clothing in the US, Europe, and Canada, operating through 3 segments: 1) Uniform & Facility Service Solutions; 2) First Aid & Safety Solutions; and 3) Other.

• Presenter views UNF as a “Highly Asymmetric” Short.  He thinks the pending Acquisition by Cintas [CTAS] will NOT clear Antitrust for several reasons:

1)      “3-to-2” Industry Structure – CTAS, UNF, and Vestis [VSTS] are the ONLY 3 Uniform Rental companies that serve National Accounts (i.e., Large Customers with Multiple Facilities), which prefer a SINGLE Provider with multiple Branches.  The Merger would shrink this Market from 3 Players to 2, a Concentration Level likely to draw FTC Scrutiny.  Since a handful of divested Branches CANNOT be combined into a New National Competitor, Presenter sees a “Real Structural Problem” that a Divestiture remedy does NOT resolve.

2)      High Branch Overlap – Approximately ~75% of CTAS and UNF Branches overlap, so any Divestiture Package that satisfies Regulators would be so LARGE that CTAS would likely “Walk Away” from the Deal.

3)      “Built to Walk” Merger Agreement – The Agreement is structured to give CTAS a “Clean” Exit IF Regulators push back, with Cost limited to the $350M Reverse Termination Fee (i.e., ~6% of the ~$5.5B Deal Value).

• Presenter notes the entire Bull Case for Deal completion is largely “Political,” emphasizing CTAS’ controlling Family are large Republican Donors and the Trump Administration is viewed as “Business-Friendly.”  Regardless, he sees Approval on these grounds as “Insufficient and UNLIKELY,” highlighting that the FTC has already issued a Second Request to “Build A Real Case” by actively collecting Evidence (i.e., Phone / Computer Data, Manager Interviews, etc.) to potentially challenge the Merger.

• At current levels, UNF shares offer a ~12.5% Gross Spread IF the Deal closes.  However, the stock traded at ~$170/share before the Deal Announcement and the ~$350M Reverse Termination Fee is worth ~$20/share, implying a “Break Price” of $190/share (~30% Downside).  Lastly, Presenter recommends owning VSTS as an “Attractive Hedge,” positioned as the primary Beneficiary of any forced Divestitures IF the Deal is approved.

Uber Technologies, Inc. [UBER]

“First-Mover Advantage” Fading as Robotaxis Erode Moat

• UBER operates a Technology platform connecting Consumers with independent providers of Ride Services, Meal & Grocery Delivery, and Freight Transportation across ~70 countries and ~10K cities worldwide.

• Presenter believes Tesla [TSLA], Alphabet’s [GOOGL] Waymo, and potentially even General Motors [GM], are ALL Competitors that represent significant Threats to UBER.  He explains that these companies can “Internalize” most aspects of UBER’s business given their proprietary Autonomous Vehicle [AV] technology, while UBER must rely on Third Party Providers to achieve its AV ambitions.

• Simply put, Presenter views UBER’s First-Mover Advantage as “Largely Irrelevant,” with Ride-Hailing becoming increasingly “Commoditized.”  Critically, he contends Unit Economics will favor the “Owners” of the Technology, ultimately resulting in continued pressure on Profitability and Multiple Contraction for UBER.  Presenter does not offer a specific Price Target but envisions meaningful Downside for the stock as AV-enabled Competitors continue to scale.

TransDigm Group Incorporated [TDG]

Aftermarket Pricing Power Eroding as M&A Targets Dwindle amid DOJ “Blockade”

• TDG designs, produces and supplies Aircraft Components in the US and Internationally, operating through 3 segments: 1) Power & Control; 2) Airframe; and 3) Non-Aviation.

• Presenter argues TDG’s “Decades of Pricing Power” have finally put the company “At Odds” with OEMs, who now view TDG’s Practices as “Predatory.”  Boeing [BA] and Airbus [AIR.FP] are increasingly IN-Sourcing Parts or steering Competitors through the Parts Manufacturer Approval [PMA] process to sell Replacement Parts 25% – 50% BELOW TDG’s Pricing – a Trend already visible in Spark Plugs and Oil Filters, with TDG’s Champion Aerospace Market Share collapsing from ~90% to ~40%.  Additionally, SLOWING Miles Flown (i.e., International Air Transportation Association [IATA] forecasts just 1.1% Growth in 2026) threatens the Duration of TDG’s HIGHEST-margin Aftermarket Revenue should Aircraft Retirements accelerate.

• Presenter also notes TDG’s “Long M&A Runway” has SLOWED alongside deteriorating Deal Quality.  The DOJ blocked TDG’s proposed ~$960M Acquisition of Stellant Systems [Private] in July over “Monopoly Concerns” in F-16 components, and TDG pivoted 2 weeks later to a ~$1.1B purchase of Prince & Izant [Private], a Deal his Checks suggest TDG won as the “Sole Serious Bidder,” yet still paid ~2 Turns ABOVE Expectations, undercutting TDG’s typical Deal Leverage.  He also notes that earlier this year TDG spent $2.2B on 2 PMA Companies, which is  OUTSIDE of its Proprietary Wheelhouse, alongside recent “Misses” on larger Aerospace Deals, including Meggitt [PH], Triumph Group [Private], and Jeppesen ForeFlight [Private].

• Furthermore, Presenter views the “Warrior Right to Repair” Provision within this year’s National Defense Authorization Act [NDAA] as a “Put Option” against TDG since it allows Military Personnel to repair Parts and access Technical Data directly.  This is clearly a Price / Volume Headwind as Aftermarket including Defense represents ~75% of EBITDA and Defense End Markets comprise ~43% of Revenue.

• TDG’s Net Leverage is ~6.3x, with nearly 1/4th of the $33.7B Gross Debt Floating and Unhedged at a 6.2% Weighted-average Cost.  Presenter believes this Capital Structure offers little room for incremental Share Repurchases or Special Dividends against a 5x – 7x Target.  He also emphasizes Cash Conversion has reached a ~15-year LOW as CapEx begins to EXCEED Depreciation.  Lastly, he flags persistent Insider Selling since Chairman Nick Howley’s 2021 Retirement, including ~$500M worth of stock sold over ~3 Years and a new 10b5 Plan from former CEO Kevin Stein.  Notably, Howley has NOT sold his ~$120M Stake in Perimeter Solutions [PRM].

• Presenter forecasts FY27 EPS of ~$44.00 vs. $48.25 Consensus and sees TDG’s FCF Yield to “Mean-revert” from <3% toward Pre-COVID Averages of 5.0% – 5.5%.  Applying a Pre-COVID ~18x Multiple, he arrives at a Price Target of $800/share (~30% Downside).  His Risk Price of $1,430/share (~25% Upside) requires a ~30x Multiple on Consensus CY27 EPS of $47.62.

• PUSHBACK: 1) TDG has weathered similar Concerns before; 2) Structural Aircraft Undersupply persists; 3) PMA Risk has been slow to materialize; 4) Mgmt. still closed ~$3B of M&A in the last 12 months despite Regulatory friction; and 5) 18x Multiple may be “Overly Punitive” against “LDD%” EPS Growth.

Swarmer, Inc. [SWMR]

“Vendor-Subsidized” Field Testing Masquerading as “High-Margin SaaS” Business

• SWMR develops Autonomous Drone Swarm Software and AI solutions in the US.

• The key tenets of the Bear Case include SWMR’s negligible Revenues, a failed Department of Defense [DoD] Catalyst, and a “Massive Wall of Supply” coming amid the stock’s IPO Lockup Expiry on September 14th, 2026.  At current levels, the company’s EV is ~$1.2B despite Revenues of just ~$330K in 2024, ~$300K in 2025, and ~$236K YTD with only ~$7M of Cumulative R&D spend.  Since going public in March 2026, the stock has rallied ~700% from its $5/share IPO price.

• Presenter dismisses the “Combat-Proven” Narrative, noting SWMR’s claims of completing 100K Missions in Ukraine were based on an “Unpaid Beta with Donated Drones” that generated “ZERO” Revenue.  Meanwhile, the company’s sole Paying Customer churned “Right Before the IPO,” and SWMR was OMITTED as a DoD Finalist for its ~$1.1B Drone Dominance Program in July 2026.

• Additionally, Presenter highlights a “Forensic Red Flag” related to SMWR’s ~$3.9M Agreement with Meta Bureau [Private] for ~16K Drones.  The 2Q26 10-Q reveals SWMR paid ~$4.9M back to the same Counterparty (i.e., ~125% “Round-Trip”) and Auditors forced a ~$2.4M “Integration Fee” into Contra-Revenue.  He also refers to the recent ~$224M Acquisition of Ratel Robotics [Private], a Ukraine-based Ground-Vehicle maker, as “Sketchy,” noting SMWR paid ~$8M in Cash + ~1M shares for a “Cost-Plus-10%” Business bolted onto a “Supposed” Software story.

• The Lockup Expiry is the primary Catalyst, during which an estimated ~27M shares come free against a tiny ~2M share Float held at a very LOW Cost Basis.  Presenter believes SMWR’s “Fundamental Value” is “At Best” $2.00 – $3.00/share (~94% Downside at the Mid-point).

• UPDATE: The September 14th Lockup Expiry fueled a ~19% DECLINE in SMWR shares.

NIKE, Inc. [NKE]

EPS “At Risk” amid Athleisure Share Loss, Shifting Trends + China Weakness

• NKE designs, develops, markets, and sells Athletic Footwear, Apparel, Equipment, Accessories, and Services worldwide.

• Presenter acknowledges that Sentiment is already very Negative on NKE, yet he contends the Street UNDER-appreciates the “Magnitude” of potential Downside.  After a “Decade-plus” of Athleisure-driven Share Gains, he sees this Trend reversing, with Consumer Preferences shifting back toward more “Traditional, Formal Apparel,” per Commentary from Footwear Peers such as Steve Madden [SHOO].

• He argues that Social Media / Marketing has “Eviscerated” Barriers-to-Entry across Branded Footwear & Apparel, but most acutely within Athletic, as the Category simultaneously grows MORE saturated with new Entrants such as Vuori [Private] and Alo Yoga [Private].  Presenter emphasizes that Sell-side Firm Bernstein Research launched its OWN Footwear Brand simply to illustrate how LOW Barriers-to-Entry have become.

• However, he feels the MOST pronounced “Red Flag” is the Growth Trajectory in China, NKE’s highest-Margin Region, where Trends have “Consistently” DECELERATED since 2021.  Local Competitors have transitioned from “Second Tier” players operating in the Sub-$80 Price Point to becoming MORE competitive in the “Premium” Tier, underscored by a wave of high-profile NBA Endorsements, with Kyrie Irving, Klay Thompson, and Steph Curry all now backing Local Chinese Brands.

• Presenter forecasts FY27 EPS of $1.40 vs. $1.70 Consensus and expects F1Q27 Results to “Miss by a Country Mile” across ALL major Geographies when NKE reports on October 1st.  Shares still trade at ~22x NTM EPS, a Premium to FASTER-growing Peers such as On Holdings [ONON], despite what Presenter views as a SECULAR, NOT Cyclical, issue.  Applying an ~18x Multiple to his $1.40 Estimate, he arrives at a Price Target of $25/share (~32% Downside).

• Lastly, Presenter flags NKE’s mid-November Capital Markets Day (incoming CFO Dave Denton’s first CMD), which could further validate the Bear Case or spark a brief “Relief Rally,” drawing a pointed comparison to Ron Johnson’s “Infamous” 2012 JCPenney [Private] Analyst Day.

• UPDATE: On September 18th, it was announced that French Soccer “Superstar” Kylian Mbappe, who previously represented NKE, signed with ONON to develop Soccer products and represent the Brand.  ONON also hired former star player Thierry Henry as Director of Football.

NewMarket Corporation [NEU]

“Over-Earning” Petroleum Additives to Normalize as Gross Profit Per Ton Declines

• NEU develops, manufactures, and blends Fuel and Lubricant Additives marketed worldwide to Refiners and others who sell Petroleum products used in Transportation and Industrial Equipment.

• Presenter believes NEU’s core Lubricant Additives business (~90% of Operating Profit) is “OVER-Earning” while a recent Missile Restocking-driven rally “Overstates” the Benefit to the company’s much smaller Ammonium Perchlorate [AP] business.  Despite an ~$8B Market Cap and ~$100M Average Daily Volume, NEU has ZERO Sell-Side Coverage and only hosts ONE Earnings Call annually, which leads the Presenter to believe many Shareholders “Do NOT Really Know” what they own.

• Presenter highlights 3 sources of EXCESS Additives Profitability:

1)      Contract Rebids – NEU won business while Berkshire Hathaway’s [BRK.A] Lubrizol was Capacity-constrained by Operational Issues, but these Contracts are now being rebid at INFERIOR Economics.

2)      Temporary Price-Cost – NEU’s Additive Pricing has historically LAGGED increases in Raw Materials.  However, with the Iran War fueling a spike in Base Oil, NEU “Aggressively” raised Prices “Sooner and Higher” vs. Competitors, creating a “Temporary” Tailwind.

3)      Chinese Competition – Richful [300910.CH] has been gaining Market Share, pressuring a formerly “Cozy” Competitive Environment.

• As a result, Presenter anticipates a near-term Price-Cost “Normalization” and gradual decline in Gross Profit per Ton, implying ~20% DOWNSIDE to Per-Ton Profitability amid “Zero-to-Negative” Volume Growth.

• Furthermore, NEU’s AMPAC Subsidiary is the largest provider of AP, a key component of Solid Rocket Fuel.  The stock rallied recently on inclusion in a “Basket” of US Missile-Restocking beneficiaries, though Presenter emphasizes AMPAC comprises just ~6% of Total Operating Profit.  Despite Headlines suggesting the US will “Quadruple” Rocket Production, he maintains this will only drive a “LSD%” increase in NEU’s AP Volumes.

• Presenter’s Price Target of $550/share (~38% Downside) is based on likelihood of a “Weak” 3Q26 Earnings Print followed by a “Slow Burn Down” as Additives Profitability continues to “Normalize.”

Alphabet Inc. [GOOGL]

Agentic Commerce and AI Search Transition to Undermine Core Ad Economics

• GOOGL provides Web-based Search, Advertisements, Maps, Software Applications, Mobile Operating Systems, Consumer Content, Enterprise Solutions, Commerce, and Hardware products through 3 segments: 1) Google Services; 2) Google Cloud; and 3) Other Bets.

• Presenter expects GOOGL to “Miss” 3Q26 Search Revenue expectations, informed by “Consistently Weak” Checks and Data Tracking.  He attributes part of the softness to a struggling Consumer and difficult Comps against very strong prior-year Search results that the Street has NOT fully modeled.  Furthermore, he maintains the “Positive Narrative” embedded in the stock, largely centered on Cloud, has overshadowed the Risks he sees building.

• Presenter highlights Agentic Commerce as the most “Underappreciated” Risk, pointing to products such as Muse [META] and Instinct [Private] as “Direct Threats” to GOOGL’s Core Business Model (i.e., Search-based Comparison Shopping), concentrated in the company’s 2 largest Verticals, Retail and Travel.  Even though the Market has focused primarily on the “OTA [Online Travel Agencies] Angle,” he argues the same Disruption impacting OTAs should logically extend to Retail-adjacent Spending.

• Presenter also flags ChatGPT [Private] Advertising as an overlooked Risk.  While ChatGPT will likely garner early Market Share from “Lower-quality” Advertisers, he contends the Platform represents the FIRST “Scaled Alternative” to Search, a Channel that has historically delivered higher ROIs to Advertisers alongside rising Costs.  Though ChatGPT may not take “Direct” Share from GOOGL, Presenter emphasizes it will likely capture a meaningful amount of “Incremental” Share.

• Lastly, he acknowledges the upcoming Gemini 4 Launch could be a potential Positive Catalyst, but notes GOOGL is uniquely tied to “Permanent” CapEx to remain “At the Frontier,” a commitment Mgmt. has openly voiced.  Unlike Microsoft [MSFT], Amazon [AMZN], and Meta [META] where CapEx is largely “Discretionary,” Presenter believes GOOGL’s Spend is more “Defensive” and essential to protecting the company’s Core Search Economics.

• He sees “Single-digit% Risk” to Consensus FY27 EPS of $15.08 and arrives at a Price Target of $250/share (~26% Downside), with any incremental deterioration from Agentic Commerce OR ChatGPT Competition pressuring the stock further.

Gildan Activewear Inc. [GIL]

Distributor “Channel Stuffing” Unwind to Strain EBITDA + Hanes Leverage Concerns

• GIL manufactures and sells various Activewear products, including T-shirts, Fleece Tops and Bottoms, Sports Shirts, Polos, Tank Tops, and Socks.

• Presenter has followed the company for many years, having successfully Shorted GIL during a 2006 – 2007 “Channel-stuffing Blowup,” when a Private Distributor with Publicly-traded Debt (subject to 10-K / 10-Q Reporting) revealed RISING GIL Inventory amid weak Sell-through.  He sees striking Parallels today following a June 2026 Report from Jehoshaphat Research, alleging the company is again “Stuffing the Channel,” compounded by the Integration of HanesBrands (closed 12/1/25) this time.

• Presenter explains that ~50% of GIL Revenues flow through 2 remaining Distributors, down from 3 after S&S Activewear (Privately-owned by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice) acquired alphabroder in 2024.  Jehoshaphat’s Receivables Analysis, adjusting for GIL’s Factored Accounts Receivable, shows DSOs stretching as HIGH as ~130 Days at the Company and ~200 at the Distributor Level.  Notably, Presenter emphasizes that GIL’s Core Category Organic Growth (only “LSD%’s”) is TOO SLOW to absorb Excess Channel Inventory, unlike prior Cycles when a faster-growing End-market “Masked” the Overhang.

• Furthermore, with ~$4.6B of Net Debt, GIL carries ~3x Leverage against FY26 Consensus EBITDA of ~$1.6B, suggesting any deterioration in EBITDA would be amplified against Fixed Interest Expense.  He also flags an unresolved Tariff Overhang, as GIL sources Cotton domestically in the US despite being Canadian-domiciled.

• Ultimately, Presenter believes GIL will need to slow Shipments into the Channel, forcing a “Come to Jesus” Earnings Reset.  He estimates $100M – $200M of “Pulled-forward” Revenue could reverse, translating to “At Least” $50M of lost EBITDA.  While he does NOT offer a specific Price Target, he notes even “Minor” Contraction of GIL’s current ~8.5x FY27 Consensus EBITDA Multiple implies $400M – $500M of Value Erosion, with additional Risk to Out-year Forecasts IF expected Share Repurchases are delayed by Leverage constraints.

• PUSHBACK: Another Presenter’s Checks indicate that while S&S’ Working Capital is rising, Sell-Through has reportedly been “Positive.”

GE Vernova Inc. [GEV]

Interconnection + Permitting Delays Threaten “Reserved” Turbine Slots

• GEV engages in the provision of various products and services that generate, transfer, orchestrate, convert, and store Electricity, operating through 3 segments: 1) Power; 2) Wind; and 3) Electrification.

• Presenter believes GEV is in the “Midst of a Transition” and faces “Rotational Risk” alongside the broader AI Ecosystem as Investors appear to be “Moving On.”  GEV was previously charactered as an “Accelerating Growth Story,” but the company’s Order Book, Growth and Earnings Momentum have begun to “PEAK.”

• A Core Holding among many Funds, Presenter describes GEV as a “Well-Owned Consensus, Crowded Long” with shares up ~50% YTD and ~5x since spinning out of General Electric [GE] in April 2024.  Many other AI-related stocks have experienced “Dramatic” De-Ratings and are now screening “Optically Cheap” (e.g., Memory Stocks trading at ~5x Outyear EPS, NVDA at ~10x).  Against this backdrop, GEV’s ~38x Multiple on Consensus FY27 EPS appears MUCH LESS compelling for Investors seeking AI Exposure.

• GEV faces near-term Fundamental issues, including Bipartisan “Backlash” toward AI Infrastructure Deployment, creating Order Fulfillment Uncertainty and denting confidence in sustained Growth.  Presenter views GEV as a “Put Option” on a Democratic Sweep in the November Mid-terms, which would likely pressure all AI Infrastructure-related names.

• Beyond Politics, Presenter sees further Headwinds to Backlog Conversion Longer-term.  While Turbine Slots are sold out through the decade, Slow Deliveries, Permit Challenges, Operational Delays, and Interconnection Limits may prompt Developers to relinquish Reserved Slots, “Destabilizing” the Order Book.  He also anticipates INCREASED Competitive / Disruption Risk from New Entrants, including Korean Manufacturers entering the Large Turbine Market and SpaceX’s [SPCX] planned Satellite Data Centers, which could begin launching Orbital AI Data Center Tests as early as Late 2027, pending Regulatory Approval.

• The GEV Bull Case rests on the company’s Services business, but Presenter argues it will NOT generate meaningful Revenue for 10+ years, “TOO DISTANT” to support Near-term Multiple Expansion.  He feels the Risk / Reward Skew is “Unattractive” and models ~25% Downside from a combination of Multiple De-Rating and Operational Execution Disappointments.  Lastly, he remarks that CFO Ken Parks’ August 27th Retirement Announcement adds further Execution Uncertainty.

DoorDash, Inc. [DASH]

WMT “Dark Store” Expansion Undercuts Restaurant-Heavy Model / Premium Valuation

• DASH provides Restaurant Food Delivery services connecting Customers with Merchants through an On-demand Food Delivery application.

• Presenter’s DASH Short Thesis is centered around Walmart’s [WMT] “Dark Store” Buildout.  Dark Stores are essentially Non-public, Retail-style Facilities dedicated entirely to picking, packing, and fulfilling Online Delivery + Pickup Orders.  During the 2026 ICR Conference in January, WMT was operating just ~7 Dark Stores and targeted 12 – 15 Lower Tier US Cities for expansion.  HOWEVER, Presenter has noticed a significant “Change in Tone” from Mgmt. in recent meetings.

• She frames this dynamic as a “Core Threat” that remains relatively UNKNOWN to most Investors, despite WMT’s plans to open 8 – 10 Dark Stores per Supercenter, potentially exceeding 30K Locations across the Top 50 US Metros.  This mirrors WMT’s “Successful Playbook” in China and India where the company opened ~800 Dark Stores in ONE YEAR.  Her checks with Real Estate Brokers indicate WMT is “Aggressively” targeting Pharmacy and former Dollar Store Locations.

• Presenter emphasizes even a “Modest” ~400 Dark Stores per year from WMT would be a “Direct Hit” to DASH, given 70% – 80% of the company’s Sales originate from Restaurant Delivery, with the remainder split between Grocery and Retail.  She notes QSRs approached WMT directly after feeling “Raked Over The Coals” on Delivery Fees by DASH and Uber Technologies [UBER].  WMT has since rolled out a string of QSR Delivery Partnerships (i.e., Subway [Private], Dunkin’ [Private], Papa John’s [PZZA]), now servicing nearby Restaurants at LOWER Fees, “Undercutting” DASH’s Core while turning previously unprofitable E-commerce Routes profitable.  WMT has NO interest in delivering for EVERY Restaurant nationally but will target Stores within <2 – 4-Miles.

• Given DASH’s PREMIUM Valuation (i.e., ~36x FY26 EPS, ~22x EBITDA), Presenter envisions significant Headline Risk and Multiple Contraction on every New Partnership Announcement signaling “WMT Is Coming After Their Business.”  Dark Stores may NOT even impact DASH’s near-term Fundamentals, but she draws a parallel to Maplebear [CART] in 2025, when continuous Amazon [AMZN] Headlines drove a ~35% decline in the shares.  Her Price Target is $129/share (~36% Downside).

• Finally, Presenter contends Peers are LESS exposed, given UBER’s Diversification with Ride Sharing and just ~26% US Restaurant Delivery Share vs. DASH’s ~66%, while CART remains insulated through its Grocery-focused, Retailer-Partnership model.  Thus far, WMT Mgmt. has been “Deliberately Vague” about the Rollout Pace, wary of the Political Sensitivity around displacing Local Stores, yet Presenter expects Dark Stores to be a KEY Topic at WMT’s Analyst Day in April 2027.

Bending Spoons S.P.A. [BSP]

“Roll-Up of Commoditized Software Assets” Masks Decelerating Organic Growth

• BSP designs and develops Software and Platforms that support acquisitions, transformations, and ongoing optimizations, with Portfolio of Assets including AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Harvest, Komoot, Remini, StreamYard, Vimeo, WeTransfer, and Tractive.

• Presenter describes BSP as a “LOWER Quality Roll-Up of Orphaned Software Assets” whose playbook is to “RAISE Prices and CUT Costs,” emphasizing Price Increases often EXCEED ~200% while ~90% of Acquired Staff is eliminated.  While this formula often works in the short-term, the Model eventually “Runs Out of Users to Churn,” forcing BSP to continuously acquire MORE businesses to drive Growth.  At ~12x Street FY27 EBITDA, the stock trades In-line or ABOVE “Premium Software Compounders” like Roper Technologies [ROP] and Constellation Software [CSU.CN] despite a “Commoditized” Portfolio that can be “Easily Disrupted” by AI.

• Notably, Organic Growth has DECELERATED from “Low-Teens%” prior to the IPO to just ~3% in 2Q26.  Presenter argues that the current Growth Rate is “Flattered” by the company’s practice of including LTM Acquisitions, highlighting “Pro Forma Growth” that benefits from adding Faster-growing Assets.  3P Data reveals DAUs and MAUs across BSP’s larger assets DECLINING at a “MSD% – HSD%” Rate since acquisition, with businesses owned for ~3 years still SHRINKING.  Mgmt. previously disclosed Net Retention in the “Low-90%’s,” a figure that INCLUDES “A Ton of Price,” but stopped reporting the metric last quarter.  Presenter believes Gross Retention is ~70% “At Best,” noting many of BSP’s products have Free / “Freemium” Alternatives.

• He highlights ~50% of Operating Income is generated by AOL, Vimeo, and Eventbrite, with ~80% of the company’s Assets acquired from 2024 onward.  AOL was purchased from Apollo Global Mgmt. [APO] at ~3.5x EBITDA, and Presenter estimates this asset represents ~2/3rds of Future FCF, implying Investors are paying a “Massive HoldCo Premium” for a business that “Would Be Down ~90%” IF Publicly-traded.  Growing Backlash toward the company’s Price Hikes has also drawn coverage from major Media outlets, with one comparing BSP’s Business Model to Valeant Pharmaceuticals.  Presenter also flags that ~40% of IPO proceeds were Secondary, which he views as a signal that confidence is “Eroding” among Insiders.

• The IPO Lockup Expiry, expected in November / December 2026, is a Key Near-term Catalyst with an estimated ~300M shares set to unlock.  Presenter concedes that a “Cheap” Cost of Capital could keep the “Self-Reinforcing Loop” of Accretive M&A going for a while but believes “Rational Investors” are likely to sell.  Applying a ~4x Multiple to FY27 Pro Forma Revenues, he arrives at a Price Target of $20/share (~48% Downside).

BETA Technologies, Inc. [BETA]

EVTOL Backlog “Mostly Non-Binding” with Range Shortfalls + Substantial Cash Burn

• BETA is an Electric Aerospace company, designs, manufactures, and sells Electric Aircraft, Electric Propulsion Systems, Components, and Charging Systems worldwide.

• Mgmt. and the Street expect a “Hockey Stick” Revenue Inflection in 2027 – 2028, though Presenter is Bearish on both BETA’s future prospects and the eVTOL space more broadly.  He thinks Air Taxis are “Trying to Solve a Problem That Does NOT Exist,” noting several Infrastructure Constraints remain “Unsolved” while the Federal Aviation Administration [FAA] has “NO Incentive to Expedite Approvals.”  Even IF the Market exists, Presenter believes BETA is the LEAST likely to reach Certification or Commercialization as the company is “At Least 2.5 Years BEHIND” Joby Aviation [JOBY] on the Certification path.

• BETA’s eVTOL design has “Basic Structural Flaws,” as its 4-Rotor Configuration (vs. 6 for JOBY) leaves INSUFFICIENT redundancy.  Presenter contends the Aircraft will “Never Get Through Certification in Its Current Design,” pointing to the Company's “Quiet Halt” of eVTOL work and full “Pivot” toward eCTOL, Electric Propulsion on a regular Fixed-wing Airplane, as evidence Mgmt. is aware of this dynamic.

• Presenter highlights Test Flight Data showing BETA’s CX300 eCTOL Aircraft performing far WORSE than claimed, with NOT a single Flight crossing even HALF the stated ~330 Nautical-Mile Max Range and an Average of just ~75 Nautical Miles.  For comparison, Textron’s [TXT] Cessna Caravan has been in service since the 1980’s and has a 1,000+ Nautical Miles Range.  Meanwhile, the CX300 is SLOWER, carries HALF the Payload / Occupants, and will likely Cost MORE.  BETA’s claim of lower Operating Costs “Ignores” Battery Replacement Costs, as well as HIGHER paid Pilot Hours per Trip that come with slower Cruise Speeds.  Presenter’s Checks with Pilots also revealed Takeoff and Landing issues.

• He argues that BETA’s ~$4B Backlog is “Heavily Overstated” as only ~32% are “Firm” Orders that are backed by just $22M of Deferred Revenue primarily from “Related Parties.”  Furthermore, much of the Order Book is comprised of “Stale” Orders from several years ago, alongside Orders from Customers with “Questionable” Credit Quality.

• BETA is burning more than $500M annually with just ~$1.3B of Net Cash, leaving LESS THAN 3 years of Runway.  Presenter is “Highly Skeptical” of Full Certification by the end of 2027, increasing the Risk of a potential “Liquidity Event” in 2028.  While he does not provide a specific Price Target, he views 2027 as a “Show-Me Year” and maintains BETA will have “Little to Show” over the next 12 – 18 months.

Akamai Technologies, Inc. [AKAM]

GPU Contracts Earn “Sub-Par” Paybacks while Hyperscalers Reap AI Returns

• AKAM provides services for accelerating and improving the delivery of Content and Applications over the Internet, ranging from Live and On-demand Streaming Video capabilities to conventional Website Content.

• Presenter believes AKAM essentially functions as a “Smaller Hyperscaler,” renting Compute secured via a “Preferred Allocation” of NVIDIA [NVDA] RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, but on Contract Terms that carry “UN-attractive” ROI.  At a recent Sell-side Conference, GCP [Google Cloud Platform; GOOGL] explicitly outlined an AI Server Payback Period of UNDER 2 years, falling to just ~1 year on the company’s proprietary TPUs.  By contrast, Presenter estimates AKAM’s signed Contracts carry Payback Periods of 3.0 – 4.5 Years.

• He calculates the company’s 1st major Deal, a $1.8B, 7-year Commitment with Anthropic [Private], implies a ~4.5-year Payback, though Initial Contract Terms may have been LESS favorable as Mgmt. worked to land a “Marquee” Customer.  AKAM’s 2nd Deal, a $600M, 4-year Agreement with a Robotics Company, implies a Payback Period of 3 – 4 years, nearly the length of the Contract itself.  Presenter believes AKAM is signing “LOW Calorie” Deals to boost Revenue Growth “Optics,” a strategy that has already forced Mgmt. to “Pause” the company’s Buyback in 2Q26 to fund ongoing HIGHER CapEx.

• Presenter is also skeptical of Mgmt.’s Agentic AI Tailwind Narrative for the legacy Content Delivery Network [CDN] business, emphasizing they have only cited “Theoretical Use Cases,” such as AI-enabled Virtual Fitting Rooms for E-commerce, WITHOUT any confirmed Customer Deployments to date.  Furthermore, IF Meta Platforms’ [META] Muse becomes the “Agentic AI Product of Choice,” META would simply leverage its OWN Infrastructure.  For AKAM’s CDN business to succeed, a “NON-Incumbent” Agentic AI Provider must both “Win” AND choose AKAM for Delivery.  In addition, this business faces “Tougher Comps” next year after benefiting from the World Cup in 2Q26.

• Lastly, Presenter recommends pairing AKAM Short vs. Long Hyperscalers, given the Setup is partially dependent on broader AI-cycle Timing.  Applying a “Premium” ~17.5x Multiple to his 2028 FCF/share Estimate of $5.20, he arrives at a Price Target of $90/share (~16% Downside).

Autodesk, Inc. [ADSK]

AI Design Tools Jeopardize Seat Counts / Margin Targets

• ADSK supplies PC Software and Multimedia Tools, including 2D and 3D Computer-aided Design [CAD] products used for Architectural Design, Mechanical Design, Geographic Information Systems & Mapping, and Visualization applications.

• Presenter’s Thesis centers on “AI Disintermediation Risk,” pointing to OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra as the FIRST Credible Evidence that General-purpose AI can automate “Meaningful” CAD and 3D Design Work, scoring 95.9% on BenchCAD vs. 83.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 84.3% for Claude Fable 5.1.  Presenter acknowledges it does NOT yet replace ADSK’s full Engineering, Building Information Modeling [BIM] or the Compliance Stack, but the product can already convert 2D Plans into editable 3D Environments, write Code to construct Models, and operate specialized Software directly, work that supports many Junior / Intermediate ADSK Seats.

• Presenter views Claude’s similar, although less “Mature,” Agentic Design capabilities as confirmation this is an Industry-wide Shift, implying ADSK now faces an entire “Ecosystem,” NOT a Single Competitor.  He believes ADSK risks becoming merely the Database and Geometry Engine beneath an AI-controlled Workflow, which would likely result in Seat Compression, Pricing Resistance, and Margin Pressure.  His Bear Case Scenario forecasts Organic Growth falling to 5% – 7%, vs. Long-term Expectations of ~10%, and FY29 Margins of just 35% – 37%, BELOW Mgmt.’s 41% Target.

• Presenter also flags deteriorating Fundamentals independent of AI, emphasizing F2Q27 Revenue grew ~16%, with ~2ppts tied to a “Transaction-model Change,” while Billings grew just ~10%, Total RPO grew only ~2%, and Unbilled Deferred Revenue DECLINED ~8%.  He also highlights ADSK’s ~$3.6B Acquisition of MaintainX, an “Unprofitable” Business purchased for a “Lofty” ~26x ARR [Annual Recurring Revenue], arguing the deal ADDS Debt and Integration Risk outside the company’s Core Design Franchise.

• Lastly, Presenter notes Autodesk University 2026, held September 15th – 17th, showcased Agentic AI feature demonstrations across the company’s verticals as expected, but LACKED Detail on Incremental Pricing Models or Consumption Revenue Frameworks.  He arrives at a Price Target of $150/share (~30% Downside) based on a combination of P/E, Price/FCF, and DCF.

The presenter would like to discuss Verisure as a long.

Verisure is the number one professionally monitored alarm provider in Europe and LATAM, selling and installing proprietary hardware, and generating revenue through monthly monitoring fees. It has a €9 billion market cap and a €14 billion EV. It IPO'd in October 2025. This is a high-quality compounder trading at a 10% steady-state free cash flow yield and approximately 6x steady-state EBITDA, that is misunderstood by the market for a few reasons. One, there are significant reinvestments masking cash flow potential. Two, there is a misunderstood AI risk. And three, there is a PE sponsor overhang.

With more than 6 million subscribers, the company has nearly 40% share of the installed base across its footprint. However, its footprint is just 4% penetrated, while the US market has a penetration of over 20%. In order to capture this massive TAM, Verisure is currently reinvesting approximately 70% of its steady-state free cash flow into acquiring new customers. Investors seem to struggle to understand how attractive this reinvestment opportunity is. With leading 7% attrition rates and impressive margins, the presenter thinks Verisure is generating 20% unlevered IRRs on each new customer, supporting double-digit free cash flow growth for years to come.

There are concerns that AI-enabled tech poses a threat to Verisure. The presenter does not think this view really holds water. The company has continued to grow uninterrupted for decades, despite concerns that DIY offerings from tech giants like Amazon and Google would take share. Moreover, in many of its core markets, regulations require alarm systems to be professionally installed and monitored, creating a meaningful barrier to entry for new competitors lacking Verisure's 12,000-person sales and installation workforce. Rather than being disrupted by AI, the presenter expects Verisure to benefit from the implementation of AI, improving efficiency across all aspects of its business.

As it relates to the PE sponsor overhang, the company was IPO'd in October 2025 by Hellman and Friedman (H&F), who have owned this company since 2011. To extend the life of the investment, H&F completed a fund transfer of the asset in December 2020 after realizing an 8x MOIC on its initial investment. The presenter believes that H&F are likely true long-term believers in Verisure's potential and have a history of holding assets for 20+ years. With today's share price at nearly the new fund's cost basis—35% below the IPO price, and more than 50% below its 52-week high—the presenter does not believe they are sellers anytime soon. The new fund’s basis is approximately today's price (a bit less than €9). Important to note, the presenter believes this is not comparable to ADT. ADT is a much worse business than Verisure for a few reasons. Verisure is completely vertically integrated with 40% market share. ADT uses an independent dealer network with inferior technology, and maintains a much lower market share (closer to 20%). This contributes to attrition that is more than double Verisure's, meaningfully weaker margins, and customer NPVs that are materially worse. And Verisure's markets have a far larger growth runway versus the nearly fully-penetrated US market.

The presenter thinks the predictability of the business lends itself to a DCF valuation. Using the presenter’s conservative base case, using an 8% discount rate, the stock could double from current levels and could compound to a triple over the next few years. The presenter thinks investors will better appreciate the company's business model, as its reinvestment rate reduces significantly in the coming quarters and its FCF generation becomes more obvious.

The presenter would like to discuss Uber as a long.

Uber has a $145 billion cap. It trades $1.5 billion per day. It is currently trading at 12x EBITDA (which is 6.5x turns below its historical three-year average).

This is not an AI loser or an AV loser. If you ride in a Waymo, Model X, an Aurora truck, or a Waabi semi, it will be clear that multiple players are going to get to Level 4+. Level 4+ is simply an industry term that means driver out, and no safety driver required in an autonomous vehicle. Uber has nearly 40 AV partners that are working towards this outcome, and the presenter thinks several of them are going to be successful in doing so. They have collectively committed to 120,000 AVs on Uber's network across those partners in the coming years.

NVIDIA is also helping. They have their own open-source platform, Alpamayo. Their incentive, by opening up an AV model, is obviously to sell GPUs into the assembly kit, but it gives autonomous capabilities to basically any OEM who wants to buy it. Componentry for AVs is also getting cheaper. The BOM (Bill of Materials) is lower by 50% to 75% over the last couple of years, depending whose estimates you look at. Lower cost components make it easier to get AV players to Level 4 and it also makes it more economical.

In terms of market share, Uber has 70% share of rides in the US. Here is a little context. Tesla has done two-and-a-half million total rides since launching last year (that is as of 2Q 2026). Waymo does 500,000 per week, Lyft does 20 million per week, and Uber does 45 to 60 million rides per week in the US.

Any of the players who crack Level 4 are going to want to go where the demand is, which is Uber. Behavior is hard to change, and Uber has a product that is more flexible than Elon's double-digit count of FSD robotaxis, because of the human driver. We all know Elon has walked back many AV claims, like incorporating the whole Tesla car park into the robotaxi fleet. He basically said the entire Tesla fleet would be capable of going into a robotaxi fleet—that if you have a Model X two years ago, you are going to bring it in, and you can have it go do rides for you at night when you are watching TV. He has obviously walked that back. To further that point, the presenter believes Uber's claim that they have gained share in the legacy AV markets of LA, San Francisco, and Phoenix, and it checks out in their data. Beyond the AV dynamics, the food delivery business has been growing healthily, with a stable to improving take-rate. The presenter also thinks the Delivery Hero deal is logical. On a pro forma basis, the presenter is mid-single digits above the Street on EBITDA in 2027 and is high-teens above the Street in 2028. The presenter thinks 20x is the right multiple for a fast-growing, profitable leader. This is where it traded prior to the AI/AV risk becoming mainstream. They also generate a lot of cash, and spend a lot on buybacks. So the presenter thinks investors get paid to fade the AI risk here.

The presenter would like to discuss Tractor Supply as a long after today's industry conference presentation. The stock was down 3.7% today, mainly, in the presenter’s opinion, driven by shorter-term duration investors who were thinking they would provide a quarter-to-date update, which they have not done over the past couple of events.

In terms of the setup, the stock started the year at $50, and traded as low as $29, before recovering to $34 over the past couple of months. In the presenter’s view, the stock was pretty much untouchable over the last year because of weak pet industry trends, as well as concerns over market share losses to Amazon, Chewy, Walmart, and the big mass retailers, which led to long-term investor capitulation.

But what makes it interesting now is that the presenter believes that full-year guidance was finally reset to a beatable level on the Q2 print. The full-year comp growth was cut to -1% to flat, from +1% to +3%, and that implies approximately -1.5% to slightly positive comp growth in the back half, despite significantly easier compares.

The current data implies that trends could end the quarter approximately 100 to 200 basis points ahead of the Street's -1% Q3 estimate. Compares then ease by approximately 360 basis points in Q4, and then they stay muted through the first half of 2027. So theoretically, the two-year math, you can extrapolate a return to low-single-digit and mid-single-digit comps by next quarter. That is in line with management's long-term algorithm, which to some extent, the presenter believes theyre iterated during today's conference presentation. So why have trends improved in recent months? The presenter thinks there are several different reasons. First, the presenter thinks the Q2 -1.5% comp growth was driven mainly by unfavorable weather back in May, and they commented on this during their last earnings call. What the presenter thinks you saw was a shifting of the spring selling season to later in the year, so you are simply delaying sales growth until this coming quarter, which is why the data seems to have accelerated quite meaningfully.

Second, the presenter thinks category trends are finally bottoming, to some extent. This is finally normalizing following COVID's excessive growth. It is important to remember that Tractor Supply's comp growth against 2019 is still one of the best in retail (approximately 6%). The presenter has also heard from several consumer staples companies like J M Smucker speak to improving pet trends in recent weeks, which is a good sign for the business. Third, company-specific initiatives, such as the push into pet animal services (which is growing at a faster rate), price investments funded by the tariff refunds, vendor rebates, as well as merchandise exchanges (for example, introducing Freshpet to the assortment), which have helped or are ramping up and are starting to help now.

And then lastly, commodity prices have become, or will likely become a big tailwind, with corn prices up approximately 25% over the last 12 months. It bodes well for an inelastic category (for example, the animal feed that they sell). And what the presenter has seen with names like Ulta Beauty, Target, and Dollar Tree is that comp growth inflections lead to significant multiple recovery. The company has historically traded between a range of 14x to 26x PE. It is currently trading approximately 17x PE (around the low end of the range). If comp growth is able to sustainably inflect to low to mid-singles for the next couple of quarters, the presenter would expect the stock to re-rate to low 20x, and then potentially higher if longer term investors start to revisit the name.

Additionally, this is a defensive name that is easier to own in this choppy macro environment with yields and oil prices rising. Ultimately, with improving top-line growth, it is a very favorable risk-reward. It screens as an attractive long, or a good hedge for a consumer short.

In terms of a price target, the presenter believes it is worth $40 to $45 (in the near term), and ultimately it could be worth $50 if investors revisit the name.

The presenter would like to discuss Turning Point Brands as a long.

Turning Point Brands is a nicotine product and rolling paper company. It has a product portfolio that includes legacy brands Stoker's, which consists of snus and chew products, and Zig-Zag, which makes rolling papers, and a much faster growing set of products that are branded FRE and ALP (both nicotine pouch brands). That is the beginning, middle, and end of the thesis. The business is primarily focused on the nicotine pouch market. FRE is wholly owned by Turning Point. ALP is a 50/50 JV with Tucker Carlson. Turning Point does not have a combustible tobacco business.

In short, Turning Point is a compelling long opportunity because of its earnings growth outlook, which is supported by both secular tailwinds as well as market share gains. The company offers direct exposure to the nicotine pouch theme, simply as a percentage of the overall business mix. They have been on a tear for this past year. ALP and FRE have both been rolled out into national chains.

Historically this was not their sales tactic. Historically Turning Point would partner with independent stores, and effectively have sales people who sold out of their trunks. This year was a big step forward in terms of making a more institutionalized push, in terms of getting incremental market share and investing in marketing. They signed a deal with TKO earlier this year. They signed Conor McGregor as their European spokesperson. They are in the middle of this business transformation.

In terms of the legacy business, you have Stoker's and Zig-Zag, which pay a dividend and generate cash flow. Towards the end of 2025, the stock ran up materially (close to $140). The shares are currently trading around $74. The stock price ran up because you started to see the benefit of these independent chains and direct-to-consumer online marketplaces selling out their FRE and ALP products.

There was an intentional effort this year to invest more in sales and marketing. They are doing that, and there is a timing mismatch here. You run into contra revenue, stocking fees, slotting fees, etc. You also run into sales force productivity issues, where you are paying them up front and they slowly scale up.

This is a business that generated $120 million of EBITDA last year, will likely generate ~$80 million this year, and the presenter thinks it will run rate at the end of the year to around $120 million as well. If you give them credit for their old multiple (approximately 25x), for a business that is growing 20% to 30% per annum, you are looking at a business that the presenter thinks is worth closer to $140 to $150 per share over the next 12 months. If you are bullish on the nicotine pouch opportunity, although it is marketed as this de-risk product, ultimately it is bringing new folks into the category. You could reach a point by the end of the decade here where if they are able to get their 10% target market share, you are looking at $1 billion of pouch revenue. Now, obviously that is very assumption-rich, and you could do your own sensitivities around that. But the presenter thinks this is a very compelling opportunity, especially as a way to play the pouch theme.

In the presenter’s opinion, the biggest risk here is Tucker Carlson. The presenter’s view is that Turning Point’s regulatory headwinds will not be a punitive measure by the Trump administration, that the FDA will not be weaponized. Historically, Trump has been relatively pro-flavored vape and flavored nicotine pouch. It is really, the presenter thinks, a difficult case to make against Turning Point, but they think that is the principal risk here. They sell flavored pouches. ALP specifically sells a mint and a berry flavor. They do not sell vapes, but vapes have gotten approved by this FDA, so you could buy a berry vape, and that is a reduced risk product in the FDA's assertion.

The presenter would like to discuss TKO as a long.

The presenter has a playbook in terms of what they are looking for in the consumer sector as potential longs They are looking for companies that fundamentally have printed well, with an elite management team, which deserve a premium multiple, but have traded poorly YTD and continue to do so.

In the presenter’s opinion, TKO sits at the intersection of short-term investors that are uncomfortable with the Middle East mix of promotional fee upside, as well as the event calendar. You saw Formula One had to cancel events. The presenter thinks a lot of investors who are long-term bulls in TKO want both incremental WWE as well as UFC site fees, and potentially more weekends spent in Jeddah or Riyadh, which they think is all fair. But if you take a step back, the stock has pulled back to a trough multiple on a forward basis at the exact moment when effectively all of their major media rights are now penciled in, including significant contractual step-ups. Those are going to start contributing in the back half and accelerate from there.

In terms of the setup, the stock is down 10% year over year, even though WWE has smashed sponsorship expectations (even versus the expectations of the perma bulls). The presenter thinks there is a little bit of uncertainty as it relates to the PSKY / HBO integration, and what does that mean if you really want to model your ratings reach on a UFC basis. But from the presenter's perspective, when you are buying it here, none of those factors are that relevant. Ultimately, they got a great step-up.

The presenter thinks Zuffa boxing is extremely interesting, so they want to come back to that as a potential third leg of the stool. You are looking at something that trades far cheaper than Formula One. The presenter thinks Ari and Mark, without question, are the best relationship managers in the business. If you really wanted to pound the table on the short thesis, media laggards are not going to buy sports, or some argument that there will not be upside for WWE’s next step-up, the presenter thinks Ari is going to take care of that.

Ultimately, the presenter thinks he has already shown that, frankly. If you just listen to what they are saying, this is a super conservative management team. They are always conservative. In Q1, they just beat-and-raised. The presenter is about to see the acceleration in the back half.

And if you look at Zuffa (their boxing promotion company), from the presenter's perspective at least, consumers have argued that there is an incremental sports league to be started—probably the best example being spring football. This is a business that already has all the contract workers in place, where they set up a ring on Friday for SmackDown, they can roll UFC Saturday, and you can see a world outside of football season where Sunday night becomes Zuffa night. It is not only not priced in, it is not even modeled. There is nobody on the Street trying to pencil out any form of actual math.

Zuffa is their version of attempting to create a WWE-style contract worker boxing media right that they can then sell. The business was formed as a 50% JV with Turki Al-Sheikh. They do not own all the upside but they also put in none of the capital risk up front. But what the presenter likes about it is it is not even part of the story / thesis at the moment. This is not like Formula One, where you hear people arguing about the undercard incremental races. No one is even bringing it up. WWE President Nick Khan is from Vegas. He is obsessed with boxing. Ari Emanuel is incredibly cagey about his ability to get stuff done. The presenter thinks there is a world in which they put on a decent amount of these fights next year, they become interesting, and then very quickly this becomes part of the story / thesis. If you were buying it at a fully priced forward multiple, it is a little bit harder to digest there. But the presenter thinks to own it here, it makes it super simple. That is call option upside.

If there is any sort of conclusion to the war, the stock rebounds effectively overnight, because people want more events in the Middle East because it has higher site fees. Globally, UFC is performing quite well. The presenter also thinks this is taking place at a talent trough. The presenter thinks there has not been a marketable Connor McGregor-type talent to market in a long time. Just the math would tell you, they will stumble their way into someone here. The presenter gets to a conservative base case / target price of $236, implying roughly 25% upside from current levels with limited downside. Investors are buying the stock near a trough multiple. On 2027 numbers, the presenter is at roughly 16x Adjusted EBITDA and 14x 2028 Adjusted EBITDA. Compared with Formula One, which the presenter would argue has a more complicated operating structure, it becomes a relatively clean story. You also have the LA Olympics in 2028, which the presenter thinks should be a major event for On Location. As you move through 2027, that should become a much bigger part of the story.

Does the presenter think this stock can double? Of course not. It is expensive and historically has been. But the presenter has seen that premium sports rights and live-event entertainment continue to command a bid. The presenter does not think the stock should be this caught up in Middle Eastern headline risk and believes the current multiple presents an interesting entry point.

The presenter would like to discuss Patrick Industries as a long.

For context, Patrick Industries is an upstream RV parts supplier. They are merging with the number two player in the industry, L CI Industries, and the deal is expected to close in the first half of next year.

The stock is currently trading at $77. Standalone, Patrick Industries has a $2.7 billion market cap and a $4 billion TEV. It has 35 million shares outstanding. Pro forma for the deal, the combined company would have a $5 billion market cap and a $7 billion TEV.

The presenter likes it for a few reasons. Number one, it is trading at a mid-cycle multiple, even on trough-ish earnings and a trough RV cycle. The stock is down 35% YTD. RV wholesale shipments have been guided down twice this year and are likely going to be under 300,000. This compares to a normalized number which is closer to 400,000. For context, shipments peaked at 600,000 during the pandemic.

Number two, you have $150 million of cost synergies that are likely conservative on a COGS base of $6 billion, and OPEX of $1.3 billion. That would add approximately $20 per share. And then the content per unit has been structurally growing. It has been from a combination of pricing as well as adding more value to the RV. Patrick focuses more on the interior of the RV, while L CI Industrials focuses more on the exterior of the RV. They have also been rolling up some of the smaller suppliers of those parts. So even though the RV industry is at trough, both companies have done a good job of compounding their top line.

Finally, the deal would increase the aftermarket exposure of the combined company. For Patrick Industries, only 10% of total revenue is derived from aftermarket while LCI Industries is closer to 30%. Important to note, aftermarket is higher margin. In terms of the pro forma valuation, they should be able to generate $1 billion of EBITDA, including synergies. The presenter has them generating a little over $1.2 billion by 2028, which does not assume a meaningful industry inflection and assumes RV units are 10% higher than they are currently. If you put a 9x multiple on that—it has historically traded in the 8x to 9x range—that equates to a $135 stock, with 75% upside from current levels.

The presenter would like to discuss Life Time Group as a long.

For those not familiar with Life Time, it is the largest owner and operator of high-end fitness centers in the US. They own / operate approximately 200 centers today.

The stock has performed well year to date, but the presenter thinks it still has room to run, in terms of both the multiple and out-year earnings. The pitch is fairly simple. Their algo is very good. They are opening mid-teens of new centers per year, and that will likely go to the low 20s by 2030. But simply from opening new centers, you get more members, and those members add 5% to 6% to revenue over time.

They also have strong same-store sales growth. In recent years, it has been low double digits. This past quarter it was 9%. It will naturally come down to 5% or 6% over time. But same-store sales are driven by taking price on legacy members, as well as mix shift (when you have old members churn). When new members come in, the bench rate for new membership is much higher. Plus, people tend to sign up for more expensive plans like a family plan. And then in-store ancillary spend—personal training, Pilates or pickleball—everything else continues to grow very quickly.

Between the member growth and same-store growth, you get combined revenue growth of 11% or 12%. There is operating leverage on that. The presenter thinks you get to low-teens EBITDA growth over time. Today it is much better than that. In the presenter’s opinion, it will be 15% + through the end of this year and for all of 2027. So the presenter believes you have a great earnings algo.

Also worth noting, they have a phenomenal customer base. The presenter thinks thematically, you have a high-end customer, in a good category (health & wellness), and it is an “in-person” experience, which the presenter thinks are all areas within consumer that are showing great growth (a great thematic trend).

Their management is also viewed as very good operators. They beat and raise every single quarter, and the presenter thinks they finally figured out how to communicate with the Street, which should bode well for the stock.

It currently trades at only 9.5x EBITDA. If you look at the stock, it was $26 to start the year, and it is $42 currently. Important to note, there were two large overhangs on the stock coming into the year. The first was that fundamentally, if you looked at membership growth, it looked like it was growing low single digits, and investors thought they were taking a lot of price and that they could not grow members. That was largely because they were opening smaller centers and not as many centers in recent years. But, more so during the pandemic, they added a bunch of “qualified memberships.” These were members who were paying materially less. For example, these members were paying approximately $60 instead of $280, and now they are simply churning those people out. They are not letting them renew or they are forcing them out more aggressively. That is obviously very good for your mix, but it makes the blended membership rate look a lot lower when the core memberships are growing 4%, and as they add more centers in coming years, let us say you get the 5% or 6%. And then there was also a massive technical overhang on it. The stock was simply not very liquid. In the presenter’s opinion, investors knew Leonard Green and TPG were going to sell every single quarter. Now Leonard Green and TPG have gone from owning over 30% a few years ago to sub-5% combined today. They are essentially done selling. It trades over $100 million per day now. So it is finally liquid enough, and investors do not have to worry about secondaries.

And when the presenter looks at the rest of the Gaming, Leisure, & Lodging sector, they compare it to hotels and cruise lines. The C-corps are amazing businesses. They do not grow that fast. They are very expensive, and they have their own issues regarding fee concerns. Then cruise lines have a myriad of issues, and this trades closer to a cruise line, but you do not have to worry about oil. You do not have to worry about oversupply in the Caribbean, or low river levels in Europe. Even though Viking is a great stock, the presenter thinks Viking trades expensive relative to Life Time although it has a similar growth profile, and actually much more predictable growth for Life Time.

The presenter thinks now that it is more liquid, with memberships expected to increase, and they will likely beat and raise again starting this quarter (and every quarter for the foreseeable future), the presenter thinks it will attract more interest from investors who had viewed it as not liquid enough or had other concerns in the past.

As it relates to the technical dynamic, with PE selling down their stakes, this obviously increases the float, so you will get the next S&P rebalance in a few weeks. There has been a lot of selling over the past few months, which means there should be a material re-balancing for them. So, you could see a few hundred million dollars worth of passive flows—which is small, but it is helpful at the margin.

In terms of the presenter's price target, they think it could trade to 13x EBITDA—equivalent to a 1x EBITDA PEG ratio—which would equate to a $65 stock price using their 2027 EBITDA assumptions.

The presenter would like to discuss Brunswick as a short.

In terms of the business, Brunswick sell sand maintains boats. The positive to this story is that most of the EBITDA or EBIT now comes from boat maintenance, but that has stopped growing, and has now been flat to declining. They will generate ~$350 million of EBIT this year, of which ~75% comes from their parts and accessories business (maintenance) and 25% is generated from their sales business. In the past, these two segments contributed closer to 50% each, but obviously given the decline in consumption and higher interest rates post-COVID, that has changed.

However, given what has gone on with interest rates and gas prices, the presenter thinks those two factors are having a fairly negative effect on boat sales. Boat sales are down 4% YTD, and the presenter suspects they will be even worse in the third quarter because of elevated gas prices. The presenter thinks you have a stock where there are expectations for both segments to be up year-over-year, and given sales are down along with elevated gas prices (the presenter believes people drove their boats less in the summer), there is likely going to be less P&A. If you put a historical multiple of ~12x EPS, that would equate to a stock in the $50s or $60s versus $70 today. And on EBITDA, you get a lot more because there is leverage on that.

The presenter's simple thesis is that this is a stock that has all the wrong factors (oil and interest rates). And if the Fed raises interest rates later this month, it is likely an incremental negative for them, because consumers tend to buy cars and boats on credit.

And from a macro / war standpoint, if you are Iran, they know that there is an election coming up in November. If you want to hurt Trump, this is the best chance to hurt him. The presenter believes that Iran will instigate, elevate, and escalate in October.

The presenter would like to discuss Aramark as a long.

Aramark is a leading global provider of food and facilities services to education, health care, business and industry, sports, leisure, and corrections clients; more recently they have entered the data center market. The largest market is the United States, with a 15-country footprint outside of that which comprises their international segment.

Aramark manages interrelated services, food, and hospitality procurement for school districts, colleges, universities, and health care. These are sticky businesses that are all very profitable, so the presenter would argue that the risk of contract infringement or anything like that is pretty low.

There are two reportable segments. They have a US and International segment. The US is approximately 70% while International is the remaining 30%. And within the US, they have the five different segments that the presenter mentioned earlier. They have been generating organic sales growth of mid-single digit plus, accelerating over the last couple of years in the +7% to +9% range. Over the last four quarters, they have added major contracts within all verticals. The Healthcare segment in particular added two significant new customers. They added UPenn Medicine, which is approximately 4,000 beds (which is how they typically measure contracts), and then they added RWJBarnabas Health, which is another 5,700 beds. Those were their two largest contracts ever.

And then in sports and leisure, they have won Stone Mountain, Georgia, which is a resort, Texas State Athletics, FSU, and then Oklahoma and Alabama Departments of Corrections. In education, they have added Texas State, Grand Canyon University, Colorado Springs, and some other big businesses like Paul Weiss, Toyota, Discovery, and Blue Origin. Year to date, they have added approximately $1.6 billion in new client wins. They have averaged adding ~$600 million per quarter in new business.

Then in April (this is what the presenter believes is exciting to investors), they have added a new business segment called Nexus, which consists of their data center management service. When all these data centers are being built, Aramark will build campuses with gyms, dining rooms, and various facilities to make it enjoyable for the workers constructing the data centers, and there are a number of these data centers being built at the moment. They build a campus right next to it where everyone is housed, and then they are managing those facilities. It is pre and post construction. The contracts are typically four to five years. Data centers are typically built in two to four years, give or take, so this is a big point of expansion.

Each per capita is approximately $40,000 to $45,000 per head, so they are meaningful contracts. They average about $140 to $160 million per year. They just started ramping, so the contribution this year will be minimal, but they should get to north of $500 million next year. The presenter has them doing a little over $1 billion in 2028. Then in 2029, the presenter has them well over $1.5 billion. The scaling is pretty fast.

They are working with three hyperscalers currently and three individual data centers, but each of those hyperscalers have several different data centers—between 7 and 12 each—so the presenter believes the ability to add within those three clients is pretty strong. You can see them generating well over $2 billion down the road by 2030 if that happens. The presenter has them generating ~$2.2 billion of EBITDA in FY 28. If you put a conservative 11x multiple on that, you can get to a $77 target price. The presenter believes the multiple has room to expand to 12x to 13x. Some of the Street analysts are giving them a 13.5x multiple, which the presenter thinks is a little rich, but 12x to 13x would equate to an $85 or $90 target price.
