The presenter would like to discuss Semtech as a long.

Semtech is a diversified supplier of analog mixed-signal components. Approximately 35% of the business is related to signal integrity (housing its high-growth FiberEdge, CopperEdge business). Another 35% lies within its protection, sensing, and wireless products. The remaining 30% is related to various IoT assets. The presenter believes you will see significant upside from that signal integrity business that houses the fiber and connectivity solutions. First, within signal integrity, Semtech holds assets utilized in transceivers, such as TIAs and drivers. Semtech should benefit materially from the upcoming transceiver cycle. First, the overall volume of high-speed transceivers should see significant growth. The presenter thinks the market is coming from a base of 80 to 90 million 800 G and up transceivers this year to 160 to 180 million in 800 G next year—so that is roughly a double in terms of volume. The second part is, within that mix, you have more products shifting to the next-generation 1.6T transceivers. The presenter believes those next-generation transceivers can offer ASPs up to 50% to 100% higher versus the 800-gig generation for their TIA products. Within the transceiver mix specifically, the presenter expects 1.6T volume to grow from approximately 20% of the mix to just under 50%, which offers pricing upside.

And on top of that, in the next generation, Semtech should maintain strong share. Along with the organic growth as well, they made a recent acquisition of HieFo, which expands their SAM within the transceiver module market and gives them assets and a roadmap to attack the emerging NPO/CPO opportunities.

Outside of the FiberEdge business, you also can look at the copper assets. There should be growth within their linear equalizer business, which is utilized to extend the reach of copper cables. Semtech's products should be deployed by a major hyperscaler—presumably Google—and there is further upside if Nvidia utilizes this technology in future improvement designs. They are also in negotiations with other partners, so it remains to be seen how that business progresses.

Outside of this broader connectivity portfolio, Semtech is also in the process of realigning its product portfolio, and they are in the end stages of divesting this cellular module business. The presenter believes this could likely add a few hundred basis points to gross margin. So as the mix shifts to more of the signal integrity business, you have a pathway to go from a high-50%s gross margin to mid-60%s longer term.

Net-net, while supply constraints remain a key risk for this industry, the presenter sees a pathway for signal integrity to roughly double versus what consensus is currently modeling. The presenter is underwriting $10 of EPS power in a few years as consensus is closer to $6. Even applying a low-20s multiple, which is slightly below their historical average but slightly above broader networking peers, you get to approximately 60% upside from today’s stock price. And if you really dream the dream on the module, on the CopperEdge side, you can easily see the stock doubling. The presenter thinks the downside from here is likely only 25% or 30%. So they think the risk-reward skew is pretty attractive at these levels.

The presenter would like to discuss SBA Communications as a long.

SBA is a communications infrastructure / tower company. It is trading at approximately 14x AFFO per share. It has an $18 billion market cap and a $35 billion EV.

From a risk-reward perspective, what the presenter is talking about as far as its multiple range—if you look at spreads versus the 10-year, it can range anywhere from 13x to 18x; so, investors are pretty optimistic on this company.

The presenter would argue that the aspect to the story that investors are not appreciating is that they are approximately a year away from having an organic growth opportunity that looks very similar to the largest tower peer in the space, American Tower, who has laid out plans for mid-single-digit top-line organic / mid-to-high-single-digits bottom-line growth. The presenter believes that SBAC is an M&A target, specifically from American Tower. The stock was trading at $170; then there were reports that it was in M&A talks and the stock subsequently traded to $210; then press reports indicated the M&A talks were over, so the stock is now trading in the high $170s. The presenter thinks those talks are likely still ongoing in some way, shape, or form.

In summary, the presenter thinks you have an attractive risk/ reward skew here. The upside on a deal is not simply the 20% to 25% you might get from multiple normalization plus positive earnings in 2028, but you also have another 25% to 50% M&A premium that could come in. Also worth noting, it is not involved at all with the AI complex, so you do not need to worry about Nvidia announcing $500 billion of financing and what that means. It should be considered a relatively safe long.

The presenter would like to discuss Reddit as a long.

This stock is extremely controversial. It has enormous, inordinate volatility, in the presenter's opinion. But when the presenter looks at this company, they do not see any other comparable property that has the same dimension of human content.

In terms of the setup, the stock sold off dramatically after they reported earnings on July 30th. The stock went out at $180 the night before; it was trading around $140 the next morning. So what caused the move? Their DAUs went down by approximately 200,000 in the US, while their international user growth was strong. So the fear is that user growth in the US is flattening out.

The other controversy regarding the stock is over their renewal with Google and their licensing agreement, where Google pays approximately $60 million this year, and there is talk that they were asking for $120 million. In terms of the magnitude of what Google and the other AI companies are spending on CAPEX, the renewal amount is insignificant. The presenter thinks that the overhang on the stock surrounding the renewal of the licensing agreement was blown out of proportion. Eventually, the presenter thinks there will be an agreement with Google, followed by OpenAI, and then Anthropic (because they are trying to sue them).

But what you have here is a company with 194 million shares outstanding, a $28 billion EV, that is going to generate $1.5 billion of EBITDA this year, going to $2 billion next year. You are talking 12.5 times enterprise value. There is some stock comp in there that is not insignificant, but this business has no CAPEX. Its revenue is growing 60%. It generate san enormous amount of cash flow. They bought back $250 million worth of stock in the quarter. They generate more content in one month than the entire Wikipedia library. The presenter believes that if you are Google or OpenAI, you are going to want to have access to this content. The controversy is that no one is going to go to Reddit, that they are simply going to go to Reddit via Google, and those subscribers are not as valuable. The presenter does not think that is going to happen, because there is still enormous growth internationally. Their ARPU growth is extraordinary.

The presenter would like to discuss Nebius as a short.

For those not familiar with it, it is a neocloud. What is a neocloud? It depends on who you ask. They are either an NVIDIA GPU reseller, or they are a play on the future of the public cloud, where enterprises are going to be renting out dedicated GPU capacity in the same way that they do from the hyperscalers today. If the market remains significantly compute constrained long-term, these players have a place in the market.

The reason why the presenter thinks it is a short is that Nebius has a $7 to $9 billion ARR target for the end of this year. They have approximately 16 data center sites under contract, but the most critical one for this year is in Vineland, New Jersey. Vineland is going to house a Microsoft contract for them, where they will get approximately $17.4 billion over the next five years. On 300 megawatts at that site, it implies about $11.6 million of ARR per megawatt.

They have delivered 50 megawatts at that site—so 50 of the 300—and they are currently facing community backlash around being able to stand up the incremental 250 by the end of the year. A week ago, there was a city council meeting to vote on whether or not Nebius can stand up the rest of the 250, and it ended in a “no” vote. The next meeting is August 17th. Presumably, there will be another vote then. Even if that occurs, there is a 45-day appeals process, which puts you out to October 1st, if all goes well, to when they can start standing up these 250 megawatts.

The partner at the site is Bloom Energy. Bloom Energy has touted their ability to stand up 55 megawatts in 55 days for Oracle, as one of the fastest deployments they have ever done. If you do the math based on October 1st to the end of the year, it does not get to the 250 that they would need. So at $11.6 million of ARR per megawatt, the presenter believes you have $2.9 billion of that $7 to $9 billion ARR target at risk. Even if they get half of that, it is still a problem for the range, because they are assuming that it is fully stood up in the guide. So where could you be wrong? There has been some speculation that you could get a large deal announcement with Anthropic on the quarter this Wednesday. Candidly, they have two over-one-gigawatt sites that are contracted—not yet built, but contracted—that investors have been speculating that Anthropic could come in and fill. But, in the presenter’s opinion, if you ask anyone how they are modeling this business, no one puts those sites in their model without anyone filling that capacity long-term. So you need to believe that Anthropic is going to sign a meaningfully upsized deal relative to what the current market rate is on a dollars per megawatt basis.

There has also been some speculation that they could sign a deal with Google for one of those full gigawatt sites. Over the weekend, there were some rumors circulating on X that suggested that it would be a $33 billion deal over five years. That is highly problematic when you back into the implied dollars per megawatt (it is approximately $7 million per megawatt). The base is currently run-rating at $10 to $11 million. The Microsoft contract is worth about $11.5 million per megawatt.

So the question is, why would they do that? It is because they know they need to raise over $20 billion plus in debt over the next year that the market likely would rebuke, when you look at what is going on with hyperscaler CDS spreads and the Bitcoin miners. If they were to sign a deal like that, it would signal a lot of desperation. And the presenter does not think this is the type of stock that can work when numbers get cut, especially when there are terminal value concerns.

In terms of price target, the presenter believes that there is 25% downside from current levels based on DCF derived values from future contracted cash flows.

The presenter would like to discuss Match Group as a long.

Everybody knows what the company does. They have Hinge and Tinder. They compete with Bumble. The pitch comes down to the balance sheets and what is changing on the balance sheets. This company has an $8.5 billion market cap, and they have bought back $1 billion of stock in the last six quarters. Their competitor, Bumble, has a $700 million EV, and most of that is debt. And Bumble is really holding on for dear life right now—the stock is currently trading at $2.

The pitch comes down to the fact that the presenter thinks Bumble is going to be gone soon, and when and if that turns out to be true, Match will be a compelling long. It has not been a good long, as it has gone through a series of different CEOs. If you go back over the last 15 years, every three to four years it cycles to a new CEO. The presenter thinks the current CEO is good. He came from Zillow, Spencer Rascoff.

He is fixated on engagement, and you can start to see that in the metrics that are available through third parties. And the real visibility of that is, Bumble is failing. For reference, Match generates $3.5 billion in revenues while Bumble only generates $800 million in revenues, so four-to-one. And then Match outspends Bumble five to one in terms of marketing dollars. The presenter believe sit does not really matter who is on the app six months ago; what matters is who is coming onto the app tomorrow. And Match is outspending Bumble by 5x. You can see the engagement metrics, number of visits, minutes per visit—both of those are declining at Bumble. Whereas at Match and Tinder, they are growing, both those sets of metrics, and that is what the CEO of Match is fixated on.

Match’s growth is approximately 4% or 5%, but that is not the bet that you are making here. The bet is the P/E multiple, which is 12.5x this year and 11x next year, and that Bumble goes away and they start to modestly increase prices (across all their various tiers). For example, you hit this button for gold status, which enables you to download more photos. They have done a tremendous job on these initiatives in the past, which they are not talking about at the moment, because the presenter thinks their likely goal is to make sure Bumble is gone. Once Bumble is gone, then they can start to tweak things on the platform. And if there are only two apps you can download—one is more serious while the other is more casual—you have a lot of flexibility. That is the bet that the presenter is making.

If that happens, the buyback, which they are buying at a higher and higher price point—the presenter gave you the number earlier—they have bought 32 million shares at roughly $33 per share; the stock is at $37. But if you study the prices that they are buying at most recently, most recently in July, they bought it at $40, and the stock just dropped. So they have been active buyers at these levels, and they are retiring a decent amount of stock.

The bet is that pricing starts to lift from 4% to approximately 7% to 8%, and you get some margin accretion because they do not need to spend much on marketing. You should get an increase in the buyback, with EPS growth that looks more like +15%, and they are the only game in town. If that happens, then the presenter thinks the P/E multiple starts to shift, because the EPS right now, right here, it would look like 8x or 9x next year's EPS, in which case they think investors are likely willing to pay 14x to 15x for a company that is growing +8% to +9% with a decent visibility.

The presenter is not telling you it is a phenomenal industry. But what they have seen is, sometimes you get phenomenal stocks in industries that are not doing well, as competitors go away. Bumble is not going away tomorrow, but investors should keep it on their radar. The presenter thinks if they continue getting additional third-party data points that Bumble is about to fold, Match should work from the long side.

The presenter would like to discuss Motorola Solutions as a long.

Motorola Solutions has a $77 billion market cap, an $87 billion EV, and trades approximately $1 billion per day.

Motorola Solutions unifies communications, video, and security technology to protect people, property, and places across public safety and businesses. Approximately two-thirds of their business is used by first responders—such as ambulances, critical infrastructure, and communications within state and local municipalities.

The pitch is that in one-third of their business, revenues are growing approximately 20% to 25% due to recent acquisitions (this is separate from their stable LMR radio business, which is the critical infrastructure segment of their business that is growing low single digits with high margins and a sticky customer base with long-term contracts). The growth segment is in what is called mesh radio networks, which is used for drone technologies.

For example, one of the growth angles to the story that the presenter thinks will get picked up by investors when Anduril Industries eventually goes public, is that this software is essentially on (the presenter estimates) two-thirds of Anduril's devices.

In addition, them anagement team is very conservative. Every quarter they have been guiding up the acquisition of Silvus Technologies that closed approximately a year ago. They have what is called a “self-healing network”, meaning that if one of the local networks goes down, they can incorporate the other devices on the network and essentially be their own local network. That business is growing 25% per year, and every quarter they have guided those numbers higher.

The Street is assuming $21 per share of earnings in 2028. The presenter thinks they can generate $25 per share of earnings, between this deal and this other acquisition called D-Fend Solutions, which is a drone-capture technology, where they can essentially hack any drones that are in an area, and instead of shooting them down, they can essentially take them over and land them safely. That business is also growing mid-20%s at 50% EBITDA margins. That is where their variance comes from versus the Street and where their management is very conservative on these assumptions. They are currently supply constrained on all these products, but they are building facilities and have doubled their sales staff to meet this demand.

In summary, they have a customer base that is very sticky, with long-term contracts and high margins.

The presenter would like to discuss Hut 8 as a long.

For background, the company has announced three contracts, which equate to $1.75 billion of NOI, with a third of it backed by Google and two-thirds backed by Nvidia. If you do a DCF of the lease payments, it is $75, and if you put a cap rate on it, it is $130. For reference, the stock is currently trading at $86.

In terms of the setup, the presenter believes there is a little bit of regulatory uncertainty based on the governor of Texas. And the presenter believes if Texas has problems with data centers, every other single pitch that is tied to data centers today would be trading lower than where they are currently trading.

In the presenter’s opinion, the Batch Zero processes that are funded by the biggest companies in the world, that have debt financing, that are going to be completed by great operators, are going to be approved. Two-thirds of the leases that the presenter mentioned, those that generate the $1.75 billion of NOI, come from the Batch Zero process, from the Corpus Christi asset of Hut 8. It is called the Beacon Point asset.

The presenter thinks that if this issue did not exist, the stock would be $20 or $30 higher. Investors have made a lot of money in it, so you have some investors taking profits. The presenter thinks this is an exceptional risk-reward, where you can deploy real capital and sleep at night knowing that you are going to make money. How much money obviously depends on how great the AI trade plays out from here.

But they have a River Bend facility where they are getting more power from Entergy, and the presenter believes Entergy wants to see some behind-the-meter investment by Hut 8, while Entergy invests to generate some of that power generation. Hut 8, the presenter believes, by the end of this year will announce an expansion of the River Bend project, which should be equal to what they have already announced in River Bend.

You should also get clarity in Texas—after the November election if not beforehand - via press releases, etc. In terms of the analyst community, one sell-side analyst’s price target, which does not give them full value for everything in the pipeline but gives enough value, is $250. The stock is currently trading at $86. The presenter thinks what has been announced, plus River Bend, plus behind the meter, should get them to a $150 price target.

And the presenter feels that the Situational Awareness unwind, the AI selloff, plus this Texas aspect, have put investors in a position where you can buy any Bitcoin miner and feel excited about the setup. You could buy Riot, and if they lease all of Corsicana it is probably worth $30-plus, but they have not really executed on much besides 25 megawatts to AMD. Core Scientific has done a lot of work with CoreWeave, but they have not announced too much, and their execution has been questioned by investors.

The presenter believes that the companies that have repeatedly delivered / executed for institutional investors are Hut 8 and Terawulf. Terawulf has announced contracts worth $17 to $19, and it is trading at $17 to $19 (the presenter believes it is still a good setup). Hut 8 has announced contracts likely worth $120, and they are likely going to announce additional positive updates, and they are viewed as good executors. The presenter feels like Hut 8 is likely the best risk-reward out of the group.

The presenter would like to discuss Amazon.com as a long.

The presenter acknowledges that this is not a controversial call, but the way they are thinking about it currently is, there is still a lot of upside even after this move. The presenter knows it is not up a lot on a year to date basis, but it is up a lot post-CY 2Q earnings. The presenter believes it is worth $400 in the near term (EPS of $18 in 2028 using a 22x multiple, which equates to a $400 target price).

The piece to the story that the presenter is excited about is the piece that they think investors are starting to come around to, which is Bedrock. It is a smaller part of the AWS AI platform. The presenter has always thought frontier model—frontier, frontier, frontier - open source does not matter. The presenter thinks in the last six months to nine months, it has become clearer that, whether it is going to be open source or not, companies are more committed to being multi-model, meaning they want to be able to use Anthropic or OpenAI, or they might also want to bring in Kimi or some of the other open-source models.

So the presenter has been trying to figure out ways to express that view. They think there are a few business models in the private markets to express this view like Baseten, Fireworks, and some of the other inference clouds. In the presenter's view, the best way, at least at their scale, to express the view that companies are going multi-model is through the cloud providers. Particularly, each one of them has a version of this - Bedrock, Foundry, and Vertex—that is for Amazon, Microsoft, and Google respectively. For reference, Bedrock's is much larger.

At the end of the day, you have a line in the Amazon business model and in the Microsoft-Google business model that is tied directly to Anthropic and OpenAI's ARR growth, because some percentage of the tokens accessed for Anthropic and OpenAI are being accessed through Bedrock, Foundry, and Vertex. That has started showing up in terms of revenue growth—it is the CAPEX converting to revenue growth—but also it is showing up in terms of higher EBIT margins, because these token-as-a-service products that are offered through Bedrock come at a marginally higher EBIT margin, which is also good for the business. The presenter does not have a view on Nebius or CoreWeave—but this is their differentiated worldview on Amazon that gets them excited. If you do the rough math on the numbers that are out there—for Anthropic as an example, and this is likely a conservative number that investors are talking about—but if they end the year at $100 billion of ARR and they have two or three gigawatts of compute, that means they are monetizing that compute at $50 billion per gigawatt (you can do it on megawatts, but let us just say $50 billion per gigawatt). The cloud providers are currently charging between ~$10 to $12 billion per gigawatt to rent that compute space, so the presenter estimates the labs are doing 80% to 90% inference margins.

It probably does not stay that high, but to the presenter, that is an exciting thing happening in the market. The end consumers of labs are growing what they are able to monetize at faster than the clouds are scaling their price. The presenter does not know how to conceptualize it, but there is certainly room for the clouds to raise their price, particularly when Anthropic and OpenAI are scooping up every bit of compute. And then there is a spillover into the marginal suppliers of compute, like the Nebiuses and CoreWeaves. The presenter has not thought enough about that yet.

But to the presenter, if your main customer is earning somewhere upwards of 80% margins, there is probably room for that cost to go up. That is another pricing lever on the cloud businesses that gets the presenter excited in terms of their longer-term view. They do think investors have come around to the fact that the CAPEX they are spending is producing faster revenue growth, but there are other levers that are exciting.

The presenter would like to discuss Astera Labs as a long.

The company specializes in designing high-speed connectivity solutions for data centers and AI infrastructure. The whole idea is that if you continue to connect clusters, you need more scale-up switch. And surprisingly, there is no merchant in scale up switch. Right now you have some competitors in the space like Broadcom, but the presenter thinks that a lot of these customers buying other XPUs do not want to be beholden to Broadcom, where traditionally they were not a great supplier to many of these customers.

The punch line is that they track Trainium units, which Andy Jassy implied is going much higher, and the presenter thinks the attach there is favorable. It is a name that historically has a lot of fear around the sustainability of growth. The presenter thinks if they can grow above mid-teens in EPS next year, and possibly above $30 to $35 in 2028, it is a stock that should re-rate as it comes more into the public view, outside of being what is viewed as a niche semiconductor coverage name at the moment.

The presenter would like to discuss Jeol Ltd. as a long.

The presenter likens Jeol to the ASML of optical. The presenter would also argue that it is cheap on an absolute and relative basis, and that the company is not well followed by investors.

The presenter believes it is a high-quality company. Their long-term operating margins are somewhat in the 40% range for their industrial segment, which is the segment the presenter cares about. They also have a really deep R&D moat, so they are not an over-earning commodity type business or anything like that.

For reference, the ticker is 6951 JP. It is a Japanese company. They have roughly a $2.5 billion market cap. Just for context, in terms of the stock and the fundamentals, they have been roughly steady—not explosive growth or anything like that—in the past few years. This is in part because their core businesses are more so tied to tools that make EUV masks. They are more levered to SKU count as opposed to volumes. It could be analogous to EDA, so that is why the business has been somewhat steady.

But the hidden gem and the crux of the thesis is that they have a front-end tool that every optical company—like Lumentum, Coherent, & Dongshan—needs to create indium phosphide and also CW (ultra-high-power lasers). From all their checks, it is clear that companies are increasing CAPEX and trying to expand capacity (the presenter believes approximately greater than 5x for this indium phosphide over the next five years). The question is, how do you play this theme through picks and shovels? This is one way you can do it. The market, it seems like they have already discovered the Lam of optical, which the presenter would argue is Aixtron in Germany, which trades at a hefty multiple (30x calendar 2027 EPS). But the market is missing the opportunity to invest in JEOL, which the presenter believes is the ASML of optical, and only trades at a mid-teens multiple on calendar 2027 EPS. The presenter believes that practically no optical revenue is baked into Street assumptions / numbers.

So the part that the presenter really cares about for JEOL is the spot e-beam tool. What that does is, it uses super precise electron beams to physically carve the gradients on the indium phosphide lasers. For reference, tool demand scales with how many lasers you want to create. This is exactly what benefits companies like Coherent and others.

The presenter would note, in this market for spot e-beam tools, this company has greater than 50% share. And then from the presenter's bottoms-up work with indium phosphide, it seems like the market will need greater than 300 tools over the next few years (call it $3 million per for these tools). So all in, this might add 10% to 20% top-line growth on top of what the Street has assumed, simply from this segment alone, which is the segment that the presenter cares about.

Again, the Street is assuming very minimal growth for this company overall, call it low-single-digit, mid-single-digit percent growth. The presenter thinks it could be 10% to 15% above that, just from the spot e-beam. Based on a fair multiple—25x calendar 2027—and using the presenter's numbers, the stock should be a double from here. The hidden gem is the spot e-beam. They literally help you create more indium phosphide. They are a toolmaker that can participate in that.

ideas.2026-07-31-myst-miko-tam-myst-consumer-i:
Yesway, Inc. [YSWY]

“Cult” Burrito Franchise with Rural Convenience Store Density Advantage

• YSWY is the 15th largest Convenience Store [C-Store] Operator in the US with ~420 Units across 7 States, concentrated in the rural Southwest.

• Presenter describes YSWY as a “Broken IPO” despite a “Rural Moat” that makes the company the “ONLY Option” for Food and Fuel in many Markets, driving Customer Loyalty and Pricing Power.  He explains that ~70% of the Footprint sits in towns with LESS THAN 20K people, and the Average Store faces FEWER than 4 Rival C-Stores within 5 miles vs. 10 – 15 for Larger Chains in more populated Markets.

• The “Inside-Store” business is the primary “Growth Engine,” contributing ~60% of Gross Profit on “Consistent DD%” Same-Store Sales Growth, with Mix shifting toward HIGHER-margin Food & Beverage.  YSWY is known for its Deep-Fried Burrito, a “Cult Following” favorite among Customers that comprises ~60% of ALL Food Sales.  Promotions are priced to undercut local Quick Service Restaurants [QSRs] (i.e., 2 Burritos + Drink for ~$7), a strategy tailored to YSWY’s Lower-income Customer base.  Additionally, most Stores run “Lean” with just 2 – 3 Employees per Shift vs. 5+ for Competitors.

• Presenter sees a path to grow Units organically from 420 to OVER 500 by 2030.  New Builds measure 1/5th the size of Buc-ee’s [Private] and “Ramp” in under 6 months, delivering 3x the Fuel Gallons and 2x the Inside Sales of Legacy stores.  On the “Fuel Debate,” Presenter is deliberately conservative: Margins ran $0.49/gallon last quarter versus a historical Low-$0.40’s range, and although a 35%+ Diesel Mix and Rural Pricing Power argue for structurally HIGHER Margins, he models a reversion to $0.40.

• At ~10x FY27 Street EBITDA, YSWY trades at a meaningful DISCOUNT to Peers in the 12x – 19x EBITDA Range.  Applying just 12x to his “Conservative” FY27 EBITDA Estimate, Presenter arrives at a Price Target of $30/share (~43% Upside), with each Incremental Multiple “Turn” worth $4 – $5/share.  Lastly, he views YSWY as a Potential Acquisition Target for Larger Competitors seeking access to their Footprint.

• RISK: IPO Lockup Expiry in October.

Warby Parker Inc. [WRBY]

Eyewear Rebounding from “Cyclical Trough” + “Game Changing” AI Glasses Launch

• WRBY is a lifestyle brand that offers Vision Correction solutions from Prescription Glasses and Contacts to Eye Exams and Vision Tests through Warby Parker Retail Stores and its E-commerce platform.

• Presenter first discussed WRBY at MYST’s 12/19/25 Consumer Idea Forum when the Warby Parker / Google [GOOGL] / Samsung Electronics [005930.KS] AI Smart Glasses Launch was nearly 1 year away and that Catalyst is now just ~2 months out.  Additionally, WRBY’s Base Business is benefiting from POSITIVE Cyclical Tailwinds fueled in part by Consumer Stimulus in the company’s Core Demographic.

• Presenter notes WRBY currently operates just ~300 Stores in the US against ambitions to reach 900, implying at Full Plan the business would represent “Just a Fraction” of the ~45K US Optical Retailers (~$68B US / ~$150B Global TAM).  2026 will also be the Industry’s FIRST “Normal” Year since the “COVID Boom / Bust” period, which was then followed by Liberation Day disruptions.  Tax Benefit Tailwinds from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act [OBBBA] add further support, with the majority falling on the $75K – $250K Household Consumer, WRBY’s Core Demographic.  The company posted +8% Revenue Growth in 1Q26 (Pre-Smart Glasses), and Presenter believes trends have ACCELERATED.

• Beyond the general Eyewear recovery, WRBY has spent the last ~2 years ramping its Optometrist Program and ~87% of Stores now have an Optometrist on site.  Presenter explains that ~80% of Eyewear Purchases are made during the Optometry Appointment.  Optometrist Utilization has IMPROVED significantly through 2026  as WRBY’s Insurance Program scales.  Notably, ~60% of Customers carry Eye Insurance, but Insurance-driven Sales still comprise just “MSD%’s” of Total Sales.

• Presenter values the Standalone Base Business at $36/share (~35% Upside) but continues to view AI Glasses as a “Game Changer.”  She anticipates a “Step Change” in Eyewear akin to the leap in Capabilities from the Apple [AAPL] iPhone vs. the old Nokia [NOK] “Candy Bar” phone in the early 2000s.  Most new Eyewear will carry Smart Functionality, which she expects to “Dramatically INCREASE” WRBY’s AUR and Sales/sq. ft., while simultaneously providing a “Halo Effect” on the Base business.

• Meta Platforms’ [META] Marketing Spend should drive Category Awareness for Smart Glasses, while recent Samsung Demonstrations have shown SUPERIOR Functionality with LONGER Battery Life vs. META’s AI Glasses.  WRBY’s product will also be able to capitalize on GOOGL’s Ecosystem (Gmail, Google Maps, Google Classroom, etc.) and integrate seamlessly with Gemini.  Presenter arrives at a Price Target of $60/share (~125% Upside) based on her FY28 EBITDA and discounting back.

• UPDATE: WRBY reported “Mixed” 2Q26 Results on August 6th: Net Revenue of $235.5M vs. $238M Consensus and Adj. EBITDA of $32.9M vs. $28.9M.  Mgmt. reaffirmed FY26 Sales / Adj. EBITDA Guidance of $959M – $976M / $117M – $119M, both BELOW Consensus of $980M / $121M, respectively.  Shares closed ~8% LOWER on the day.

Somnigroup International Inc. [SGI]

Mattress “Monopoly” Consolidating Share amid Peer Bankruptcy Filings

• SGI develops, produces, and markets Mattresses, Adjustable bases, Pillows, and other Sleep & Relaxation products under the Tempur-Pedic, Sealy, Stearns & Foster, and Sleepy's brands.

• Presenter describes SGI as a Mattress and Bedding “Monopoly” consolidating the Industry at the “Demand Trough,” positioning the company to “Compound” even IF the Market never recovers, while offering Investors a “Call Option” on any future Earnings Growth.  Additionally, SGI’s Vertical Integration enables End-to-End control of the Supply Chain, enabling the company to capture MORE Margin Dollars per unit.

• The Competitive Environment is becoming MORE favorable as every meaningful Competitor has either filed for Bankruptcy or is “On the Cusp” of doing so: 1) Sleep Number [SNBR] has filed Chapter 11; 2) Purple Innovation [PRPL] still does NOT generate positive EBITDA; and 3) Serta Simmons Bedding [Private] is distressed enough that Presenter ultimately expects a “Chapter 22” (i.e., Second Chapter 11 Filing).  As Peers continue to struggle, they will “Donate Share” to SGI, bolstering both Sales AND Margins.  Lastly, Unit Demand is running ~30% BELOW 2019 levels and given a 7–8-year Replacement Cycle, Presenter believes it is “Pretty Reasonable” to assume Demand is AT or NEAR the Bottom.

• Deal Synergies from SGI’s February 2025 Mattress Firm acquisition have been raised from $100M to $235M, and the pending Leggett & Platt [LEG] Acquisition will extend SGI’s Vertical Integration “Upstream” into Components.  Presenter also highlights Mgmt.’s Alignment, noting CEO Scott Thompson is among the stock’s largest Shareholders.

• Mgmt. previously published an FY28 EPS Target of $5.15, but after incorporating LEG and tempering some of Mgmt.’s Industry Assumptions, Presenter models $6.00 (vs. $4.75 Consensus).  In the near-term, Presenter sees SGI transitioning to a “Free Cash Flow Machine” that could begin buying back stock as early as 2H26.  Applying an 18x P/E Multiple, he arrives at a Price Target of $110/share (~68% Upside).

• UPDATE: On August 6th, SGI reported slightly weaker 2Q26 Results (Net Sales of $1.82B vs. $1.88B Consensus and Adj. EBITDA of $296.5M vs. $299.4M ) and Mgmt. reduced FY26 Adj. EPS Guidance to $2.85 – $3.15 from $3.00 – $3.40.  Shares closed ~7% LOWER on the day.

Hermes International [RMS.FP]

“Perma-Short” Forced to Confront “Prolonged Deceleration” OR “Painful” Supply Cuts

• RMS.FP designs, manufactures, and sells luxury Leather Goods, Ready-to-Wear, Silk, Jewelry, and other Lifestyle Products under the Hermès brand, with Handbags the primary Growth and Margin driver.

• Presenter argues RMS’ “Unicorn” Multiple (~35x FY26 EPS) prices in “Double-digit%” EBIT Growth into the next “Decade and Beyond,” a Premium he views as UNSUSTAINABLE.  The company’s Growth is almost entirely driven by the Leather Goods business, where $15K – $20K Handbags anchor Demand on the “Perception” of a ~2x Resale Value on the Secondary Market, a figure Presenter emphasizes is essentially “Untrackable.”

• His central Bear Argument hinges on the idea that, unlike most Industries, “Luxury Does NOT Benefit from Scale,” yet RMS is now >10x LARGER vs. ~2 Decades ago, and the product has become “Ubiquitous.”  Notably, Auction Data and Wait Times reveal that Secondary Market Resale Prices are DECLINING, undercutting the “Scarcity Premium” embedded in current Valuation.

• Furthermore, Presenter notes that Mgmt. recently “Walked Back” their “6% Volume, 5% Price” Growth Algo, which historically fueled the company’s “Double-digit%” EBIT Growth.  Under this framework, he sees 2 paths forward – a “Prolonged Deceleration” OR an “Abrupt” Supply Reduction – either of which risks a material “EPS Cut.”

• Lastly, Presenter refers to RMS as a “Perma Short” on the Terminal Value until the Multiple resets to a more “Reasonable” level, rather than a Near-term Trade on a potential EPS Miss, since Mgmt. retains tight control over Supply and is unlikely to “Blow Up” in any single quarter.  Applying a ~25x Multiple to his FY27 EPS Estimate of ~€50.00 (vs. €50.92 Consensus), Presenter arrives at a Price Target of €1,250/share (~18% Downside).

Ferrari N.V. [RACE.IM]

F80 Hypercar Fueling Growth Inflection while Secondary Market Values “Go Parabolic”

• RACE.IM designs, manufactures and sells Luxury Performance Sports Cars, as well as providing Spare Parts & Engines and Repair, Maintenance & Restoration services.

• Presenter describes RACE as a “Pure Play” on ACCELERATING High-Income Discretionary Spending, arguing record Capital Markets activity is minting a NEW cohort of High Net Worth [HNW] and Ultra-high Net Worth [UHNW] Individuals whose spending is concentrating on a “Narrower” set of categories.

• He explains that Travel demand remains robust, per recent results from Viking [VIK], Hilton Worldwide [HLT], and Marriott International [MAR], while demand for “Hard Luxury” (e.g., Richemont [CFR.SW]) holds firm and “Soft Luxury” (e.g., Hermès International [RMS.FP]) struggles.  Notably, he characterizes RACE’s Multi-year Underperformance vs. Luxury Peers as “Indiscriminate” rather than Company-specific, leaving the stock at a “Trough” Absolute and Relative Multiple, just as Top-line Growth is set to RE-accelerate.

• Presenter points to RACE’s new F80 Hybrid Hypercar as the Growth Catalyst, citing a ~€3.5M Base Sticker Price before Aftermarket “Personalization.”  He expects ramping F80 Shipments to fuel Organic Revenue Growth from current “MSD%’s” toward “LDD%’s” beginning in 3Q26 and continuing through most of FY27, powered by a “Richer” Product Mix and HIGH-margin “Personalization” Revenue.

• Additionally, Presenter addresses 2 legs of the Bear Case:

o    Growth Algo Reset – During RACE’s FY25 Capital Markets Day, Mgmt. reduced their Long-term Growth Outlook from ~10% to ~5% amid softening Secondary Market Values and uncertainty around the company’s nascent Electric Vehicle [EV] program.  However, RACE has EXCEEDED Guidance every quarter since, with “Double-digit%” Growth expected to resume in 3Q26.

o    Brand Equity – Residual Values, which have been pressured across the company’s Hybrid lineup, have finally found a “Floor,” while Secondary Market Values for RACE’s HIGHER-tier, more “Brand-representative” models have gone “Absolutely Parabolic” this year.  Presenter interprets this as evidence that Brand Equity is “As Strong As It’s EVER Been,” even following the company’s “Unsuccessful” EV launch.

• Applying a ~37.5x Multiple to his FY28 EPS Estimate of ~€13.00 (vs. €11.82 Consensus), Presenter arrives at a Price Target of €485/share (~43% Upside) and sees the Setup paying off through both POSITIVE Earnings Revisions and Multiple Expansion.

Owens Corning [OC]

Trading BELOW Sum-of-the-Parts Value Following Rejected Carlisle [CSL] Bid

• OC provides Residential and Commercial Building Products in the US, Europe, the Asia Pacific, and Internationally, operating through 3 segments: 1) Roofing; 2) Insulation; and 3) Doors.

• Presenter frames OC as an “Interesting Target” in an ACCELERATING Building Products Consolidation Cycle given the company’s strong Competitive Position in Residential Roofing alongside Insulation and Doors.  In June 2026, the Wall Street Journal reported that Carlisle Companies [CSL] made “Several Unsolicited Attempts” to acquire OC in the months prior.  The stock rallied ~20% on the news but has since “Round-Tripped,” trading near levels seen PRIOR to the Takeover Report.  CSL has subsequently reported Earnings and declined to comment on any potential transaction.

• Presenter views this situation as part of a broader Industry “Roll-Up” vs. a “One-Off Bid,” emphasizing QXO [QXO] has been acquiring businesses in MULTIPLE areas of the Building Products ecosystem.  Critically, QXO’s strategy of concentrating its own tier of the Value Chain provides justification for “Defensive Consolidation” among vendors like OC and CSL to maintain negotiating leverage with Customers.  As such, Presenter believes OC will ultimately be acquired either entirely or in “Pieces” and sees “Massive” potential Synergies from combining with other Vendors.

• Additionally, he contends that ongoing Industry Consolidation structurally IMPROVES Long-term Profitability and justifies a HIGHER Multiple for what were historically Cyclical Earnings streams.  Presenter’s Sum-of-the-Parts Analysis yields a Price Target of $180/share (~30% Upside) on a Standalone Basis and believes the Strategic Interest from CSL creates a “Floor” for the stock.  Lastly, he explains the business is mostly exposed to Repair & Maintenance rather than New Construction, LIMITING Sensitivity to Fed Rate Policy and Housing cycles.

• UPDATE: OC reported better-than-expected 2Q26 Results on August 5th: Net Sales of $2.76B vs. $2.66B Consensus and Adj. EPS of $3.93 vs. $3.09.  Mgmt. guided 3Q26 Net Sales to $2.6B – $2.7B, bracketing Consensus of $2.68B.  Shares closed ~5% HIGHER on the day.

Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd. [NCLH]

“Sandbagged” Guidance Masking “Real” Turnaround Progress

• NCLH operates a fleet of Passenger Cruise Ships offering an array of Cruise Itineraries and Theme Cruises in North America, Europe, the Asia-Pacific, and Internationally.

• Presenter frames NCLH as a “Total Disaster” amid an otherwise “Healthy” Cruise Market.  As a result of Elliott Investment Mgmt.’s Activist Campaign, the company has replaced its CEO, CFO, most of Senior Mgmt., and the majority of the Board.  The New Team has “Reset” Guidance, which Presenter views as “Exceptionally Conservative” relative to the operational steps Mgmt. has “Quite Effectively” laid out.

• He acknowledges NCLH will require a Multi-year Turnaround effort rather than a “Quick Fix,” yet Mgmt. has accordingly “Written Off” 2H26 and 1H27, guiding to a resumption of Growth in 2H27 with FY28 the first potential “Breakout Year.”  Presenter also views NCLH as a Strategic Asset, explaining MSC Cruises [Private] has made several failed attempts over the past decade trying to scale in the North American and Caribbean Markets.  He contends that MSC will ultimately have to “Buy Their Way In”, with NCLH representing the BEST solution.

• While Presenter is NOT “Betting on a Takeover,” NCLH’s significant “Strategic Optionality” combined with Elliott’s continued involvement and a highly incentivized Mgmt. Team offers Investors MULTIPLE ways to win.  Based on his forward Estimates, NCLH trades at a Discount to ALL Peers.  Assuming a “Re-Rating” toward the company’s LOWEST-Multiple Peer (i.e., Carnival [CCL]) as the Turnaround progresses, Presenter arrives at a Price Target of $28/share (~51% Upside).

MGM Resorts International [MGM]

Osaka Casino Opportunity Potentially Worth ENTIRE Current Market Cap

• MGM operates as a Gaming & Entertainment company in the US, China, and Internationally through 4 segments: 1) Las Vegas Strip Resorts; 2) Regional Operations; 3) MGM China; and 4) MGM Digital.

• While the MGM Story is “Complicated,” Presenter’s Thesis is simple by comparison: The company’s upcoming MGM Osaka property remains “Overlooked” by the Street despite ranking as the FIRST and ONLY licensed Casino in Japan with potential to drive meaningful upside for the stock.  During the 2Q26 Earnings call on July 29th, 2026, Mgmt. confirmed Osaka remains on track and on budget for its scheduled Fall 2030 Opening.

• The property is expected to generate ~$2B of Operating Income in ~5 years, with ~$880M attributable to MGM based on the company’s 44% Ownership of the Project.  Presenter applies a 10x Multiple to this figure to arrive at an ~$8.8B Valuation for MGM Osaka alone, representing a significant portion of MGM’s current Market Cap.

• People Incorporated [IAC] owns a 26.7% stake in MGM and has bid $48.30/share for the remaining stock it does NOT already own, ultimately seeking just over 50% of the Post-deal Equity.  Presenter characterizes the approach as unusually “Soft,” noting IAC has conditioned itself on Board Acceptance rather than “Going Hostile.”  However, he feels the Bid Price reflects an attempt by Barry Diller to “Steal” the company and expects the MGM Board and Shareholders to REFUSE the deal.  Notably, several months prior to the bid, the Board valued MGM at $60/share EXCLUDING Osaka, reinforcing his view that the stock offers considerable Upside with Minimal Downside at current levels.

Krispy Kreme, Inc. [DNUT]

“GLP-1 Loser” Narrative Ignores Substantial “Big-Box” Throughput Opportunity

• DNUT operates a Global Doughnut and Sweet-treats platform through Owned / Franchised Doughnut Shops, Delivered Fresh Daily Points of Access, and E-commerce channels in the US, Canada, Mexico, Europe, and Japan.

• Previously negative on DNUT, Presenter has since “Flipped Long” for the FIRST time, referring to the story as an “Under-the-Radar Turnaround” that is ~1/3rd Complete.  He believes the Market has largely “Forgotten” DNUT, writing the company off as a “GLP-1 Loser” burdened by elevated Leverage and an overhang from JAB Holding’s [Private] ~43% stake.

• Historically, DNUT had been “Logistics HEAVY,” distributing Doughnuts via an Owned Trucking Fleet and a steep McDonald’s [MCD] Supply Agreement.  However, the Fleet was replaced by Contracted Trucking in April, driving   LOWER Insurance Costs and ENHANCED Service Rates, and while costly to exit, the MCD Agreement was terminated in July.

• The company is now refranchising Internationally-owned Geographies, shifting from Capital-Employed to a Capital-LIGHT Model.  Franchisee-generated System Sales rose from ~25% at YE25 to ~42% following 1Q26 refranchising in Japan, progressing toward Mgmt.’s Goal of >50% entering FY27.  DNUT’s Network Infrastructure is only ~25% utilized, but Presenter anticipates 100+ Shop Openings this year, nearly all via Franchisees, while large Customers such as Walmart / Sam’s Club [WMT], Target [TGT], and Costco [COST] remain “Lightly Penetrated.”  As DNUT scales and resumes Marketing Spend, he expects “MEANINGFUL Deleveraging” through Operating Leverage, Cost Discipline, and a MORE Franchised, Cash-generative Business Model.

• The company’s Leverage Profile is already IMPROVING, with Net Debt/EBITDA falling from ~6.7x at YE25, to ~5.5x exiting 1Q26, and guided toward ~5.0x by YE26.  Revenue peaked at ~$1.69B in 2023, declined to ~$1.52B in 2025, and should drop further to ~$1.35B in 2026 as Owned-store Sales convert to Royalties and MCD-related Revenue “Rolls Off,” before returning to Growth in 2027.  Similarly, EBITDA peaked in 2023 at ~$212M (~12.5% Margin) but should rebound in 2027 to ~$147M at ~10.7% Margins, still “Depressed” by Company-owned Stores, which Presenter views as the core source of Upside as DNUT refranchises.

• The stock currently trades at ~9.3x FY27 Consensus EBITDA, and Presenter models a ~8% EBITDA CAGR to $185M by 2030 as FCF Conversion RISES from ~10% (2026 Guidance) to ~30% (2029 – 2030).  As Debt approaches ~$700M (vs. ~$890M currently) and the Revenue Mix shifts toward Franchise Royalties, he sees DNUT’s Multiple EXPANDING to ~11x, implying a Fair Value of ~$8.20/share in 2030, or Price Target of $5.00/share (~57% Upside) after discounting back 3 years at 15%.  However, given the Model’s transition toward Royalties, applying a “More Appropriate” 10% Rate yields a Price Target of $6.00/share (~89% Upside).

• Finally, Presenter flags strong Insider Alignment, emphasizing that Bernardo Hees (Founder / Partner at 3G Capital, Former CEO of Burger King [QSR]) joined DNUT’s Board in June 2025 and purchased ~$2.9M worth of stock in May 2026.  Per Mgmt., Hees sees significant untapped potential in the DNUT Brand and supports the Franchise model.

• PRESENTER UPDATE: “Mgmt. did a good job on the 2Q26 Print (August 6th).  Revenues of $331M beat Consensus of $303M and Mgmt. reaffirmed the FY26 Outlook.  The company has lapped the softest potential quarter (i.e., Fewer people eat Doughnuts in the Summer) and 3Q / 4Q create opportunities for ‘Seasonal Doughnuts’ (e.g., Cider, etc.) that generally help drive Comps.  I am optimistic about what they can do in 3Q and 4Q.”

DoorDash, Inc. [DASH]

DashPass “Loyalty Moat” Driving Durable Share Gains + Several “Call Options”

• DASH provides Restaurant Food Delivery services connecting Customers with Merchants through an On-demand Food Delivery application.

• Presenter explains that DASH shares are down ~10% YTD partly due to an “Investment Cycle Overhang.”  However, he contends Consensus Incremental Margin Forecasts are “TOO LOW,” emphasizing that Margins are set to INFLECT in 2027 as Investments “Roll Off” and the company’s International and Grocery businesses reach Profitability.  He acknowledges that softer Order Growth driven by HIGHER Average Order Values [AOVs] within Grocery has drawn some “Bear Nitpicking,” yet notes this segment continues to grow FASTER than Core US Restaurant Delivery, while 3P Data reveals Bookings are tracking WELL AHEAD of the Street.

• Furthermore, Presenter highlights DashPass Penetration as evidence that DASH’s Share Gains are “Durable,” emphasizing that ~80% of Bookings are now generated by DashPass members (vs. ~65% for Uber One [UBER]).  While ~22% of Uber One members also subscribe to DashPass, only ~3% of DashPass members are Uber One subscribers, despite UBER offering BOTH Mobility and Delivery.  He attributes this to a straightforward “Consumer Preference” for DASH, which continues to take Share from UBER domestically, while Grubhub [Private] remains an “Immaterial” Long-term Share Donor to the Industry.

• Lastly, Presenter underscores 2 “Underappreciated Long-term Call Options”:

o    POS [Point-of-Sale] Device – Already “Live” in several US Cities with an expected 2027 Launch, this new product represents a potential Competitive Threat to Toast, Inc. [TOST]; and

o    Robotics Initiative – DASH recently announced DoorDash Air in partnership with Wing [GOOGL], Flytrex [Private], and Manna [Private] after receiving FAA Certification to operate its own Drone Delivery service.  This, along with the company’s existing Dot Delivery Robot, should materially LOWER Delivery Costs and structurally INCREASE Take Rates from 2028 onward.

• Applying a ~22x Multiple to his FY27 EBITDA Estimate of $5.4B (~14% ABOVE the Street’s $4.73B), Presenter arrives at a Price Target of $275/share (~40% Upside).

• UPDATE: DASH reported solid 2Q26 Results on August 5th: Revenue of $4.45B vs. $4.34B Consensus and Adj. EBITDA of $914M vs. $843M, while 3Q26 Marketplace GOV Guidance of $33B – $34B bracketed the Street’s $33.5B Estimate.  The stock closed ~3% HIGHER on the day.

The Vita Coco Company, Inc. [COCO]

Rising Competition Threatens Coconut Water “Fad”

• COCO produces, markets and distributes Coconut Water and other plant-based beverages, primarily through its Vita Coco brand alongside Runa, Ever & Ever and PWR LIFT with Sales split ~80% Branded vs. ~20% Private Label.

• Presenter expects COCO shares to “De-Rate” as the Coconut Water Trend SLOWS and Growth / Margins compress.  Coconut Water carries over 3x the Electrolytes of Sports Drinks and is healthier than Soda, but it is “Having a Moment” in 2026, benefiting from viral TikTok memes and a hit “Coconut Water” song by rapper Trim.

• Presenter’s Short Thesis is focused on RISING Competition:

o    COCO holds ~50% US Category Share but does NOT own its means of Production – an “Asset-light” Model he likens to BellRing Brands [BRBR] in Protein, where Competitive Intensity continues to pressure Growth.

o    Presenter is SKEPTICAL of Mgmt.’s assertion that COCO can “Double” Household Penetration from ~20% over the next few years, citing Energy Drink penetration at ~40% and Orange Juice at ~80%.  Buying Trends also show clear Seasonality (skewing higher in Summer months), while Coconut Water remains an “Acquired Taste” that “Caps” penetration, with some Critics describing the flavor as “Dirty Socks.”

o    Notably, ACV Distribution is now FULLY penetrated outside of Convenience Stores, leaving Growth reliant on Comps and Pricing as Competition INTENSIFIES.  Danone [BN.FP] owns #2 player Harmless Harvest, Celebrity-backed Coco5 has emerged, and Cactus-based Cali Water has gained a foothold within Walmart [WMT].

o    With ~98% of Sales concentrated in Coconut Water itself, Product Extensions will NOT “Carry the Day,” and COCO faces a tough 4Q26 comp against November 2025’s WMT “Planogram Reset,” which shifted the Category to higher-traffic Shelf Space resulting in “Outsized” Growth.

• Furthermore, the largest Strategics have favored “Build Over Buy,” LIMITING the odds of M&A Optionality:

o    Coca-Cola [KO] owned ZICO from 2009 – 2021, but divested it to PE as an underperforming, Non-core asset;

o    PepsiCo [PEP] was a rumored bidder for COCO in 2017 for <$1B and was rebuffed but now distributes O.N.E;

o    Keurig Dr Pepper [KDP] exited its Minority Stake in COCO in 1Q25.

• Presenter sees a Setup that will test Demand Elasticity following 2 Price Increases last year.  COCO faces Margin Pressure from RISING Container Freight Rates (~6% of Sales), as Coconuts are processed in SE Asia against Total Transportation Costs of ~15%.  A “Put Option” on a Super El Nino across Coconut-growing regions (Philippines, Brazil, Thailand, Vietnam) could weigh on Yields, Coconut Prices, and Gross Margins.  Combined, he estimates 200bps – 400bps of COGS Headwind against a business targeting “High-teens%” EBITDA Margins.

• Lastly, Presenter references Celsius Holdings’ [CELH] acquisition of Alani Nu at ~3.2x EV/Sales, mirroring COCO’s current Valuation on FY28 Consensus Estimates.  His Price Target of $42/share (~36% Downside) is split evenly between lower Cash Flow Estimates and Multiple Compression toward ~14x EBITDA, against ~25% Upside Risk.  He concludes flagging HEAVY Insider Selling by MULTPLE Executives this Summer and the $220M+ Copra acquisition, which could accelerate “Headline Growth” and temporarily mask the expected deceleration.

Celsius Holdings, Inc. [CELH]

Scanner Data to Inflect Following “Temporary” SKU Reset

• CELH develops, processes, manufactures, markets, sells, and distributes functional Energy Drinks and Nutrition & Wellness products in the US and Internationally under the CELSIUS, Alani Nu, and Rockstar brand names.

• Presenter explains that CELH has quickly become the #3 Player behind Red Bull [Private] and Monster Beverage [MNST], serving as PepsiCo’s [PEP] “Category Captain” in Energy Drinks, a role analogous to MNST’s with Coca-Cola [KO].  His Thesis rests on Secular Category Trends that remain “As Strong As Ever” – Energy is growing “HSD% – LDD%’s” and continues to take Shelf Space from Beer, Juice, and other categories.  Additionally, Red Bull recently took a “HSD%” Price Increase, paving the way for both MNST and CELH to follow on Pricing through 2027.

• Shares have underperformed materially as the company has NOT “Rationalized” SKUs in recent years amid distractions from rapid PEP Distribution Expansion and recent acquisitions of Alani Nu and Rockstar.  However, CELH is now discontinuing or deprioritizing ~24% of SKUs, distorting Scanner Data, and driving headline Nielsen figures “Down LSD%’s” in 2Q26.  This decline has been compounded by delayed Shelf and Cooler Expansion at large partners (now mostly “Fixed” and ramping in 2H26) and separate PEP Convenience-store stocking issues, alongside “Noise” related to Amazon’s [AMZN] Prime Day shift.  Importantly, Presenter emphasizes that remaining SKUs are growing at a “Healthy HSD% – LDD%” pace and maintaining Category Share.

• Furthermore, he dismisses “Bear Narratives” around Competition from Costco Wholesale’s [COST] Kirkland Energy Launch and Cannibalization from Alani Nu as “NOT Meaningful.”  He views Kirkland Energy as a means for COST to grow within the Category RATHER THAN take Share from CELH and refers to potential Alani Nu Cannibalization as a “Normal Part of Portfolio Rebalancing.”  Lastly, Presenter believes MNST’s and Red Bull’s Sugar-free Growth is largely the result of EXISTING Customer Conversion, as opposed to Share Gains vs. CELH.

• He expects Scanner trends to IMPROVE through the balance of the year as the company laps its “SKU Reset” and Shelf Expansion ramps.  CELH shares currently trade at a ~9% Free Cash Flow Yield and ~13x Presenter’s FY27 EPS Estimate of $2.20 (vs. $1.97 Consensus), a significant DISCOUNT to MNST at ~36x and KO at ~25x.  Applying a “Conservative” ~20x Multiple to his FY27 EPS Estimate, he arrives at a Price Target of $50/share (~71% Upside), with further Upside potential from Multiple Expansion IF Growth begins to outpace MNST.

• UPDATE: CELH reported weaker 2Q26 Results on August 6th: Revenue of $818M vs. $873M Consensus, Adj. EBITDA of $184M vs. $198M and Adj. EPS of $0.36 vs. $0.41.  Mgmt. expects 3Q26 trends for the Celsius Brand to mirror current results and sees Growth resuming in 2027.  Shares fell ~18% on the Print but REBOUNDED ~17% the next day on reports that Rockstar Founder Russ Savage built a 4.7% stake and is vying to take over as CEO.

Brightstar Lottery PLC [BRSL]

Free Cash Flow “Gusher” Nearing End of Fee Payment / Hardware Upgrade Cycle

• BRSL, formerly known as International Game Technology [Old Ticker: IGT], provides a portfolio of Lottery solutions including Lottery Mgmt. services and Instant Lottery systems worldwide.

• Presenter’s Thesis is built on BRSL’s “Cyclical Cash Flow Cycle,” driven by large, periodic Lottery Contract Payments.  The company made one such payment in April, with a second, smaller payment tied to a Lottery Scratch-game Contract due late in FY28.  Between these payments, he expects a “Multi-year Cash Machine” Stretch of roughly 7 years, with Free Cash Flow shifting from NEGATIVE to $2 – $3/share alongside a Dividend Yield approaching ~10%.

• Presenter argues Generalist Investors and “Quant Screens” MISREAD this Cyclicality, flagging risk of a potential Dividend Cut whenever Cash Flow turns temporarily negative around a Contract Payment.  He expects BRSL to “Clear” these screens as Cash Flow reverts to a “Gusher,” beginning with 2Q26 Earnings (8/4/26 BMO) and accelerating into 3Q26.

• Presenter sees shares “Re-Rating” toward ~$30/share (~200% Upside) as Free Cash Flow ramps to $2 – $3/share, implying a ~12x Multiple at the Mid-point.  Lastly, he flags Mega Millions and Powerball as a “Swing Factor” on Quarterly Results, noting both Jackpots crossed ~$700M simultaneously in July, positioning 3Q26 for a “Likely Beat.”

• UPDATE: BRSL reported strong 2Q26 Results on August 4th: Adj. EBITDA of $286M vs. $267.5M Consensus and Adj. EPS of $0.11 vs. $0.05.  Mgmt. reaffirmed the company’s FY26 Profitability and Cash Flow outlook, and shares rose ~12% on the day.

D’Alba Global Co., Ltd. [483650.KS]

ULTA + COST Distribution Wins Signal K-Beauty Share Gain Acceleration

• D’Alba Global manufactures and sells Cosmetic products in South Korea, including Sprays, Essences, Toners, Ampoules, Sunscreens, Facial Masks, and other products.

• With shares trading at 17.6x FY27 Street EPS, D’Alba Global is among the “Cheapest in the Global Beauty Space” despite boasting the “Second HIGHEST” Growth Rate among listed Global Peers, with 50%+ y/y Revenue Growth.  Presenter notes the company recently IPO’d and has garnered limited Sell-side Coverage outside Korea but expects the stock to attract MORE attention amid an “Imminent” US Sales Inflection.

• The D’Alba Franchise was built on a “Viral” Spray Serum that has sold ~50M units since launch.  The Mist category now represents ~46% of Sales, down from ~70% in 2021, yet still grows over 40% ranking as the company’s most mature line.  Importantly, the “Halo” created by this Serum enabled D’Alba to diversify into other Verticals such as Sunscreens and Balms.  Presenter highlights that the Brand has reached the Top 100 of all Health & Personal Beauty products on Amazon.com [AMZN] in the US with LIMITED Marketing Spend.

• South Korea comprises ~34% of Sales growing “LDD%’s,” while Japan represents ~19% growing ~70%, yet Presenter expects a Mix Shift as the company follows the playbook of larger “K-Beauty” Brands entering Western Markets.  As an example, she points to APR Co. [278470.KS], owner of Medicube, which generated ₩63B (~$42M) in North America Sales in 2023 and is expected to EXCEED ₩1.2T (~$800M) in 2026.  This Growth fueled an ~8x increase in the stock over 18 months, making APR the most valuable Beauty company in Asia.  D’Alba’s North America Sales totaled just ₩65B in 2025, though Presenter sees 2026 as the Year the company achieves US Scale, driven by MORE aggressive Marketing ahead of a “Heavy” SKU-release Calendar in 2H26.  The North America business is currently growing OVER 200% y/y, and Presenter believes it can sustain a similar pace near-term.

• She highlights several Datapoints as evidence D’Alba’s US Sales Push is GAINING traction: 1) AMZN 3P Sales Data showcases “Consistent, Triple-Digit% Growth”; 2) In December 2025, Ulta Beauty [ULTA] launched products in 200 stores with Sales running 87% ABOVE Expectations within the first 2 weeks, prompting a full Network Rollout by April 2026 and DOUBLING the SKU count from 23 to 46; and 3) Costco Wholesale [COST] added the company’s products to 150 stores in December 2025 with plans to expand to 225+ Stores.

• Customs Import Data reveals Shipments to the US ACCELERATING through the remainder of 2026, and Presenter argues that US Adoption of “K-Beauty” products remains “Very Early.”  Notably, this Category comprises just ~1.8% of the US Beauty Market vs. ~10% for French products.  Conversely, K-Beauty’s Share in more established Markets (i.e., ~6% in Japan, ~12% in SE Asia, and ~14% in China) points to an “Ample Growth Runway” in the US.

• Presenter’s FY28 EPS Estimate of ~₩26K is WELL-ABOVE the Street’s  and applying a “Conservative” 16x Multiple, she arrives at a Price Target of ₩415,000/share (~87% Upside).  Current Operating Margins are UNDER 20% vs. ~25% for typical “Indie” Beauty peers, a gap Presenter believes D’Alba can close.  Lastly, she sees potential for rising M&A Activity across the space, creating further “Optionality” for the stock.

Transcript:

5. Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) — Long / Merger Arb

Presenter: I'll pitch something boring — we like WBD long into the potential close of the Ellison/Paramount deal. WBD signed to be acquired for $31 in cash. The stock has de-rated to a ~low-20s% implied spread. If the deal doesn't close by October 1 you also collect ~$0.26/share per quarter — roughly $7m/day — as a ticking fee.

Almost every approval is in (a little UK outstanding). The consequential item is the state-AG lawsuit led by California's Bonta alleging anti-competitive dynamics. A federal judge in Oakland (a Biden appointee) got the case and put a TRO in place. On paper you wouldn't want her, but her actual ruling history is more moderate than her profile.

The sequence matters. When the suit was filed WBD actually traded up, because the allegations were more benign than feared. Then people hoped for a longer gap between the TRO and the preliminary injunction — a full PI hearing is a mini-trial with cross-examination, which could pressure a settlement. Instead the judge set a short ~2-week timeline to the PI hearing, signaling she'd grant the PI and not to expect an early settlement. So last Friday the companies front-ran the inevitable PI and simply said they won't close until they resolve it with the states. The stock dipped slightly, but the PI was already priced into the spread.

Why it's interesting: the merits are weak. In one of three markets they alleged ~27% share; the usual concern threshold is ~30%, and even then there are concessions available. On concentration metrics (share, HHI) it's a weak case — consultants suggest the defense wins ~85%. And crucially both sides want to settle: Ellison wants to close fast (strategic reasons plus the ticking fee) and has offered concessions; Bonta appears driven by political optics — he's up for reelection and has higher ambitions (California AG → governor), so extracting a visible "scalp" and settling is the logical path.

Catalyst: this week both sides file preferred trial schedules (Friday), and give-or-take the following Friday you should get a trial-date announcement, which will largely determine the spread. Earliest realistic trial is ~November; the states are pushing for April. A late-2026 / early-2027 start likely produces a settlement before/around year-end — an attractive ~20%+ spread plus ticking fee. An April start pushes settlement into early Q1 and would read as more biased toward the states (short PI window but long trial timeline).

Q (break case): Probably ~$17, but there are multiple decision nodes before you'd realize that — you'd learn the trial date, decide whether to sit through the trial (very high likelihood of a pre-trial settlement), and even an adverse ruling would be appealed (an accelerated appeal, likely 2H27 for a ruling), so $17 really means "deal dead / very late." Anchor to the fact you're being paid toward $31-plus-ticking. (Amy notes she's in it too but sizes it small — ~2% — scared of the crowded arb base.)

4. Vonovia (VNA GY) — Short — Sachin Gupta (formerly Fir Tree)

Event-driven short into Berlin elections. Vonovia owns rent-controlled German housing (~25% of assets and NOI in Berlin). ~€40B debt, ~€18B market cap, ~€2.5B NOI — i.e. a ~5% cap rate financed just ~50bp over the German 10-year after Bund yields rose ~3.5%. Short is timed to the Berlin parliamentary election on September 21, where Polymarket odds now favor the Left party + Greens over the incumbent CDU.

• Expropriation tail: the 2021 "DWE" referendum to socialize Berlin housing passed ~60%, with owners to be paid ~40 cents on the dollar in 100-year, 3.5% bonds (≈30 cents present value). CDU slow-played it; a Left/Green win revives the risk. Berlin can constitutionally expropriate (a carryover quirk), and Berlin unemployment at ~12% (above COVID levels) sharpens the politics.

• Even absent expropriation, presenter argues a 4% cap on un-invested, low-quality rent-controlled stock is far too tight; re-rating toward a 7.5% cap (3.5% Bund + 300–400bp) roughly halves that portfolio. Because Berlin is ~25% of assets against a levered capital structure, a ~50% hit to those assets could roughly halve the equity.

• Credit angle: heavy 2026–2028 maturity wall at ~1.8% average coupons refinancing at ~4.5–5% drives cash generation toward zero versus a ~10% dividend commitment; reliance on 0% convertibles (dilution, capped at ~15% of market cap) is pushing them toward secured debt, which would subordinate and widen the unsecured bonds (~160bp over). Trade is short equity and short unsecured credit.

• Apollo/DWE wrinkle: a Jan-2026 shareholder-agreement amendment has the parent guarantee the debt and returns of the Apollo-backed "bad box" (DWE) — good parent box now backstops the bad box. Thesis is short-dated (works in ~60 days, cover on the 22nd, day after the election) with wrong-footed, vacationing European investors prone to overreacting to headlines.

Transcript:

4. Vonovia (VNA GY) — Short — Sachin Gupta (formerly Fir Tree)

Presenter (Sachin Gupta, formerly Fir Tree): I'm pitching a short on Vonovia — a German real estate company that owns rent-controlled housing across several German geographies. The ticker is roughly VNA GY. Biggest exposure is Berlin: ~25% of assets and ~25% of NOI.

Balance sheet: ~€40B of debt, ~€18B market cap, ~€2.5B of NOI — so at the market cap it's roughly a 5% cap, but German rates have moved up a lot (Bund 10-year ~3.5%), so you're financed only ~50bp above the sovereign. This is really a short-dated trade around the Berlin parliamentary election on September 21.

On Polymarket, the incumbent CDU (Christian Democrats) is no longer favored; the Left party and the Greens are. That matters because in 2021 there was a Berlin referendum to socialize housing that passed by ~60% — the "DWE" initiative — under which owners would be expropriated and paid only ~40 cents on the dollar in 100-year bonds at ~3.5%, i.e. ~30 cents present value. Owners pushed back and the CDU, once it controlled the parliament after 2023, slow-played the bill. A Left/Green win revives it.

Berlin is unusual: as a carryover from its divided past it doesn't fully follow the federal constitution and retains the ability to expropriate property. Federally the CDU is trying to jam through a bill barring expropriation before they become lame ducks, but that's arguably unconstitutional in Berlin. So people assume it's stable, but it isn't a foregone conclusion.

Even setting expropriation aside, you're short a ~4% cap on un-invested, low-quality rent-controlled stock — look at the listings; walls unpainted, poor condition. A 4-cap is what Class-A New York trophy real estate trades at. If it re-rates to a ~7.5% cap (3.5% Bund + 300–400bp spread), that portfolio roughly halves. Because Berlin is ~25% of ~€X of assets against this levered structure, a ~50% hit to those assets could roughly halve the equity, and the ~€40B of unsecured debt (trading ~160bp over) would widen materially given the long duration — so you can make money short the bonds and short the equity.

Refinancing: when rates were near zero (even negative) they raised a lot of debt to buy assets. Now there's a heavy 2026–2028 maturity wall at a ~1.8% average coupon; refinancing at ~4.5–5% pushes free cash toward zero, which is a problem against a ~10% dividend commitment. To manage it they've done 0% convertibles (dilutive), capped at ~15% of market cap, and are now contemplating secured debt — which primes the unsecured and causes spreads to widen.

Extra wrinkle: in 2023 Apollo put money into the rent-controlled "DWE" box; now Apollo wants protection, and in January 2026 the shareholder agreement was amended so the parent guarantees the debt and returns of that box. So the good parent box now backstops the bad Apollo box — the guys who are good at getting their money back at everyone else's expense.

Why now: it can work in ~60 days — it's not a multi-year carry. The wrong base of investors is on vacation over the next several weeks, and going into an election you tend to get aggressive political headlines. Cover on the 22nd, the day after the election. Q (odds): roughly a 33% chance the Left wins and ~23% the Greens — additively ~56%, with some correlation, so it's tilted in our favor. Q (how do you trade it): for a European stock people over-react, so if you get the chance to cover into a panic on a favorable outcome, take it.

2. Genuine Parts Company (GPC) — Long

Presenter: GPC — ~$130 stock, trades roughly 16x / ~10x on a consolidated basis. They announced a tax-free spin targeted for Q1 2027. International is a decent business in Europe and a better business in Australia (small market).

Now it's a more focused standalone team with a sense of urgency that can't hide behind the other business — Motion.

Motion is the other ~50% of EBITDA and ~75% of enterprise value. It's an industrial distributor: ~80% MRO, ~20% capital projects. Its end markets track PMIs, which have been improving the last several months. Guidance embeds mid-single-digit-ish growth; they just beat in Q2. On a standalone basis with its own capital structure there's real opportunity for capital deployment and M&A — it's a ~6% share player in a fragmented market; the #2 is AIT.

Every turn on Motion is worth a lot. If you talk to the sell-side, some put Motion at only ~13–14x — there's really only one analyst covering both auto and AIT-type names — so the SOTP is under-appreciated.

6. CoreCivic (CXW) & GEO Group (GEO) — Long

Presenter: I manage a small/mid-cap special-situations fund, and we like GEO Group and CoreCivic. The stocks have rallied but are only back to roughly post-election levels, and between the ICE build-out and real-estate monetizations we think there's ~50%+ upside over the next few months.

ICE revenue is approaching ~50% of both companies. GEO screens a touch healthier because of its higher-margin monitoring (ISAP) business and slightly higher ICE exposure — though there's been some controversy and a leadership change at ICE. Occupied beds in the system stagnated and then re-accelerated in June/July; the government portal only started updating recently, so you can now track it roughly weekly.

Background: earlier this year the government floated several ways to expand owned real estate — buying warehouses from developers, even "Alligator Alcatraz," and acquiring facilities from the private operators. They rolled back the impractical warehouse idea, but after Trump signed a ~$75B ICE funding bill (enforcement + real estate), CoreCivic announced its first two real-estate monetizations in early July at a little over ~$300k/bed — the street had expected closer to ~$200k — and the stocks ran.

We think it's just getting started. Initial media reports were ~10 facilities; now it looks like 15+. If they monetize 15 facilities anywhere near those prices, that approaches the entire market caps of both companies. The monetizations are tax-free to the companies (cash to the government), so you get large buybacks with little dilution — aside from small tuck-ins like a recent CoreCivic pharmacy deal.

On current numbers CXW trades ~6x EV/EBITDA and GEO ~8x. Reactivations have been happening for a year and will continue. The system is ~65,000 occupied beds today (across all private operators) versus a government goal of ~100,000; the funding is there. The government prefers to own rather than lease because owned facilities face fewer blue-state legal/permitting challenges — that's why California-style facilities are being bought out, and why the administration is incentivized to do it (harder for a future administration to unwind).

Process differences: CoreCivic wants to sell the real estate first and negotiate the master (operating) contract after; GEO wants to do both simultaneously. There's an appraisal process we don't have full access to, but the first CoreCivic prints were large — high-cost metro markets where replacement cost is ~$200–300k+/bed, with reported figures around $270k depending on facility size and adjacent expansion land.

Q (2028 political risk): Yes, a future administration could wind detention down — but that's far away, the money is committed for the next year-plus, and the timeline here is now-through-midterms. As they delever and buy back stock, we don't think the multiple de-rates; if anything it could re-rate. GEO also has the ISAP monitoring business (exclusive contract, much cheaper than housing someone awaiting a court date) that could re-ramp — not in our numbers, so it's gravy.

Framing: we run bed-price / after-tax-proceeds sensitivity tables. Using ~$225k/bed on ~5–10k beds for CoreCivic and assuming buybacks over ~2 years at higher prices, we get CXW toward ~$46. This isn't an AI stock or a generic Trump-policy stock — it's trackable: occupancy updates on the government portal, and we set a daily email alert on it.
