1. Compass (COMP) — Long — Irenic Capital

Structurally improving residential brokerage. Presenter (Irenic) argues Compass is the emerging predominant player in U.S. residential real estate, a fragmented, structurally-improving industry analogous to how commercial real estate services consolidated (CBRE-style). Low-teens share by value, skewed to the luxury/high-end market. Stock at a low base (base case work starts around $12) with what he frames as a de-risked macro setup — housing activity is depressed but tied to life events (divorce, job moves, family changes), so it "can't get much worse."

• Anywhere Real Estate acquisition (closed early January) is transformative; synergy capture is going well but the market already understands it — not the real driver of upside.

• Under-appreciated lever is agent productivity: typical Compass agent does ~5 units/year vs. ~10 achievable; Compass recruits and coaches around productivity, plus best-practice/referral sharing across the network.

• Attach services (title, escrow) are an under-monetized revenue layer; filling attach rate could roughly double that revenue over a few years. Presenter sees ~30% earnings upside before any housing recovery, with more torque on a normalization through the 2020s and some operating leverage.

• Management: Robert Refkin — controversial in the industry but viewed as a great operator with a vision that has played out. Stock is volatile because it is crowded/shorted, levered, and seen as a macro/AI-disruption debate. Presenter thinks AI is a modest negative at most; scale, network and referral flywheel dominate over the medium term.

• Long side discussion of the NAR / "clear cooperation" MLS changes: despite unbundling fears, fees are not compressing (brokers effectively holding fee levels, e.g. Greenwich contracts locked around 2.75%); U.S. fees remain the highest internationally with little drift toward global levels.

Transcript:

1. Compass (COMP) — Long — Irenic Capital

Presenter: I'm at Irenic Capital. I've spent a lot of time in housing / real estate services, and I like Compass here. The stock is levered — call it ~3.5x currently — but let me talk about the business and why we're in it.

Compass has low-teens market share by value (not by transactions), because they focus on the luxury / high-end market — that's important to the thesis. This is a structurally improving industry, and the analogy is what happened in commercial real estate services: over time you get a predominant player, and Compass is emerging as that predominant residential brokerage. There are a couple of other decent players, but it's a decent-to-good business in an industry that is structurally improving.

On the macro: the housing market has been depressed for a while. What's interesting is that home sales are largely tied to life events — divorce, moving for a job, family changes. So activity is close to a floor. We don't know exactly why or when it turns, but it can't get much worse. From a macro standpoint that's interesting, and Compass is a winner in an eventual recovery.

Their average home value is very high-end, so even with weak activity their addressable market has grown ~5% because of price/mix. They're a niche and they're winning share within it — the situation changes day to day, but broadly they benefit from what's happening.

They closed the acquisition of Anywhere Real Estate early in January — a transformative deal. There's a synergy/production opportunity, and it's pretty well understood; it's not like we have a synergy number that's a multiple of what they've disclosed. Management has done a good job keeping things in order, and we think they'll achieve the synergies, but that's not where the outperformance comes from.

What's more interesting is what they don't talk about: agent productivity. There are roughly 22 productivity buckets; a typical Compass agent does about 5 units a year, and you can get to ~10. Compass was structurally built by recruiting around productivity, so productivity can be structurally higher than peers. There's a lot they can do — deal sharing, best practices across the network. If the average agent goes from ~5 units to ~6–7, that's real.

The other interesting piece is attach services — title, escrow, and so on. The attach rate hasn't moved much. When you look out a few years and fill in some of that revenue, it can be ~100% higher. So before any housing recovery we get roughly 30% earnings upside. Then layer in a housing recovery they don't even model — normalized sales through the 2020s — plus operating leverage on the business, and there's real torque.

Our base case work starts around $12. In a housing-recovery scenario you get meaningfully more, and there's leverage on the operating metrics — Compass has a lot of torque relative to an average operator.

Management: Robert Refkin. He's a controversial guy in the industry, but a great operator; his vision over the last decade has been spot on. I wouldn't call it purely a jockey stock, but we've done a lot of work and like him.

Q: Why is it so volatile — crowded, shorted? Presenter: A few things. One, it's crowded. Two, it's levered. Three, depending on the day, people treat it as a macro / "do I love it or not" name. The main bear argument is AI disruption — part of Compass's appeal is the tech stack, and the worry is you could just buy a Coldwell Banker-type CRM without all the coaching. But I think there's a huge benefit from the platform and network — referral business, insurance, etc. On any given day if you screen the factors, it looks tied to the AI trade; over a medium horizon, how they operate — retaining the highest-productivity agents — dominates. The industry had been losing top agents for years; in the last ~5 years that's changed. If you're a top-5% "Ryan Serhant"-type producer, you can demand your price, and Compass is built to keep you.

Q (fees / unbundling): Are we still in the aftermath of the unbundling dynamic — are fees drifting toward international levels? Presenter: On the MLS / clear-cooperation changes from about a year ago — brokers are generally obligated to put inventory into the MLS, with some exceptions, and there were changes around how listings are advertised and a requirement that buyers sign an agreement specifying the fee. You'd have thought you'd see fee compression — it used to be ~6% almost no matter what — but you're not seeing it. Internationally U.S. fees are the highest and there's little drift lower. Brokers are effectively locking arms — e.g. in Greenwich contracts got set around 2.75%. On top of that we're in a low-volume, tight-supply, K-shaped market: if you're a buyer you're paying up for scarce inventory and still paying a fee. It's a unique moment.

ideas.2026-07-17-myst-miko-tam-myst-industrial:
Trane Technologies PLC [TT]

Upward EPS Revisions to Materialize as ALL 3 Business Lines Inflect Simultaneously

• TT designs, manufactures, sells equipment and service solutions for Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning [HVAC], and Custom and Transport Refrigeration.

• Presenter describes TT as a “Lazy Short” among Hedge Funds that he now views as an “Underappreciated Recovery Story” at a time when ALL 3 of the company’s Business Segments are INFLECTING simultaneously for the first time in recent memory.  Applied HVAC (i.e., Custom / Large-scale Commercial) comprises ~65% of the business, of which Presenter “Conservatively” estimates ~15% is related to Data Centers.  The remaining ~35% includes Residential HVAC, where he sees a Recovery underway, and Transport Refrigeration, which is now “Turning a Corner” after a 2 – 3-year decline.

• Presenter’s Thesis is centered on an anticipated Margin Improvement in the recovering segments (i.e., Residential HVAC and Transport Refrigeration).  His Checks suggest these businesses could achieve 50% – 60% Incremental Margins vs. the ~25% currently embedded in Street Estimates and he believes this dynamic can ultimately fuel “HSD%” EPS Revisions for FY27.

• The stock is currently trading at ~25x Presenter’s Above-Consensus FY27 EPS Estimates, and applying a 30x Multiple, he arrives at a Price Target of $555/share (~18% Upside).  Lastly, he highlights TT's upcoming 2Q26 Earnings Report on July 30th, 2026, as a key near-term Catalyst.

TransAlta Corporation [TA.CN]

FCF to Surge as Data Center Buildouts “DOUBLE” Power Prices

• TA.CN is a Canadian Independent Power Producer [IPP] with a diversified, contracted Power Generation portfolio across Canada, the US, and Australia, operating through 5 segments: 1) Hydro; 2) Wind & Solar; 3) Gas; 4) Energy Transition; and 5) Energy Marketing.

• Presenter's Thesis is built on a “Structural Setup” in Alberta's 11GW Deregulated Power Market, where a prior Overbuild of Renewables pressured Power Prices toward ~C$40 and forced the “Mothballing” of dispatchable Thermal Capacity, raising reliability concerns.  Since 2024, the Provincial Government has “Courted” Data Centers to absorb that stranded Capacity, a strategy Presenter believes simultaneously bolsters Power Prices, sustains a viable Thermal Generation mix, creates Jobs, expands GDP Growth, and monetizes “Cheap,” stranded Natural Gas on which the Government collects a Royalty.

• TA's fleet includes ~900MW of Hydro, ~2.4GW of Solar, and ~200MW of Wind, all fully contracted, alongside ~4.8GW of partially contracted Gas, leaving ~52% of Total Megawatts under contract.  Under the Alberta Electric System Operator’s [AESO] Phase 1 Large Load Integration framework, ~1.2GW of Interim Capacity was allocated between 2 Data Center projects: 1) TA's ~230MW Keephills project, backed by Brookfield Corporation [BN] and CPP Investments [Private]; and 2) A ~970MW project from Pembina Pipeline [PBA] backed by Meta Platforms [META].  Presenter attributes Hyperscaler interest in Alberta to “Abundant” affordable Gas, a temperate Climate, and access to Water and Fiber, highlighting unusually “Clear Alignment” among the Provincial Government, the AESO, and the IPPs – a rural, “PRO-Business” environment he believes creates LESS friction and “NIMBYism” vs. a Market like the US Mid-Atlantic Grid (i.e., PJM Interconnection).

• Presenter expects Alberta Power Prices to RISE toward C$85 – C$100 once the ~1.2GW of New Load is fully drawing Power by ~2029, consistent with commentary from Traders, IPPs, and TA Mgmt., who guided to an C$85 – C$125 Long-term Wholesale range at the company’s March Investor Day.  At C$85, Presenter models ~C$3.00/share of incremental Free Cash Flow in 2029, and at C$100, that figure grows to ~C$4.00/share.

• Presenter sees FURTHER Upside from Phase 2, or “Bring Your Own Generation” [BYOG], by which BN is seeking to scale its Keephills allocation to a “FULL Gigawatt” from its initial ~230MW.  TA is separately pursuing BYOG qualification for ~1.5GW of underutilized Thermal Capacity and maintains an additional ~800MW of “Mothballed” assets and ~2GW of NEW development projects positioned in the Interconnection queue, ALL of which Presenter views as “Embedded Optionality” BEYOND his Base Case.

• He expects a finalized MOU with BN later this year, laying out Long-term Financial Projections that “De-risk” the path toward C$4.00+ of FCF/share.  Applying an 8x – 10x FCF Multiple and discounting back, Presenter arrives a “Mid-to-High-C$20s”/share Price Target (~45% Upside) by year-end.

Shoals Technologies Group, Inc. [SHLS]

Data Center Revenue Ramp “Ignored” due to “Overblown” Competitive Fears

• SHLS provides Electrical Balance of System [eBOS] solutions and components in the US and Internationally.

• Presenter, an Alternative Energy Specialist, describes SHLS as the DOMINANT eBOS Player in US Clean Tech, offering essentially the “Electrical Plumbing” for Solar Farms.  While the Core business is already growing “Mid-20%’s” and ACCELERATING this year on Market Share Gains, the primary driver of the Long Thesis is SHLS’ entry into the Data Center space.

• SHLS is beginning to produce Recombiner Boxes for Battery Storage and Mgmt. guided to a ramp from “Zero” in 1Q26, to $30M – $35M in FY26, then DOUBLING in FY27, forecasts Presenter views as “Conservative” amid his expectation that Battery Storage reaches ~25% of Revenues by FY28.  He notes SHLS is one of the core partners of privately-held ON.Energy, which recently discussed Revenues scaling from ~$40M FY24 to ~$90M in FY25, ~$900M in FY26, and ~$6B in FY27.  The company is also developing a Busway product MORE effective than 800 Volt Architectures, requiring LESS Copper and Labor, with Orders expected to materialize by 1Q27.

• Presenter explains that “Margin Noise” from New Product ramps and Facility consolidation has weighed on recent results, but he feels Gross Margins have “Bottomed” in 1Q26 and should INCREASE in 2H26.  Separately, ~$13M in Legal Expenses (i.e., ~10% of EBITDA) this year stem from a Patent Infringement Lawsuit against a Chinese company.  A court case is scheduled for August, but Presenter thinks this may resolve beforehand with SHLS receiving a Cash Settlement, removing this “EBITDA Drag” in FY27.

• Finally, Presenter views Competitive Concerns from Nextpower [NXT] as “Way Overblown,” since SHLS has a BETTER product and will continue to OUTGROW the Market this year.  Shares trade at just ~9x his FY28 EPS Estimate (~6.5x EBITDA), against his forecast of ~60% Upside to Consensus EPS in FY27 and ~100% in FY28, supporting his Price Target of $21/share (~104% Upside).

Resideo Technologies, Inc. [REZI]

ADI Global Distribution [ADIG] Spin-Off Catalyst to Close Valuation Gap vs. Peers

• REZI develops, manufactures, sells, and distributes Comfort, Energy Management, and Safety & Security solutions in the US, Europe, and Internationally.

• Presenter's Thesis centers on REZI's upcoming Spin-off of ADI Global Distribution [ADIG], expected to begin trading on August 4th, at a 1-for-2 Ratio (i.e., 1 ADIG share per 2 REZI shares held).  The combined businesses currently trade at ~8.5x FY27 EBITDA, a meaningful DISCOUNT to Sensor and Distribution Peers, including: Allegion [ALLE] at ~11.6x, A.O. Smith [AOS] at ~10.0x, Carrier Global [CARR] at ~13.3x, Honeywell [HON] at ~17.8x, Johnson Controls [JCI] at ~18.2x, Masco [MAS] at ~11.9x, and WESCO [WCC] at ~11.0x.  He expects this gap to NARROW through the Separation and subsequent Execution, creating an “Immediate Catalyst” with potential for a 2x – 4x EBITDA Turn “Re-Rating” toward Peer Multiples.

• REZI first announced the Spin in July 2025, and after an initial rally, shares pulled back in November and again in May amid 2 sets of “Execution Issues.”  Following each company’s Investor Day last week (REZI 7/13/26 Presentation / ADIG 7/14/26 Presentation), Presenter believes the “Bar Has Been RESET” heading into the upcoming Spin.  Furthermore, he feels the Setup is NOT dependent on a Housing Recovery, framing this as ADDITIONAL potential Upside rather than a scenario he is underwriting.

• “Re-Rating Drivers” include TAM Expansion, Cost Synergies, and De-levering through FCF Deployment.  In his Base Case, Presenter applies a ~10.5x EBITDA Multiple to each Standalone Entity arriving at $31.00 per REZI RemainCo share and $28.00 per ADIG share, or $14.00 per REZI share after adjusting for the 1-for-2 Distribution Ratio, together supporting his Combined Valuation of $45/share (~26% Upside).  Over time, Presenter anticipates FURTHER Multiple Expansion as Synergies are realized and Execution improves, underpinning his Long-term Price Target of $50+/share (~40% Upside).

Pool Corporation [POOL]

“Misattributed” Market Share Concerns Masking Recovery

• POOL distributes Swimming Pool Supplies, Equipment, related Leisure, Irrigation, and Landscape Maintenance products in the US and Internationally.

• POOL shares have remained under pressure amid several “Technical” Headwinds UNRELATED to the company’s Fundamentals.  Presenter notes that Berkshire Hathaway [BRK/B], formerly the 4th Largest Holder, exited its entire position in 1Q26 due to an “Internal Power Struggle” at the firm rather than a negative view on POOL.  The stock’s issues were further compounded by its removal from the S&P 500 Index, a “Reshuffling” of the Mgmt. Team, and deteriorating Sentiment around the broader Pool Market.  Presenter argues that current Street Estimates assume NO Recovery beyond Replacement-level Demand, ignoring potential Upside from New Construction.

• Investors appear to be “Conflating” 2 separate issues: 1) General “Softness” in the Pool Market; and 2) An emerging Narrative that Heritage – the Pool-Distribution business inside Home Depot's [HD] SRS Distribution unit – is taking significant Market Share from POOL.  Critically, Presenter does NOT see evidence of Share Loss in Industry Data or his own Checks.  He views Pentair's [PNR] negative Pre-announcement as the main source of “Panic” among Pool-related names and contends the Downside Risk to POOL's Earnings is “Significantly LESS” than PNR’s Disclosure implies.

• As the anticipated Pool Market Recovery plays out, Presenter sees potential for FY27 EPS to reach ~$12.50 (vs. $11.81 Consensus).  Applying a ~24x Multiple (still below POOL’s 15-year Average Multiple of ~30x), he arrives at a Price Target of $300/share (~49% Upside) against “Minimal” Downside from current levels.

• UPDATE: POOL reported 2Q26 Earnings on July 23rd, 2026.  Despite “In-Line” Revenues, an EPS / EBITDA “Beat” and Mgmt. reiterating the Full-Year EPS Guidance Range of $10.87 – $11.17 (vs. $10.98 Consensus), the stock closed down ~6.6% on Gross Margin concerns related to higher Freight Costs and Customer Mix.

Navios Maritime Partners LP [NMM]

“Asymmetric” Risk-Reward amid Dry Bulk Inflection / Robust Backlog + Insider Buying

• NMM owns and operates Dry Cargo and Tanker Vessels in Asia, Europe, North America, and Australia.

• Presenter explains that NMM represents one of the LARGEST Holdings in his Transportation-focused Fund for several reasons: 1) The stock is “Very Inexpensive” trading at just ~40% of NAV of ~$185/share and ~4.0x FY27 EPS, with a ~20%+ Free Cash Flow Yield; 2) The story is “Catalyst Rich”; and 3) Significant Insider Buying and anticipated company Share Repurchases.

• Presenter highlights that NMM’s Multi-year Investment period has produced a “High Quality” ~9-year-old Shipping Fleet of 170 Ships, DIVERSIFIED roughly ~1/3rd each across Container, Tanker, and Dry Bulk Shipping.  Notably, NMM’s current Backlog stands at ~$4B (~DOUBLE the company’s Market Cap!) with ~70% of the existing Fleet Contracted (“2026 and the Majority of 2027 are Locked In”).

• Importantly, the less attractive Container Ships are contracted out to ~2030 at “Very Profitable” Rates, leaving NMM's Spot Exposure concentrated in Dry Bulk, where the Market is “Heating Up” with the BEST Supply / Demand Imbalance in Shipping (close to NEGATIVE Net Fleet Growth after Scrappage).  Furthermore, a “Massive” Iron Ore Project in West Africa known as Simandou came online in the last ~6 months, requiring Capesize Vessels and favorably altering the major Dry Bulk Trade Lanes.  As a result, Presenter expects Australia-China Volumes to be replaced by West Africa-China, a 2x – 3x LONGER Ton Miles Journey that will reduce effective Capacity.

• Now that the “Heavy” CapEx Cycle is complete, he sees NMM reaching its 25% Net Debt Target in ~2 – 4 quarters, freeing up capacity to repurchase a SUBSTANTIAL amount of stock at “40 Cents on the Dollar” which should fuel a major “Re-Rating.”  The Street models EPS nearly DOUBLING this year to $18.14 (from $9.94 in FY25), and Presenter forecasts FY28 EPS of ~$23.00 (vs. $20.95 Consensus).  The Fleet earned ~$26K on Average in 1Q26 (vs. ~$13K “Cash Break-Evens”) and with most Capacity “Locked Up” on guaranteed Multi-year Charters, Presenter envisions “NO Scenario” in which NMM loses money over the next several years, always a real risk in Shipping.

• Even though the Shipping sector carries a “Bad Reputation” and can be “Volatile,” he points to an Asymmetric Situation – applying a 5x Multiple to his FY29 EPS Estimates (or ~60% of NAV), Presenter arrives at a Price Target of $115/share (~61% Upside), while he struggles to see the stock trading below $60/share under any “Reasonable” assumptions.

• Lastly, Chairwoman/CEO Angeliki Frangu is the largest Shareholder with ~21% of the Shares Outstanding, and she has been buying ~$100K worth of stock EVERY day for the last ~3 months up to $80/share, viewing the stock as “Greatly Undervalued.”  She also owns IDRs [Incentive Distribution Rights] that pay out ~$500M if NMM distributes $20/share in Cash.  While Presenter is NOT underwriting this scenario, he believes it is possible and capable of driving the stock toward $200/share.

Modine Manufacturing Company [MOD]

Climate Solutions RemainCo “UN-Modeled” Despite “Capacity-Constrained” Market

• MOD develops, manufactures, and markets mission-critical Thermal Solutions to diversified Global Markets and Customers in a wide array of Commercial, Industrial, and Building Heating, Ventilating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration [HVAC&R] applications.

• Presenter views MOD as an Attractively-valued, High-Quality Industrial business that remains “Misunderstood” by the Market.  He believes the recent ~30% Pullback from Highs owes MORE to “Index-based Forced Selling Mechanics” than to Fundamentals, and expects MOD to “Re-Rate” HIGHER as the Market appreciates the company’s Strategic Split into 2 focused, “Streamlined” Entities: 1) SpinCo – Thermal Management Solutions business formed by combining MOD’s Performance Technology business with Gentherm [THRM] through a Reverse Morris Trust [RMT]; 2) RemainCo – Climate Solutions company focused on the HIGH-growth Data Center and Commercial HVAC & Refrigeration End Markets.

• The Thermal Management business, while less desirable than Climate Solutions, will be the “Scaled Leader” and expand its capabilities in Precision Flow Management.  Mgmt. expects to realize significant value through Cost Synergies and Incremental Commercial opportunities in various attractive End Markets including Power Generation, Commercial, Medical, and Heavy-duty & Light Vehicle.  On a Pro Forma basis, the combined business generated Revenues of ~$2.6B with Adjusted EBITDA Margins of ~13% and Net Leverage of ~1.0x.

• Presenter is surprised that the Sell-side has NOT yet published any Standalone RemainCo Models.  He refers to RemainCo as a “Climate Solutions Pure Play” with Data Center representing ~75% of Total Revenues, a supply-constrained End Market.  He expects this business to grow 40% – 60% over the next several years supported by a ~4B Long-term Agreement with a Hyperscaler running from 2027 through 2029.  Importantly, MOD’s Fixed Cost Base is already developed and Volume is contracted (i.e., 20 Chiller Lines with 10 already Operational).  Presenter estimates ~25% Incremental Margins in the near term as the business scales, but views 30% – 35% as a more realistic “Steady-state” Range.  He also notes CEO Neil Brinker, a former Danaher [DHR] Executive, is implementing the Danaher Business System [DBS] “80/20 Playbook,” improving MOD’s Business Mix and Margin Profile.

• Stripping out the THRM consideration and SpinCo Cash, Climate Solutions RemainCo trades at just ~14.3x Presenter’s FY28 Pro Forma EBITDA and ~12.0x FY29.  For context, he highlights Carrier Global [CARR] trades at ~12.5x FY28 EBITDA despite just ~5% Top-line Growth and ~7% Data Center Exposure, while Vertiv Holdings [VRT] trades at ~20.3x FY28.  In terms of Strategic Transaction Comps, Eaton Corp. [ETN], which trades at ~17.9x FY28, recently paid $9.5B (~22.5x) for privately-held Boyd Corp. in March, while Ecolab [ECL] just closed its Acquisition of CoolIT Systems [Private] for $4.75B, representing over 20x EBITDA.

• Applying ~16x to his FY29 (March Fiscal) EBITDA Estimate of $1.0B, Presenter arrives at a Base Case Price Target of $318/share (~39% Upside), yet he can envision MOD’s Multiple expanding toward ~18x, still a DISCOUNT to both Strategic Comps and Public Peers.  His Bear Case of $185/share (~20% Downside) reflects a 12x Multiple on a “More Conservative” EBITDA Forecast of $830M.  However, this would imply a “De-Rating” BELOW CARR despite 8x FASTER Growth and 10x MORE Data Center Exposure.

• Lastly, Presenter identifies several Catalysts: 1) F1Q27 EPS Results on July 29th, during which Mgmt. should provide some Segment P&L; 2) SpinCo Transaction Close in Late October / Early November (around F2Q27 EPS Results); and 3) Potential GICS Sector Reclassification from Building Products to Electrical Equipment, which should “Bode Nicely” for Fund Flows.

Karman Holdings Inc. [KRMN]

Defense-Tech “Compounder” with Significant Revenue Visibility + Secular Tailwinds

• KRMN specializes in the design, testing, manufacturing, and sale of Mission-critical Systems for existing and emerging Missile, Defense, and Space programs, offering Payload Protection and Deployment, Aerodynamic Interstage, and Propulsion systems.

• Presenter explains that KRMN shares, along with Defense-Tech more broadly, have pulled back considerably (i.e., DOWN ~60%) from January Highs, driven largely by “Opacity” around Mgmt.'s Organic Growth Disclosures since the company’s IPO.  However, Presenter's own Analysis triangulates to 1Q Organic Growth of ~15%, pushing back against Bears arguing Growth has turned NEGATIVE, and highlights that Mgmt. reaffirmed the HIGH-end of 20% – 25% FY26 Organic Growth Guidance with ~90% Revenue Visibility on the 1Q26 Earnings Call.

• Furthermore, he expects Mgmt. will once again reiterate the High-end of Guidance on the upcoming 2Q26 Earnings Call in early August and sees potential for Revenue Visibility to approach 95% – 100%, ultimately restoring “Credibility” to the stock.  He contends this Growth is underpinned by “Very Sustainable, Secular” Demand for a business capable of 25%+ Organic Top-line Growth with ~30% Margins, as Government efforts to “TRIPLE or QUADRUPLE” various Missile Programs phase in through 2027 – 2028, a dynamic he believes warrants a PREMIUM Multiple relative to traditional Industrials.

• Shares currently trade at ~25x FY27 Consensus EBITDA, WELL BELOW Peak Valuations.  Presenter sees potential for a “Re-rating” back toward $70 – $80/share (~62% Upside at the Mid-point), representing a 35x – 40x Multiple on his FY27 EBITDA Forecast and “Under 30x” his FY28 Estimate.  Lastly, he recommends pairing KRMN Long against AeroVironment [AVAV] Short to hedge broader Defense-Tech Risk.

First Solar, Inc. [FSLR]

“Imminent” Tariff Catalyst to Create “Permanent Structural Advantage”

• FSLR provides Photovoltaic [PV] Solar Energy solutions worldwide, offering PV Solar Modules with a Thin Film Semiconductor technology that provides a LOWER-carbon alternative to conventional Crystalline Silicon PV Solar Modules.

• Presenter’s Thesis hinges on a “Looming” Decision related to Section 232 Tariffs, the outcome of which he believes will be “Extremely POSITIVE” for FSLR.  Section 232 targets Silicon-based Polysilicon inputs, however, since the company uses Cadmium Telluride [CdTe] instead, FSLR would NOT be subject to the Tariff.  Presenter frames this as a meaningful Competitive Advantage resulting in HIGHER costs for FSLR's Silicon-based Rivals.

• While the decision has been delayed repeatedly, Presenter expects an Announcement in the “First Half” of August 2026.  Notably, while this Catalyst is “Partially Reflected” in Street Estimates, he contends it is “Barely Reflected” in the current Share Price and should result in: 1) A direct Earnings “Boost” and; 2) Multiple Re-Rating given the “Durable and Permanent Structural Change.”

• Presenter’s ~$30.00 EPS Estimate for FY28 is roughly in line with Consensus, though his Price Target of $400/share (~89% Upside) implies significant Multiple Expansion assuming the Tariff outcome aligns with his Thesis.

• RISK: “50% Probability” of further Section 232 decision delays

ESAB Corporation [ESAB]

Poised for Re-Rating amid “Transformational” Nuclear Acquisition

• ESAB manufactures Automated Welding and Cutting Equipment, Consumables, and Gas Control Equipment for Industrial customers globally.

• Presenter describes ESAB as a “NON-Crowded, Out-of-Favor & Inexpensive Stock,” emphasizing that NO Hedge Funds are represented among the Top 17 Shareholders.  Shares sold off at the onset of the Iran War despite just ~7% exposure to the Middle East, a dislocation he believes has created a “Unique Opportunity” for a company with ~55% Recurring Revenues and a strong Track Record of consistent Free Cash Flow generation.

• His Thesis centers on ESAB’s recently completed acquisition of Eddyfi Technologies, which is expected to be Earnings Accretive, enhances the Revenue Mix, and should support a HIGHER Multiple given ~30% of EddyFi Revenue is Nuclear-related – an End Market that typically commands a premium.  Since the Deal just closed in June, benefits are NOT yet contemplated in Sell-side Forecasts, with Mgmt.’s Pro Forma Guidance expected to be provided alongside 2Q26 Earnings Results (July 6th BMO).

• Presenter's FY28 EBITDA Estimate of $800M sits ABOVE the Street's $756M, built on “Minimal” Synergy assumptions and a “Modest” recovery in the Middle East.  He adds that Mgmt. pointed to Pricing IMPROVEMENTS on the 1Q26 Earnings Call and signaled they are likely to RAISE Full-year Guidance.  Lastly, he highlights a recent Sell-side Survey indicating near-term Industry Trends are “Inflecting Positively.”

• At ~8.3x FY28 Consensus EBITDA, WELL BELOW peers Illinois Tool Works [ITW] at ~16x and Lincoln Electric [LECO] at ~14x, Presenter feels ESAB shares are NOT pricing in any potential Fundamental Improvement in the Core business or any Synergies from Eddyfi.  Applying a ~14x Multiple to his FY28 EBITDA Estimate, Presenter arrives at a Price Target of $138/share (~53% Upside).  Finally, he notes that 4th-largest Shareholder Mitchell Rales, Co-founder of Danaher Corporation [DHR], remains a “Strong Supporter” of the stock.

• RISK: Potential Global Industrial or Mining Recession pressuring Organic Growth BELOW Presenter’s estimates, which he views as “Unlikely.”

Compass, Inc. [COMP]

RE Brokerage “Pseudo-Monopoly” with “Free Call Option” on Commission Split Reversal

• COMP provides an End-to-End Technology platform for Residential Real Estate in the US.

• Presenter emphasizes that COMP boasts OVER 80% Market Share in Luxury Markets such as San Francisco, Washington DC, Manhattan, Miami, and the Hamptons following the company’s January 2026 close of the Anywhere Real Estate [HOUS] acquisition.  The timing of the Deal aligns favorably with the recent INFLECTION in Existing Home Sales and robust Pricing Gains for “Ultra High-End” Markets, which Presenter believes will drive “Double-Digit” Gross Transaction Volume [GTV] Growth for 2Q26.

• Beyond the current quarter, he anticipates “Strong” Earnings Power for the combined entity going forward even if the Housing Market remains “Unchanged.”  COMP and HOUS EACH produced ~$300M of Annual EBITDA prior to the Deal, and Mgmt. has identified $400M+ in near-term Cost Cuts with the combined Free Cash Flow generation expected to fuel “Rapid Deleveraging” of the Balance Sheet.

• Presenter highlights a potential change in Commission Splits as an “Underappreciated” source of Incremental Upside.  He explains that Splits have shifted consistently in the Broker’s favor over the past 13 years, with their share now over 80%.  However, he believes this trend will stop and may even REVERSE once Fees are netted – a dynamic he frames as ADDITIVE to COMP's Economics, with every 1-point change in Commission-Splits worth +13% – 14% to EBITDA.

• Presenter’s Base Case assumes a 10% – 15% EBITDA “Beat” in FY27 and applying a 13x Multiple to his Estimates, he arrives at a Price Target of $18/share (~50% Upside) with potential for further Upside IF the Housing Market continues to improve.

Cardinal Infrastructure Group Inc. [CDNL]

High-growth Civil Infrastructure Roll-Up with Substantial “Tuck-In Arbitrage” Potential

• CDNL is a Civil Contracting company providing Site Development and Infrastructure Services to the Residential, Commercial, Industrial, Municipal, and State Infrastructure Markets in the Southeastern US.

• Presenter feels CDNL remains “Off the Radar” having come Public in December 2025.  The stock was initially grouped into the “Resi Stock Bucket,” yet the shares have outperformed following a 1Q26 “Beat & Raise” and the completion of several Accretive Deals.  He refers to CDNL’s primary business as a “Wet Utility,” offering Underground Prep Work for New Developments.  Historically, the majority of Sales (~70%) have been driven by Resi, but Non-Resi has recently begun to grow FASTER.  Importantly, he highlights CDNL’s FIRST Data Center win in 1Q, opening a NEW Growth Vertical in an area where specialized Labor needs have created a “Bottleneck” for these time-sensitive projects.

• Presenter further describes CDNL as an early stage, MULTI-YEAR “Growth Roll up” with SIGNIFICANT “White Space” since the company currently operates in just 4 US Cities: Raleigh (~70% of 2025 Sales), Charlotte, Greensboro, and Atlanta (entered in 1Q).  He points to “Massive” Public vs. Private Valuation Arbitrage, with CDNL trading at ~27x FY26 EBITDA while ACCRETIVELY executing Platform Deals at ~6x and sees a “Tremendous” opportunity to acquire “Mom & Pop” Labor-intensive Construction businesses across the Southeast at even LOWER Multiples (i.e., ~4x) given owners’ limited Exit Strategies.  The Geographic Pipeline continues to EXPAND, and CDNL is funded through 2027 after completing a ~$335M Equity Raise in June.  The company’s Scale provides substantial Operating Leverage and Mgmt. has astutely vertically integrated Other Services (i.e., Paving).

• Since 2018, CDNL has grown Organic Revenues at a ~35% CAGR, accelerating to ~60% in 1Q26, and Presenter believes the Street is UNDERMODELING the business by forecasting a deceleration to ~12% from 2H26 through 2027.  He thinks the company can sustain 20%+ Organic Growth BEFORE Accretive M&A, while holding EBITDA Margins at ~20%.  He models 25%+ Upside to FY27 Consensus EBITDA of $170M and layering in his ~$600M Deal Capacity Estimate, sees potential for another ~$100M of Incremental EBITDA.

• Presenter views CDNL as a “30%+ Compounder” that will continue to “Roll Up” businesses in the Southeast.  He compares the stock to Construction Partners [ROAD] in 2022 which rose from ~$20/share to ~$100/share, but with just ~5% Organic Growth and ~HALF the Margins, while another comp with some “AI Juice,” Sterling Infrastructure [STRL], “Rocketed” from ~$50/share in 2023 to ~$1000/share earlier this year.  Lastly, he notes the CEO is the #1 Shareholder and has NOT sold a share, nor does he plan to.

Cameco Corporation [CCJ]

Uranium Supply Deficit “Overlooked” Despite RISING Reactor Order Pipeline

• CCJ is a Uranium Mining company that also owns Westinghouse Electric Company, a Nuclear Reactor and Services provider, and offers Uranium Enrichment services.

• Presenter explains that CCJ jumped from ~$80/share to ~$110/share following last October's announcement of a US Government Investment in Westinghouse with plans to build up to ~10 Nuclear Reactors.  Earlier this year, the stock ran to ~$130/share before “Fading” alongside broader Market weakness once NO formal Deals were announced.

• While difficult to handicap “Exact Timing,” Presenter sees a HIGH probability of a Catalyst materializing before the end of 2026, pointing to a “Wave” of recent momentum: 1) The DOE approved a $17.5B Loan Program with 7 Letters-of-Intent [LOIs] signed with Utilities to build Power Plants; 2) An Executive Order targets 2 Reactors built per year through 2030; and 3) Westinghouse recently received “Fast-tracked” NRC [Nuclear Regulatory Commission] approval for AP1000 Reactor design updates.  He also notes the eventual catalyst could be tied to ongoing Japan and South Korea Trade Negotiations with the US, yet the Middle East conflict likely slowed progress on these talks.  [On July 21st, Trump approved a Nuclear Agreement that may allow Saudi Arabia to enrich Uranium estimated to be worth “Tens of Billions of Dollars” and span 30 years.]

• Ultimately, Presenter believes formal Deal Announcements will prompt the broader Market to “Wake Up” to the opportunity.  Longer term, he sees “Clear Value” in the Westinghouse and AP1000 franchise BEYOND a purely Domestic story, citing an International Reactor Growth Opportunity alongside “One of the MORE Compelling Uranium Supply / Demand Imbalance Narratives” over the next ~20 years given the pace of the Global Buildout.

• While Presenter does not offer a specific Price Target, he believes the stock could retrace recent Highs of ~$130/share (~52% Upside), with the path toward 2 Reactors built per year likely to hold at least through the remainder of the Trump Administration.

Techtronic Industries Company Limited [669.HK]

Power Tools Leader with “Hidden” Data Center Exposure + Considerable Margin Upside

• Techtronic engages in the manufacturing and sale of Electrical and Electronic products, operating through 2 segments: 1) Power Equipment; and 2) Floorcare & Cleaning.

• Presenter describes Techtronic as a “High Quality Industrial Compounder” with a strong Competitive Position in the company’s core Power Tools segment, which comprises ~95% of Revenues.  The business has generated ~15% Top-line CAGR over the past decade, driven primarily by: 1) An ongoing shift from Gas / Corded Tools to Cordless, reinforced by US Regulatory Tailwinds around Outdoor Noise restrictions; and 2) Techtronic’s Milwaukee and Ryobi brands’ Battery-Platform “Lock-In,” whereby Contractors who buy Tools in 1 Category reuse the SAME Batteries across the Full Product range, widening the company’s “Moat” over time.

• Another key pillar of the Thesis is Techtronic’s exposure to Data Center Construction, which represents a “Low-Teens%” of Total Revenue with the HIGHEST Margins across the business, as disclosed by Mgmt. on the last Earnings Call.  Presenter believes Growth is being fueled by Mechanical, Electrical and Engineering Contractors (e.g., Quanta Services [PWR], MasTec [MTZ], Comfort Systems USA [FIX]), with whom Milwaukee maintains “Dominant” Market Share.  Notably, Stanley Black & Decker [SWK] has separately quantified its exposure to this End Market at OVER 20% of Revenues when including Utility-related Demand, a signal of further Growth potential.

• Techtronic also has a meaningful Margin “Catch-Up” opportunity, as the company’s Operating Margins are LOWER relative to Peers Makita Corporation [6586.JP] and SWK, despite ~5% HIGHER Gross Margins.  Presenter attributes this to “Elevated” SG&A Spending rather than a Structural Cost Disadvantage and believes Techtronic can expand current ~9% EBIT Margins toward Peers at ~15% over time.  Additionally, he highlights that the company’s NET CASH Balance Sheet has enabled the launch of its “First Ever” Share Repurchase Program.

• Presenter expects Techtronic to “Sustainably” compound Earnings plus Dividends at a 20%+ Total Shareholder Return.  He models FY28 EPS of $1.15 vs. the Street’s $1.01 (NOTE: the company reports Earnings in US$) and applies a 20x Multiple to arrive at a Price Target of HK$200/share (~56% Upside) inclusive of Dividends.
